author: Sonali Kolhatkar
title: New Mexico’s Challenges Hold Lessons for the Struggle for Universal Child Care
content:
New Mexico is finding out that successfully providing universal child care requires giving teachers a living wage.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

The state of New Mexico in 2025 made headlines for being the first in the nation to enact free universal child care. A 12-year-long grassroots push by advocacy groups and activists to address the dismal state of child well-being resulted in Gov. Michele Lujan Grisham signing a bill to expand eligibility for no-cost, government-provided child care to all the state’s residents, regardless of income.

It was a historic bill, one that paved the way for New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani to enact a similar program.

According to the Santa Fe New Mexican, enrollment in New Mexico’s government-provided child care centers jumped over the past year, with 15,000 new enrollees recorded since the program was launched. But waitlists are also growing as demand rapidly outpaces supply. And dire stories are emerging, such as Vox Media’s June 2026 story headlined “How to Screw Up Universal Childcare.”

Expanding free child care to meet growing need isn’t as simple as opening new facilities and enrolling families. Early childhood education requires well-trained staff who are paid generously enough to remain on the job. And that appears to be the biggest obstacle to fully realizing New Mexico’s pioneering program and ensuring that all those who need child care get it.

A June 2026 report by the child advocacy group New Mexico Voices for Children (NM Voices), examined every aspect of child well-being in the state including “early childhood education” — which is the term preferred by advocates to describe child care. The report concluded that, in spite of great strides, New Mexico was falling short in serving the families who need most help, and urged policy makers to “build on recent progress by strengthening the early childhood workforce, expanding access to high-quality programs and ensuring students receive the academic and social supports they need to succeed.”

Enrollment in New Mexico’s government-provided child care centers jumped over the past year, with 15,000 new enrollees recorded.

Matthew Henderson, executive director of OLÉ Education Fund, which helps organize child care workers, underscored how “the universal child care system is definitely something to celebrate, and we do celebrate it because it has given thousands of parents free child care, saving them tens of thousands of dollars.” And Gov. Lujan Grisham, who leaves office at the end of the year, has pinned her legacy to New Mexico’s early childhood education program and hopes it offers a model for the rest of the nation. She told the Associated Press, “My hope is, as we watch elections take hold around the country, that our congressional candidates are talking about these investments, our gubernatorial candidates are talking about these investments” in child care.

And yet, according to Henderson, “there are still parents who can’t access [the program] because the administration has not been smart about how to grow the state’s capacity.”

Child care workers, who are disproportionately low-income women of color, and who are charged with caring for the most vulnerable members of society, are also egregiously underpaid. Although New Mexico’s early educators are now compensated as much as $16-$19 an hour — which is higher than the state’s $12-an-hour minimum wage — it’s not nearly enough to prevent constant turnover and worker shortages.

The New Mexico Early Childhood Education and Care Department (ECECD), which is the government agency overseeing the state’s child care centers, announced a “wage and career lattice” for employees “to support long-term recruitment and retention.” Henderson lauded the approach as “really excellent,” but accused the administration of “slow-walking any attempts to implement professional compensation for the workforce.”

Teresa Madrid, executive director of a New Mexico-based advocacy organization called Partnership for Community Action agreed, telling the Santa Fe New Mexican that the “wage and career lattice is something that has been part of ECECD’s strategic plan for the last several years, and we are now in 2026 with no implementation, no action and no dollars committed to that wage and career lattice.”

content:
14 Ekim’de ben de sahadaydım. Eminönü, Balat, Alibeyköy ve Maslak hattında teslim etmem gereken siparişler vardı. Hava bir bastırıyor, bir normale dönüyordu; ara ara sağanak geliyor, sonra kesiliyordu. Sağanağın en sert anına Sirkeci’de yakalandım. Ana arterler kullanılamaz haldeydi, her yer göle dönmüştü. Motosikletle yol almaktan çok suda yüzüyor gibiydik.


Haberleri takip etmek için bile sığındığımız benzinlikler motosikletçilerle doluydu. Duraklara sığınan insanlar bankların üstüne çıkmıştı. Bot da olsa yağmurluk da olsa, üzerimizdeki ekipmanın hiçbiri o yağmura dayanmadı. Bazı bölgeler tamamen kilitlenmişti. Motosikletin her zaman bulduğu dar aralar bile kapanmıştı ve suyun içinde kaldığımız çok an oldu. Böylesini ilk kez gördüm.


14 Ekim bize bir kez daha şunu gösterdi. Kötü havada kurye ya çalışıp canını riske atıyor ya da çalışamayıp gelirini kaybediyor. Her iki durumda da faturayı kurye ödüyor.


Kuryelerin karlı havada çalışma koşulları: Tehlikeler, baskılar ve haklar


24 Şubat 2025


Sağanağı sele çeviren kent


Vali Davut Gül’ün açıklamasına göre İstanbul’da metrekareye 261 kilogram yağış düştü. Bu, Meteoroloji’nin ölçüme başladığı 1942'den bu yana kentte görülen en yüksek değer. Önceki rekor 200 kilograma yakındı. Valilik bugün 3 kişinin hayatını kaybettiğini, 2 bin 722 kişinin kurtarıldığını açıkladı.


Aşırı sıcaklar, ani sağanaklar ve fırtınalar artık istisna değil. İklim krizi bu olayları sıklaştırıyor. Ama aşırı yağışın sele, selin de afete dönüşmesi kaçınılmaz bir doğa olayı değil. Bunu büyük ölçüde kentin nasıl kurulduğu belirliyor. Betonlaşan kentte yağmur suyu toprağa sızamıyor. Dere yataklarına yerleşim alanları kuruluyor. Altyapı, büyüyen kentin gerisinde kalıyor. Ana arterlerde aşırı yağışa karşı alternatif tahliye sistemleri bulunmuyor. Sonuçta yollar dakikalar içinde göle dönüyor.


Bu tablo tek bir kurumun ya da tek bir dönemin eseri değil. İmar kararlarını veren merkezi yönetim de altyapıdan sorumlu yerel yönetimler de bu sonuçta pay sahibi. İklim krizi bir etken ama altyapı yeterli olsa, kent bu kadar betonlaşmasa ve dere yatakları yapılaşmaya açılmasa aynı yağış bu kadar büyük bir yıkıma yol açmazdı.


Kurye için trafik iş yeridir


Bu tablonun en ağır yükünü açık havada çalışanlar taşıyor. Kuryeler, inşaat, temizlik, tarım ve belediye işçileri… Çoğumuz için trafik, bir yerden bir yere gitmek için kullandığımız bir ulaşım alanı. Kurye için ise trafik iş yerinin ta kendisi. Ofiste çalışan biri için kötü hava, işe gidip gelirken katlanılan bir zorluk, kurye içinse ise iş yerinin baştan sona tehlikeli hale gelmesi demek. Görüş mesafesinin düşmesi, kaygan ve su basmış zemin, artan kaza riski, kuryenin iş yerindeki çalışma koşullarıdır.


Bu yüzden kötü havayı bir hava durumu haberi olarak değil bir iş sağlığı ve güvenliği meselesi olarak konuşmamız gerekiyor. Göle dönen bir cadde, kurye için su basmış bir iş yeridir. Yazın aşırı sıcak, kışın buzlanma da aynı meselenin parçası.


Uyarı vardı, tedbir gün içinde geldi


Kuryeler 14 Ekim’de gün boyu sağanak ve fırtına altında sipariş taşıdı.

Kurye Haber

’e gün boyunca çok sayıda kaza ihbarı ulaştı. Beşiktaş’ta bir kuryenin motosikleti suya gömüldü. Bir başka görüntüde bir kurye, sele kapılmamak için devrilen motosikletine tutunuyordu. Kocaeli, Sakarya ve Antalya’daki kuryeler de benzer koşullarda çalıştıklarını gösteren video ve tanıklıklarını doğrudan Kurye Haber’e iletti.


Vali Gül ertesi gün, vatandaşların meteorolojik uyarıları dikkate almasının can kaybını ve zararları azalttığını söyledi. Bu açıklama, uyarıların önceden yapıldığını resmi ağızdan teyit ediyor. Meteorolojik veriler tedbirin çok önceden alınmasını gerektirse de motosiklet yasağı ancak gün içinde, hava çoktan kötüleşmişken, saat 18.30 sularında açıklandı. Yasak ise 21.00'de başladı. Kuryeler yasağın açıklandığı andan uygulanmaya başladığı saate kadar bile şiddetli yağış altında çalışmak zorunda kaldı. Önleyici tedbir, zorluklar yaşandıktan sonra değil, yaşanmadan önce alınmalı.


Ama sorumluluk yalnızca valilikte değil. Platform şirketleri, uyarıları herkes kadar bilmesine rağmen sistemlerini kapatmak için valilik kararını bekledi ve yasak gelene kadar sipariş almaya devam etti. Kuryelerin can güvenliği kuryeleri çalıştıran şirketlerin değil, valiliğin kararına bırakıldı.


Yasak geldiğinde de herkes uymadı. Kurye Haber’e özellikle mahalle aralarındaki işletmelerle ilgili şikâyetler ulaştı. Kısa mesafelerde denetim olmayacağını düşünen bazı yerel işletme sahipleri …

author: Aizel Tugalon
title: 17 Filipino workers in British Columbia fight back against labor trafficking
content:
TORONTO – Seventeen Filipino temporary foreign workers (TFW) in British Columbia (B.C) have come forward to campaign against fraudulent recruitment agency Helping Hands Immigration Services (HHIS) that trafficked them into precarious conditions.

In a press conference held with Migrante BC and Damayan BC, the workers described how they became victims of labor trafficking, including being forced to work long hours, receiving inadequate pay, and experiencing wage theft.

The 17 migrant workers who came from Taiwan, worked over four months in Newfoundland as seasonal workers at a seafood processing plant. After their seasonal employment, they were referred to HHIS recruiters Cherry May Ricafort and Vincent Macalipay to process extension of work permits. According to the workers, the two allegedly took advantage of the situation knowing that they were newcomers and that their work statuses were about to expire.

“We left the Philippines with our hopes and dreams. With the desire for a better future for our families, we took risks working in different countries,” one of the workers said.

In the Canadian immigration system, the Temporary Foreign Worker Program allows Canadian employers to hire foreign workers to fill temporary jobs when qualified Canadians are not available.

There are two main types of work permits in Canada, an employer-specific work permit or commonly known as a closed-work permit, and an open work permit (OWP). A Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) is a document that an employer in Canada may need to obtain before hiring a foreign worker.

HHIS recruiters Ricafort and Macalipay promised to process the workers’ two-year LMIA and work permit for harvester/laborer work in British Columbia. The recruiters received an initial fee of CA$5,000-8,000 (~P221,000 to P354,000) that was sent to Ricafort’s personal bank and some to a registered business account Strive Employment and Labour Contractors Services Ltd. (Business #745000836).

After receiving initial payments, the recruiters instructed the workers to travel to Vancouver to sign an agreement. Under the agreement, the workers had to undergo a probationary period to prove they are capable of performing farm work. However, some of them were brought to work at hotels, some were brought directly to farms in Keremeos.

Five workers were sent to different hotels to work as housekeepers. Some were assigned to Best Western Plus at Marina Drive and the others at Grand Park Hotel in downtown Vancouver.

Ricafort instructed the workers to keep quiet and not talk to anyone about their working conditions. The workers spent two months working at the hotels before learning that they were being paid CA$7.50 (~PHP330) per room cleaned instead of the proper hourly pay which was never explained to them before they started working. The minimum wage in the province is CA$18.25/hr (~P800) and living wage in Vancouver is CA$27.85/hr (~P1,230).

When they learned that there was no LMIA waiting for them, the workers decided to withdraw their application and asked for a refund. But Macalipay told the workers that it was non-refundable, and threatened the workers that if they don’t vacate their temporary housing, he would call the police and the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) because they have no legal status in Canada and they can be deported.

Twelve of the workers were deployed to three farms in Keremeos, Lidhar Farm Lasser Produce and Mom and Pops Farm Market and were instructed not to tell coworkers about their situation and employment status and that they could only talk to Ricafort and Macalipay about their employers.

“Many of us worked for long hours, about 80 to 100 hours per week but we only got paid for 40 hours and were deprived of a day off. Our employers would remit our salaries to Cherry and Vincent. Before we get our monthly pay, our recruiters would deduct CA$500 (~PHP 22,115) from all of us for the ‘processing fee’,” a worker said.

The workers also disclosed that they were told that they would be charged CA$120 (~P5,300) per month for their accommodation but when they received their salaries, each of them had been charged with CA$350 (~PHP 15,480).

At Mom and Pops Farm Market, the workers learned that Macalipay told their employers that they had a two-year work permit. However, when they talked to their employers, they revealed they do not have plans on obtaining LMIAa for them. When the workers discussed their situation among themselves, they …

author: CNT Madrid
title: 14 de octubre: Huelga General Educativa en la Comunidad de Madrid
content:
Este 14 de octubre de 2026, el sector educativo de la Comunidad de Madrid está convocado a una jornada de huelga que abarca a

personal docente, investigadoras, PTGAS, estudiantado y familias.

 Frente a décadas de desmantelamiento programado por parte del Gobierno regional del Partido Popular y la complicidad de las instituciones, se responde con la movilización unitaria.


El ataque a lo público no ocurre de forma aislada.

 La huelga del 14 de octubre coincide y se articula con la huelga indefinida del personal de 0 a 3 años y la del profesorado de primaria y secundaria, creando un frente unificado en todas las etapas educativas.


Además, esta lucha se cruza de lleno

con la crisis del derecho a la vivienda.

 La educación pública no es un derecho efectivo cuando estudiantes y trabajadoras somos expoliadas por el sistema rentista o expulsadas de nuestras casas. Sin vivienda digna no hay educación pública.


Para dignificar las condiciones laborales y garantizar una enseñanza de calidad, se exige:


Salario y condiciones laborales:

recuperación real del poder adquisitivo

 con un incremento salarial lineal e igualitario ajustado al coste de vida en Madrid, junto a un complemento de capitalidad sin condicionantes meritocráticos. Reducción drástica de la carga lectiva y burocrática.


Bajada de ratios por aula

: máximos de 13 alumnos en Infantil, 15 en Primaria y FP, 20 en Secundaria y 23 en Bachillerato. Límites estrictos en aulas con Necesidades Educativas Especiales (NEE).


Refuerzo de plantillas

: plan de choque para la cobertura inmediata de sustituciones y aumento de profesionales de Pedagogía Terapéutica (PT), Audición y Lenguaje (AL) e Integración Social (TIS).


Infraestructuras y modelo educativo:


Creación urgente de

más de 100.000 plazas públicas de FP.


Plan de climatización sostenible

 frente al cambio climático y erradicación total del amianto.


Fin de la construcción por fases y

revisión del modelo bilingüe segregador

 en favor de aulas de enlace.


Tras el éxito movilizador que tumbó la Ley de Universidades (LESUC) en 2025,

la asfixia financiera continúa.

 El Plan Plurianual de Financiación firmado por la Conferencia de Rectores (CRUMA) y el ejecutivo regional mantiene la inversión en un insostenible 0,4% del PIB, ignorando el mínimo legal del 1% fijado por la norma estatal.


En la Universidad Complutense de Madrid (UCM), el equipo rectoral

ha actuado como correa de transmisión de estos recortes

: fusión de grupos, cierre de turnos de tarde, asfixia a los presupuestos de facultad, recortes salariales al personal predoctoral y reestructuración precaria en bibliotecas. Un rechazo institucional que ya quedó demostrado en la consulta impulsada por UCM x la Pública, donde casi 8.000 personas votaron con un 95% de oposición a este plan de ajuste.


Se exige para las universidades públicas:


Financiación mínima del 1% del PIB regional.


Parálisis inmediata de la privatización

 y del desvío de dinero público hacia fondos de inversión y universidades privadas.


Cese de los ataques salariales al personal predoctoral

 y recuperación de las plantillas y servicios (como bibliotecas e infraestructuras verdes).


Respeto a la autonomía universitaria y garantía plena de los derechos de reunión, protesta y manifestación en los campus.


Se llama a toda la comunidad universitaria y a las trabajadoras de la enseñanza a secundar el paro,

salir a las calles y sumarse a las concentraciones y acciones de protesta.

 se publicó primero en

Sindicato CNT de Madrid

.

author: infolibre
title: Συγκεντρώσεις ενόψει της Πανελλαδικής ημέρας δράσης ενάντια στην ακρίβεια, την Πέμπτη 15/10
content:
“Πέμπτη 15 Οκτώβρη 2026 – Ημέρα Πανελλαδικής Δράσης για επαναφορά του 13ου-14ου μισθού/σύνταξης, ουσιαστικές αυξήσεις σε μισθούς/συντάξεις και μέτρα κατά της ακρίβειας”


Καλέσματα:


Αθήνα, 18:00 στη Πλ. Κλαυθμώνος


Θεσσαλονίκη, 18:00 στο Άγαλμα Βενιζέλου


Καλέσματα/Αφίσες:


Σωματεία εργαζομένων – Σύλλογοι συνταξιούχων


Πέμπτη 15 Οκτώβρη 2026 – Ημέρα Πανελλαδικής Δράσης


για επαναφορά του 13ου-14ου μισθού/σύνταξης, ουσιαστικές αυξήσεις


σε μισθούς/συντάξεις και μέτρα κατά της ακρίβειας


Συγκέντρωση Σωματείων Δημοσίου και Συνταξιουχικών Σωματείων


Στην Αθήνα, πλατεία Κλαυθμώνος, 6μμ., με πορεία προς ΥΠΟΙΚ και Βουλή


Στη Θεσσαλονίκη, άγαλμα Βενιζέλου, ώρα 6μμ.


Τα Σωματεία δημόσιου τομέα και συνταξιούχων καλούμε Σωματεία, Συλλογικότητες, αγωνιστές. εργαζομένους και συνταξιούχους να δώσουν δυναμικό «παρών» στις κινητοποιήσεις που διοργανώνουμε σε όλη τη χώρα, την Πέμπτη 15 Οκτώβρη 2026, Ημέρα Πανελλαδικής Δράσης για επαναφορά του 13ου-14ου μισθού/σύνταξης, ουσιαστικές αυξήσεις σε μισθούς/συντάξεις και μέτρα κατά της ακρίβειας. Στην Αθήνα, πλατεία Κλαυθμώνος, ώρα 6μμ., με πορεία προς ΥΠΟΙΚ και Βουλή. Και την ίδια ώρα στη Θεσσαλονίκη, στο άγαλμα Βενιζέλου.


Συνάδελφοι, συναδέλφισσες,


Το πακέτο των μέτρων της κυβέρνησης Μητσοτάκη που ανακοινώθηκε από την 90ή ΔΕΘ, δεν είναι τίποτα περισσότερο από μια νέα προεκλογική εξαγγελία γεμάτη από ωμό εμπαιγμό με «ρεαλιστικά λόγια». Το «κοστολογημένο» πρόγραμμα, ύψους 2,2 δισ. ευρώ για το 2027 και 3,5 δισ. ευρώ μέχρι το 2030, αποκαλύπτει ποια πολιτική κρύβεται πίσω από τις ντυμένες με επικοινωνιακά τεχνάσματα «ρεαλιστικές» τάχα διακηρύξεις και ποιους τελικά εξυπηρετεί. Από τη μια μεριά δισεκατομμύρια για το κεφάλαιο και την πολεμική βιομηχανία, χωρίς περιορισμούς, και από την άλλη ψίχουλα με τη μορφή των επιδομάτων στους εργαζόμενους και στους συνταξιούχους, για να μην διαταραχθεί η «δημοσιονομική πειθαρχία». Με το πακέτο των μέτρων, το οποίο, όπως ισχυρίστηκε, «κινείται στα όρια του δημοσιονομικού χώρου, διότι οι υπερβάσεις δαπανών οδηγούν σε ευρωπαϊκή επιτήρηση», σε καμιά περίπτωση, δεν καλύπτονται οι τεράστιες απώλειες που έχουν υποστεί οι εργαζόμενοι και οι συνταξιούχοι. Το μόνιμο επίδομα των 500 ευρώ στους δημοσίους υπαλλήλους, με έναρξη καταβολής από το Δεκέμβρη του 2027, «το οποίο θα συνυπολογίζεται και στη σύνταξη τους», και η αύξηση της ετήσιας ενίσχυσης από τα 300 στα 400 ευρώ, που θα αποδίδεται κάθε Νοέμβριο σε συνταξιούχους άνω των 65 ετών, θέτοντας, χωρίς τεκμηριωμένη εξήγηση, 300.000 χαμηλοσυνταξιούχους εκτός, δεν αποκαθιστούν τις περικοπές του 13ου-14ου μισθού και της 13ης 14ης σύνταξης, ούτε μπορούν να καλύψουν τις τεράστιες απώλειες των συνταξιούχων, οι οποίοι από το 2010 έχουν χάσει πάνω από 160 δισ ευρώ, ποσό που κάθε μήνα αυξάνεται.


Την ίδια ώρα, η ακρίβεια και η αισχροκέρδεια λεηλατούν καθημερινά το εισόδημά μας, με τις τιμές στα βασικά αγαθά, στα ενοίκια και ιδιαίτερα στην ενέργεια να παραμένουν στα ύψη. Ο χειμώνας που έρχεται προμηνύεται ακόμη πιο δύσκολος, με τον πόλεμο ΗΠΑ-Ιράν να τροφοδοτεί νέες πιέσεις και αυξήσεις στο κόστος της ενέργειας. Κι ενώ οι επιχειρηματικοί όμιλοι συνεχίζουν να θησαυρίζουν, με τα καθαρά κέρδη τους να αγγίζουν το ρεκόρ των 60,5 δισ. , εργαζόμενοι και συνταξιούχοι καλούνται να διαλέξουν τι θα πληρώσουν: το ρεύμα, τη θέρμανση ή το φαγητό. Η κυβέρνηση, αντί να προστατεύσει το λαϊκό εισόδημα και να βάλει φρένο στην ακρίβεια και στην αισχροκέρδεια, αφήνει την αγορά «τους» να λειτουργεί σε βάρος των εργαζομένων και των συνταξιούχων. Περιορίζεται μόνο σε μέτρα-ασπιρίνες και προσωρινά επιδόματα, με τα οποία ουσιαστικά ενισχύει με κρατικό χρήμα τους ενεργειακούς ομίλους.


Συνάδελφοι, συναδέλφισσες


Η κυβερνητική υποκρισία χτυπάει κόκκινο. Από τη μία, ο πρωθυπουργός αντιμετωπίζει τις ζωτικές ανάγκες των εργαζομένων και των συνταξιούχων ως επικίνδυνο «δημοσιονομικό βάρος», επισείοντας τον μπαμπούλα της «ευρωπαϊκής επιτήρησης» και των μνημονιακών καταναγκασμών για να αρνηθεί την επαναφορά του 13ου-14ου μισθού/σύνταξης και πραγματικές αυξήσεις σε μισθούς και συντάξεις. Από την άλλη, η «δημοσιονομική πειθαρχία» πάει περίπατο όταν πρόκειται για την εξυπηρέτηση των νατοϊκών σχεδιασμών και της πολεμικής οικονομίας: δισεκατομμύρια ρέουν ασταμάτητα για εξοπλισμούς-μαμούθ (Rafale, Belh@rra, F-35) και 3 δισ. ευρώ (με το συνολικό κόστος να αγγίζει τα 5,5-6,5 δισ. ευρώ) για τη σκοτεινή συμφωνία της «Ασπίδας του Αχιλλέα» με το κράτος-δολοφόνο του Ισραήλ. Την ίδια στιγμή, ως συνεπής «μπακαλάκος του νεοφιλελευθερισμού» σκορπά δισεκατομμύρια …

author: Maira Escardovelli
title: Fim da escala 6×1 é a maior mudança na jornada do trabalhador brasileiro desde 1988
content:
O Senado Federal aprovou nesta quarta-feira, 14 de outubro, a Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) que determina o fim da escala 6×1, que estabelecia seis dias de trabalho, com somente uma folga por semana. O novo texto constitucional prevê a redução gradual da jornada de trabalho semanal de 44 para 40 horas, sem redução salarial. Desde a promulgação da Constituição Federal de 1988 que a jornada de trabalho no Brasil não sofria uma redução. Foi a Constituição da redemocratização do país que diminuiu para 44 horas a jornada máxima de trabalho semanal que era até então de 48 horas.


A chamada “PEC do fim da 6×1” é uma das principais bandeiras de campanha para a reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

A votação teve 75 votos favoráveis e apenas um contra, o do senador Hamilton Mourão (Republicanos-RS), ex-vice-presidente no governo de Jair Bolsonaro. No fim da votação dos dois turnos, os senadores aliados ao governo chegaram a entoar um dos jingles mais famosos da campanha à reeleição de Lula.


A votação em dois turnos no mesmo dia foi viabilizada a partir do requerimento apresentado à Mesa Diretora pela líder do governo no Senado, Teresa Leitão (PT-CE), que conquistou a assinatura de 56 senadores para aprovação do pedido. Partidos de oposição ao governo, como Progressistas (PP) e Partido Liberal (PL), liberaram suas bancadas para votação da PEC. A bancada do Republicanos votou a favor da proposta.


Líder do PT no Senado, Teresa Leitão foi a articuladora da votação da PEC em dois turnos


“Sim, principalmente pelas trabalhadoras, mães atípicas, que serão as mais beneficiadas”, afirmou a senadora Damares Alves (Republicanos-DF), durante a votação. O apoio às mães atípicas é uma das principais bandeiras defendidas pela ex-primeira dama Michelle Bolsonaro, que ocupará uma cadeira no Senado Federal no próximo ano.


Na abertura da sessão desta quarta-feira, o presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), destacou que cumpriu com sua palavra ao pautar a discussão da PEC. “Nos últimos meses e semanas, afirmei publicamente que a proposta seria pautada depois das eleições.

Assumi esse compromisso para que cada senador e senadora pudesse decidir, passada a disputa eleitoral, com liberdade, consciência e convicção. Hoje, nesta sessão deliberativa, cumpro a minha palavra”, declarou Alcolumbre. “Para quem acorda cedo, pega ônibus lotado, cumpre sua jornada e volta para casa no fim do dia, essa é uma mudança gigantesca”, completou.


Em suas redes sociais, o presidente Lula também comemorou a aprovação. “É oficial: a escala 6×1 acabou! Hoje é dia de comemorar uma conquista histórica de milhões de trabalhadores e trabalhadoras. O fim da 6×1 é mais do que uma mudança na jornada. É mais tempo para viver, descansar, estar com a família, acompanhar os filhos crescerem, cuidar de si e aproveitar a vida. Quem trabalha tanto para construir o Brasil também merece ter tempo para viver”, declarou a postagem do presidente na rede social X (antigo Twitter).


Mesmo ausente no Senado, o candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro também votou, de forma online, a favor da PEC que põe fim à Escala 6×1. Até a última terça-feira, 13 de outubro, o candidato evitou se comprometer com a votação da proposta e defendia como alternativa ao fim da escala 6×1, a inclusão na Constituição do regime de pagamento por hora trabalhada. A mudança ocorreu depois de uma visita ao pai, o ex-presidente, Jair Bolsonaro, que está em prisão domiciliar, condenado pela tentativa de golpe de Estado.


Flávio Bolsonaro não se manifestou nas redes sobre o assunto e preferiu publicar um vídeo, na noite desta quarta-feira, defendendo a redução da maioridade penal.


O caminho até a aprovação da PEC


A votação foi pautada após ter sido aprovada em dois turnos pela Câmara dos Deputados no dia 27 de maio deste ano. Na ocasião, o presidente da Casa, Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), determinou a discussão pelo plenário no mesmo dia em que o parecer do relator, o deputado Leo Prates (Republicanos-BA), foi aprovado na Comissão Especial sobre o tema da Casa Legislativa por 34 votos favoráveis e 4 contrários. Já no plenário, a aprovação do texto veio com 472 votos a favor e 22 contra, no primeiro turno e 461 a 19, no segundo turno.


Apesar de ter sido aprovada pela Câmara em maio, a PEC só voltou a ser discutida no Congresso Nacional cerca de quatro meses depois. A demora inspirou a oposição e o Centrão a

desenvolver a proposta

 de substituir o fim da jornada 6×1 …

title: Αντιφασιστική διαδήλωση, την Πέμπτη 15/10, 18.00 στη πλατεία Βασ. Γεωργίου, Πάτρα
content:
Αντιφασιστική διαδήλωση στην Πάτρα με αφορμή την δολοφονική επίθεση φασιστών σε μέλος του αντιφασιστικού κινήματος στην Ελευσίνα.


Καλέσματα/Αφίσες:


αναρχική ομάδα “δυσήνιος ίππος”


ΟΥΤΕ ΣΠΙΘΑΜΗ ΓΗΣ ΣΤΟΥΣ ΦΑΣΙΣΤΕΣ


ΤΣΑΚΙΣΤΕ ΤΟΥΣ ΦΑΣΙΣΤΕΣ ΣΕ ΚΑΘΕ ΓΕΙΤΟΝΙΑ


Αντιφασιστική διαδήλωση με αφορμή τη δολοφονική επίθεση φασιστών σε βάρος αντιφασίστα στην Ελευσίνα


Πέμπτη 15 Οκτωβρίου 18.00 Πλ. Γεωργίου


αντιφασιστες/αντιφασιστριες


Το μεσημέρι της Πέμπτης 8/10 στην Ελευσίνα δύο φασίστες στήνουν ενέδρα σε αντιφασίστα σύντροφο στη γειτονιά του. Εκείνος αντιστέκεται [ισοπεδώνοντας τον έναν]και έπειτα μαχαιρώνεται πισώπλατα από τον δεύτερο στα πόδια και στον κορμό. Ούτε απόπειρα ληστείας ήταν, ούτε “οπαδικό”, όπως ισχυρίστηκαν αρχικά οι θρασύδειλοι φασίστες στην κατάθεση τους στους μπάτσους και που στοχευμένα αναπαρήγαγαν ορισμένα καθεστωτικά μέσα για αποπολιτικοποίηση του γεγονότος [όπως είχαμε δει να γίνεται και στην περίπτωση της δολοφονίας του αντιφασίστα Παύλου Φύσσα] Αντιθέτως, ήταν μια προμελετημένη και στοχευμένη επίθεση απέναντι σε γνωστό για την πολιτική του ταυτότητα αντιφασίστα.


Ανέκαθεν ο ρόλος του φασισμού μέσα στον καπιταλισμό είναι συγκεκριμένος. Ως η πιο ολοκληρωτική μορφή του αστικού κράτους, ο φασισμός εξυπηρετεί την ανεμπόδιστη ροή του κεφαλαίου. Δεν είναι τυχαίος ο χρόνος στον οποίο οι φασίστες ξεπηδούν και προμοτάρονται από την κυριαρχία. Το καπιταλιστικό σύστημα βρίσκεται σε κρίση και γεννά πολέμους ώστε να ανακάμψει μέσα από την πολεμική βιομηχανία, ενώ η κοινωνική βάση εξαθλιώνεται και φτωχοποιείται αδιάκοπα. Η συνθήκη αυτή επιτάσσει περισσότερο από ποτέ πειθήνιους πολίτες, πρόθυμους να παραγκωνίσουν τα ταξικά τους συμφέροντα, να σφαγιάσουν και να σφαγιαστούν στο όνομα του έθνους. Όμως η εθνική ενότητα δεν είναι παρά η “συμφιλίωση” των καταπιεσμένων με τους καταπιεστές τους. Ο βασικός ρόλος των φασιστών, εξυπηρετώντας προτίστως τον ίδιο σκοπό με το κράτος, είναι να δημιουργούν εσωτερικούς εχθρούς (μετανάστριες, κουήρ άτομα και οποιαδήποτε κοινωνική ομάδα δεν εμπίπτει στα πρότυπα της “κανονικότητας”),να καταστέλλουν τα κοινωνικά κινήματα που προασπίζονται την αξιοπρέπεια και την ελευθερία και να αποπροσανατολίζουν την οργή της κοινωνικής βάσης απο τους πραγματικούς υπαίτιους -δηλαδή το κράτος και το κεφάλαιο- για την καθημερινή ταξική βία που αυτή δέχεται. Όσο κι αν προσπαθούν να παρουσιαστούν ως αντισυστημικοί, στην πραγματικότητα οι φασίστες κάνουν την πιο βρώμικη δουλειά του συστήματος.


Απέναντι στην επιχειρούμενη επέλαση του φασισμού, εμείς προτάσσουμε τον μαχητικό κοινωνικό αντιφασισμό. Ο αγώνας μας είναι δίκαιος και αναγκαίος. Απέναντι στην σαπίλα του φασισμού, του εθνικισμού, του μισογυνισμού, της μισαλλοδοξίας, του φόβου και του σκοταδισμού, στήνουμε αναχώματα μέσα απο την ταξική αλληλεγγύη, προτάσσοντας τη συντροφικότητα και τη δράση απέναντι στην απόλυτη απονέκρωση και βία των καιρών. Η νίκη είναι δική μας, όσο και αν οι φασίστες και συνεργοί τους επιχειρούν να ποδοπατήσουν όποιο σηκώνει κεφάλι. Δεν τρομοκρατούμαστε, μαχόμαστε, ισοπεδώνουμε τον φασισμό στις συνειδήσεις, το δρόμο και κάθε άλλο πεδίο της καθημερινότητας.


Φασίστες κουφάλες θα περάσουμε από πάνω σας


ΚΚΕ(μ-λ) 


Αντιφασιστική συγκέντρωση και διαδήλωση την Πέμπτη 15/10 στις 18:30 στην πλ. Γεωργίου


Το ΚΚΕ(μ-λ) καλεί τον λαό και τη νεολαία της πόλης στη διαδήλωση ενάντια στην επίθεση των δύο φασιστοειδών, σε αντιφασίστα την Πέμπτη 8/10 στην Ελευσίνα. Με το σύστημα να βρίσκεται σε φάση πιο ουσιαστικής εμπλοκής στα σφαγεία των πολέμων, να τσακίζει δικαιώματα και να διαλύει κατακτήσεις, οπλίζει με την πολιτική του τα χέρια των φασιστών, στοχοποιώντας αντιφασίστες, πρόσφυγες και μετανάστες, προκειμένου να τρομοκρατήσει τον λαό και να περάσει την επίθεσή του. Ο φασισμός τσακίζεται με τον λαό στον δρόμο!


ΘΑΝΑΤΟΣ ΣΤΟ ΦΑΣΙΣΜΟ ΚΑΙ ΣΤΟΝ ΙΜΠΕΡΙΑΛΙΣΜΟ!


ΤΟ ΦΑΣΙΣΜΟ ΤΣΑΚΙΖΟΥΝ ΑΓΩΝΕΣ ΛΑΙΚΟΙ!


Η ΤΡΟΜΟΚΡΑΤΙΑ ΔΕΝ ΘΑ ΠΕΡΑΣΕΙ – ΤΟΥ ΛΑΟΥ Η ΠΑΛΗ ΘΑ ΤΗΝ ΣΠΑΣΕΙ.

title: Actualités de la guerre et de la révolution au Myanmar (Birmanie) : entretien avec un camarade du « Front internationaliste antifasciste » (AIF)
content:
Pour comprendre la situation actuelle en Birmanie, il est nécessaire de revenir à la fois sur l'héritage de la dictature militaire, l'histoire des luttes sociales et ethniques locales, comme sur les diverses tentatives avortées de démocratisation.


Après une période de domination par le Japon pendant la seconde guerre mondiale, et devenu indépendant du Royaume-Uni en 1948, le Myanmar, dont le territoire accidenté n'a jamais été réellement contrôlé par les britanniques, voit s'affronter le gouvernement central à des mouvements ethniques armés (Karen, Kachin, Shan, etc.) et à la guérilla du Parti communiste birman (

CPB

). L'armée, héritière des forces coloniales, se présente comme le garant d'unité nationale fantasmée, tant le pays est une mosaïque ethnique et culturelle.


En 1962, le général Ne Win prend le pouvoir par un coup d'État et instaure un régime militaire. L'armée, rebaptisée Tatmadaw, devient l'institution centrale du pays, contrôlant l'économie et l'administration pendant que la répression s'abat sur l'opposition. Le Myanmar restera isolé sur la scène internationale pendant des décennies, sous sanctions économiques, pendant que ses habitants s'enfoncent dans la misère. Ils le resteront, car encore aujourd'hui un quart de la population vit sous le seuil de pauvreté.


En août 1988, une révolte massive éclate, connue sous le nom de «

 

Soulèvement 8888

 

» : des millions d'étudiants, ouvriers et moines bouddhistes descendent dans la rue pour réclamer la démocratisation du régime. La répression est sanglante.


Face au régime, une partie de l'opposition birmane prend les armes ou intensifie sa lutte préexistante. Citons L'Armée karen de libération nationale, le Parti communiste de Birmanie (

CPB

), et Le Front démocratique des étudiants de Birmanie, fondé en 1988 par des militants étudiants, qui devient l'un des principaux groupes de résistance.


En 1990, la junte organise des élections et la Ligue nationale pour la démocratie (

LND

) d'Aung San Suu Kyi les remporte. La junte annule le résultat, maintient son pouvoir, et place Aung San Suu Kyi en résidence surveillée pendant 15 ans. Cet échec renforcera la résistance armée comme seule alternative.


En 2008, le régime militaire lance une réforme politique et adopte une nouvelle Constitution, qui maintient le rôle dominant de l'armée (elle contrôle 25

 

% des sièges au Parlement et conserve les ministères clés comme la Défense et l'Intérieur). Malgré une nouvelle victoire en 2015, la

LND

 n'a donc qu'un pouvoir limité.


Souvent présenté par les blocs centraux occidentaux comme une période de «

 

transition démocratique

 

» (en réalité plus une stratégie de l'armée de libéralisation économique), ses résultats s'avèrent plus que mitigés :


 Les conflits ethniques persistent (guerres contre les Karen, les Kachin, les Rohingyas)

 

;

 L'exploitation capitaliste se renforce : droits des travailleurs bafoués, syndicats désormais autorisés mais réprimés par la

LND

, salaires extrêmement bas malgré la création, rapidement délaissée, d'un salaire minimum, investissements étrangers captés par les élites militaire, qui contrôlent, et disputent aux minorités ethniques depuis des décennies l'extraction du gaz, des pierres précieuses et des ressources naturelles

 

;

 L'armée mène à partir de 2017 une campagne de nettoyage ethnique contre la minorité musulmane des Rohingyas, provoquant l'exode de 700 000 personnes vers le Bangladesh, dans le silence d'Aung San Suu Kyi.


Cependant, après les élections de novembre 2020, qui ont donné une victoire écrasante à la

LND

, certains généraux craignent une réforme de la Constitution, ce qui les pousse à fomenter le putsch du 1

er

 février 2021. Ce coup d'État déclenche la «

 

Révolution du printemps

 

», un soulèvement marqué par des manifestations massives et la forte présence d'une jeunesse ayant grandi à l'ère d'internet.


Dès les premiers jours, la junte écrase toute contestation : 1 500 morts, 12 000 arrestations, torture, viols et exécutions extrajudiciaires seront recensés.


Face à cette violence, une partie de la population se tourne, comme en 1988, vers la résistance armée :


 Création des Forces de défense du peuple (

;

title: Marco Rubio’s Visit to Athens Raises Questions About Western Democracy
content:
Athens, Greece – U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited Athens to talk about democracy and to deepen political ties with the right-wing Greek government. However, his visit also stirred public outcry, with demonstrators showing anxiety about Greece’s growing militarization and the potential to get entangled in foreign conflicts.


Rubio arrived last Tuesday evening for the sixth round of the U.S.-Greece Strategic Dialogue. By the next day, he stood on Pnyx Hill, the Acropolis behind him, and delivered a speech that invoked ancient Greece to defend Trump’s “America First” approach. He called on Europeans to “awaken from their long slumber.” His nationalist speech called for dominance in supply chains and future technologies.

CNN

 and the

Washington Post

 viewed the speech as a campaign ad for his potential candidacy in the 2028 U.S. elections.


Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis described Greek-U.S. relations as being “

at the highest level ever

,” while Rubio referred to Greece as “such a strong partner.” The leaders announced that Greece agreed to spend up to

$4 billion on a U.S. arms deal

 along with a joint counterterrorism program.


Yet, the streets of Greece during Rubio’s visit told a different story.


Rubio’s Arrival and the Protests


During Rubio’s arrival,

hundreds of demonstrators

 took to the streets of Athens in opposition to his visit.


Among them was Omar Almaani, a Palestinian living in Norway, who drove a van to Greece covered with images of Palestinian suffering and statistical figures.


He called the project “Witness on Wheels” to raise public awareness. “All these numbers are not just aesthetics,” he said. “They are human beings. Every one of them has their own life, their own smile, their own history.”


Almaani said he lost friends, acquaintances, and family members in Gaza. Despite such circumstances, he urged that protests in solidarity with Palestine continue.


“Whatever is gonna happen, it will not stop us; it will not scare us,” he said. “We will stay for the truth, we will stay for humanity.”


Giannis Sifakakis of the Stop the War Coalition spoke at the same protest. “We are here today because we are fighting for Palestine and against U.S. imperialism,” he said. “The Greek government is going deeper into the war on the side of Trump and Netanyahu.”


On the evening of Wednesday, October 7, despite the

24-hour public gathering ban in Athens

, a crowd of pro-Palestinian demonstrators gathered in front of the Israeli Embassy. They organized to mark

three years of genocide in Gaza

.


Protesters gather in front of the Israeli Embassy on October 7, 2026, in Athens, Greece. Photo contributed by Elvis Takahashi Mantello.


Greg, a Greek demonstrator, said he was there for two main reasons, “one, to honor the Palestinian resistance and two, to shout against the genocidal settler colonial regime of Israel.”


Konstantina Kartsioti, an organizer for the Anti-Imperialist Movement, linked the protest with Rubio’s visit, stating, “the collaboration of the Greek state with the Zionist entity and U.S. imperialism.”


“We are telling Palestinians they have the right to resist and the right to return,” she said. “We hope to join the resistance from Greece to Gaza, from Gaza to the West Bank, to Jenin, to Nablus … We unite, and we are telling [people] we must fight and win.”


Why Greece Matters to Rubio


The Strategic Dialogue covered energy, defense, trade, technology and investment. Discussions also centered on U.S. companies such as

ExxonMobil and Chevron, the Vertical Corridor and electricity interconnections

 linking Greece with regional allies.


Greece’s ambition is to strengthen its role as a

regional energy hub

, distributing American liquified natural gas (LNG) to its European markets. The U.S., on the other hand, eyes

Souda Bay and Alexandroupoli

, which are both military logistics bases that project power across the Eastern Mediterranean, Eastern Europe, and the Middle East.


These discussions highlight the impact of Rubio’s visit by demonstrating how Greece serves as the perfect “model NATO ally,” combining strong self-defense investments with a dominance in strategic energy and logistics networks that support American interests.


The Contradiction


Rubio’s openly American-centric speech on Pnyx Hill talked about the ideals of protecting democracy and its future based on ideological goals.

title: Στρέφη, Σάββατο 17 Οκτωβρίου 2026: Αντιφασιστική – Αντικατασταλτική συγκέντρωση και πορεία γειτονιάς
content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης:

Στρέφη, Σάββατο 17 Οκτωβρίου 2026: Αντιφασιστική – Αντικατασταλτική συγκέντρωση και πορεία γειτονιάς


Η Ανοιχτή Συνέλευση Υπεράσπισης του Λόφου Στρέφη καλεί σε αντιφασιστική και αντικατασταλτική συγκέντρωση και πορεία γειτονιάς, το Σάββατο 17/10/2026 στις 18:30.


Η πορεία θα πραγματοποιηθεί ενάντια στη διαρκή στρατοπέδευση αστυνομικών δυνάμεων στον λόφο Στρέφη.


Το κάλεσμα:


Ημερολόγιο Λόφου Στρέφη – Οκτώβριος 2026


Εδώ και ενάμιση χρόνο, οι μπάτσοι έχουν στρατοπεδεύσει στον Λόφο. ΜΑΤ, ΔΡΑΣΗ, ΟΠΚΕ, ασφαλίτες και κάθε λογής κατασταλτικές δυνάμεις έχουν γίνει κομμάτι μιας καθημερινότητας την οποία το κράτος θέλει να καταστήσει κανονικότητα, ενάντια στην οποία αγωνιζόμαστε.


ΤΟΤΕ


Η υπόθεση της Prodea


Ένας χώρος που χρησιμοποιείται καθημερινά από τους κατοίκους και τους ανθρώπους της γειτονιάς, αντιμετωπίζεται ως ένα ακόμη κομμάτι της πόλης που χρειάζεται «αξιοποίηση» και διαχείριση. Η απάντηση στις πρακτικές τους έρχεται μέσα από την ίδια τη γειτονιά και την καθημερινή παρουσία ανθρώπων που δεν αντιμετωπίζουν τον Λόφο ως μια δημοτική περιουσία προς εκμετάλλευση, αλλά ως κομμάτι της ζωής και δράσης τους. Η αποχώρηση των εργολαβων δεν σημαίνει ότι τελείωσε η ιστορία. Γιατί το ζήτημα δεν ήταν ποτέ μονάχα το ποια εταιρεία θα αναλάβει ένα έργο. Είναι ένα συνεχές μοντέλο που θέλει τον δημόσιο χώρο να γίνεται αντικείμενο επενδύσεων, «αναβάθμισης» και τελικά εμπορευματοποίησης. Και αυτό το μοντέλο συνδέεται άμεσα με όσα συμβαίνουν συνολικά στα Εξάρχεια και στο κεντρο της Αθηνας: την τουριστικοποίηση, την άνοδο των αξιών της γης, την αλλαγή των χρήσεων και την προσπάθεια να αλλάξει σταδιακά το κοινωνικό και πολιτικό περιβάλλον.


Μέσα σε αυτήν τη διαδικασία βρίσκεται και η αστυνομική κατοχή του Λόφου.


ΤΩΡΑ


Στον Λόφο Στρέφη, με την εντολή κράτους, Δούκα και επενδυτών, πολιτικές συνελεύσεις και εκδηλώσεις καταστέλλονται από τους μπάτσους, γονείς και παιδιά τραμπουκίζονται, οι έλεγχοι και οι εξακριβώσεις εντείνονται με πρόσχημα τη διακίνηση ναρκωτικών, γίνονται δολοφονίες δίπλα σε ΜΑΤ και ΟΠΚΕ και τα ένστολα σκουπίδια τρομοκρατούν τα παιδιά.


Οι ίδιοι μπάτσοι που χαράζουν φασιστικά σύμβολα και κάνουν σεξιστικά σχολιάκια σε θηλυκότητες, που κατουράνε παντού για να σημαδέψουν «τον χώρο τους», εγκαθιστούν και επιβλέπουν τη ναρκοδιακίνηση για να καταστήσουν τον Λόφο έρημη χώρα.


Τι θα γίνει, πότε θα φύγουν?


Το ζήτημα δεν είναι μόνο ότι οι αστυνομικές δυνάμεις βρίσκονται πάνω απο το κεφάλι μας και για τόσο καιρό. Είναι ότι μια παρουσία που λέγανε πως θα ήταν προσωρινή και αναγκαία για την διατήρηση της “ασφάλειας”, κινδυνεύει να γίνει μέρος της καθημερινότητας. Όπως νομίζουν ότι έχουμε συνηθίσει τους μπάτσους στη γειτονιά, έτσι να συνηθίσουμε τους μπάτσους και στον Λόφο, να θεωρήσουμε φυσιολογικό έναν δημόσιο χώρο που επιτηρείται μόνιμα, να φτάσουμε στο σημείο η παρουσία τους να μη μας προκαλεί πλέον καμία εντύπωση. Να δεχόμαστε να γράφουν φασιστικά συνθήματα, να παρενοχλούν, να μας τραμπουκίζουν.


Αυτή η κανονικοποίηση είναι ίσως το πιο σημαντικό κομμάτι της υπόθεσης. Να παγιωθεί η αντίληψη ότι οι μπάτσοι αποτελούν κάποιο κακόγουστο διακοσμητικό στοιχείο του Λόφου. Και μαζί με τους μπάτσους, κάτι μας λέει ότι ίσως τους έρθουν και άλλες φαεινές ιδέες…


Και εδώ, το ζήτημα του Στρέφη συναντά το γενικότερο ζήτημα για τα Εξάρχεια. Η τουριστικοποίηση και ο εξευγενισμός δεν αλλάζουν μόνο τις τιμές των ακινήτων ή τα καταστήματα μιας περιοχής. Αλλάζουν το ποιοι μπορούν να κατοικούν σε αυτήν, ποιοι αισθάνονται ότι τους ανήκει, ποιες χρήσεις θεωρούνται αποδεκτές και ποιοι χώροι παραμένουν πραγματικά διαθέσιμοι χωρίς την προϋπόθεση της κατανάλωσης.


Μας είπαν ότι οι μπατσοι είναι εδώ μέχρι ο Εξωστρεφής να παραχωρηθεί.Τόσο τους κόφτει για ενα μικρό αυθαίρετο σε δασική έκταση. Δεν είναι απλώς ποιος θα διαχειριστεί το συγκεκριμένο κτίριο. Είναι τι θα σημαίνει η λειτουργία του μέσα στον Λόφο. Ο Εξωστρεφής έχει υπάρξει χώρος συνελεύσεων, προβολών, εκδηλώσεων, συλλογικής κουζίνας, παιχνιδιού και συνάντησης. Ένας χώρος όπου μπορούσες να βρίσκεσαι χωρίς να είσαι πελάτης και έτσι πρέπει να μείνει. Γιατί το να αποκτήσει ο Εξωστρεφής μια εμπορική χρήση και να γίνει ακόμη ένα μαγαζί στον Λόφο δεν είναι ούτε ουδέτερη αλλαγή, ούτε φυσικό ακόλουθο. Σε μια περιοχή που ήδη μετατρέπεται όλο και περισσότερο σε χώρο κατανάλωσης και τουρισμού, άλλο ένα κατάστημα δεν αποτελεί απλώς μια νέα υπηρεσία, αλλά ενισχύει μια συγκεκριμένη αντίληψη για το τι σημαίνει να υπάρχεις στον δημόσιο χώρο: κάθε χώρος πρέπει να παράγει, να …

author: Cas Smith
title: Responding to the far-right threat in Ireland
content:
It’s no secret that the far right is on the rise in several European countries, capitalising on the rising cost of living, health and education and lack of access to housing — largely laying the blame on immigration and the “failure” of multiculturalism.

In Ireland, a wave of far-right protests in 2022 targeting refugee and asylum-seeker accommodation sites was followed by a racist riot in Dublin in November 2023, in the aftermath of a stabbing attack. More recently, pogroms targeting refugees and migrants in Belfast took place between June and September this year.

Paul Murphy – Teachta Dála (a member of the Irish parliament, TD) for Dublin South-West, representing the People Before Profit-Solidarity (PBP-S) alliance, has played a leading role in building the movement against this tendency in Ireland.

Murphy recently spoke to Green Left, explaining that the Irish far right started gaining traction in online spaces during the COVID-19 pandemic, before taking a significant step forward during Europe’s refugee crisis in the wake of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

This allowed far-right figures and groups to grow in influence as asylum cases rose, going from “an entirely marginal, entirely peripheral almost entirely irrelevant force in Ireland” to one that had a notable presence on the ground in some communities, being able to elect some councillors and influence populist national parliamentarians.

As the number of Ukrainian refugees arriving in Ireland has declined since its 2023 peak, these groups have maintained their narrative through the targeting of International Protection Accommodation Services (IPAS) centres, which host asylum seekers from various backgrounds.

“They employed very racist rhetoric — suggesting that these people were a danger, tapping into fears that people have,” Murphy said.

Along with scaremongering, the far-right suggested that these centres were “luxury accommodations that homeless Irish people weren't getting — when in fact, they're terrible and overcrowded”.

Murphy said that in response to the scapegoating of refugees, “the government ended up adopting a lot of effectively far-right policies, forcibly making people homeless”, including deciding not to open any more IPAS centres. “Any single man who arrived here was made homeless. Not just homeless, made to rough sleep.”

Murphy said the far right then turned towards a feigned concern for the cost-of-living crisis, which – alongside housing – has been a key challenge in Irish society since the 2010s.

However, although far-right activism around immigration has slowed, it has continued to influence how people understand rising costs and the lack of housing supply.

“If you asked a random person in the street four or five years ago: ‘Why do we have this housing crisis?’, they would have said that this is about the developers, the landlords, the political parties that represent those interests,” Murphy said.

“People would have put forward a basic class analysis of the housing crisis.

“Whereas now, there's a chance that if you ask a random person [this question], they would attribute it to ‘so many people coming in’.”

Murphy said the government “is delighted for this narrative to emerge” and “adds to it significantly because it distracts from its own responsibility”.

Recent protests around the cost of “green” diesel, which is used widely in agriculture and taxed at a different rate, were widely supported, but all of the identified leaders had connections with the far right and or spouted far right ideas, said Murphy.

“They blockaded ports and they won considerable concessions in the context of a generally passive working class and an absence of social movements — with the exception of Palestine,” Murphy said.

“We supported it, [but] we said ‘there's a problem with this leadership, and the trade union movement needs to take the lead’,” said Murphy. Regarding the demand for cheaper diesel, “It can't just be about bringing the price of fossil fuels down, we need free public transport, we need to have retrofitting, we need to get away from reliance on fossil fuels...”

Murphy said that a “big positive” is that the trade unions are now “stepping onto the pitch in terms of the cost-of-living crisis” and there have been “unprecedented turnouts and votes for strike action across the public sector”, in pursuit of demands around cost-of-living protections and wages.

Far-right electoral formations — such as the quasi-fascist National Party …

author: Unknown
title: The Land to Those Who Work It:  Land Reform and Socialist Agriculture in the German Democratic Republic
content:
About Studies on the DDR


The German Democratic Republic (Deutsche Demokratische Republik, DDR) was a socialist state founded in East Germany in 1949 as a democratic, anti-fascist reaction to the Second World War and the subsequent restoration of monopoly capitalism in West Germany. The DDR represented a new Germany – one in which the land was redistributed, the means of production socialised, agricultural production organised into cooperatives, and significant advances made in gender equality, education, healthcare, and other areas of society. The DDR also cultivated friendly and close-knit economic relationships with other socialist states and exercised political and material solidarity with countries and movements fighting for their independence in Latin America, Asia, and Africa. In this series, we use the German acronym DDR instead of the English acronym GDR specifically because it has become a positive point of reference in many parts of the world and especially for countries in the Global South.


After the reunification of Germany in 1990, the DDR’s economy was dismantled and treated as a prototype for the shock therapy austerity measures that were soon imposed on other countries – not just the former socialist states. At the same time, the DDR was politically, judicially, and morally delegitimised. The publications in this series are a rejection of the narrative propagated by enemies of socialism, both new and old, that the demise of the DDR – and other socialist projects – proves the inevitable failure of any socialist policy and economy.


Through the series Studies on the DDR, the Internationale Forschungsstelle DDR (International Research Centre DDR), and Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research seek to stimulate a renewed engagement with the history, achievements, and principles of the DDR. After all, millions of people around the world are still fighting for advancements that were once a given in the socialist system of the DDR but were lost with its downfall.


1. Introduction


The state of contemporary global agriculture and food production urgently begs for alternatives. If the global food supply were distributed fairly and equally, everyone would have enough to eat. Yet, in 2025, 645 million people – roughly one out of thirteen – worldwide went hungry.

1

 Prices are further inflated through financial speculation on food, raw materials, and land, perversely ensuring that profits are reaped not only from basic goods needed for survival but also from growing rates of hunger as rising commodity prices themselves become targets of speculative trading.

2


While just over one-third of the world’s food continues to be produced by small farmers,

3

 massive agricultural corporations such as the ABCD Group – Archer Daniels Midland, Bunge, Cargill, and Louis Dreyfus – dominate global food cultivation, processing, marketing, and distribution.

4

 The result is that companies like those in the ABCD Group have a near monopoly over advanced agricultural technology and increasing control over globally centralised production and processing chains. This concentration of land ownership and the means of food production reinforces patterns established during the colonial era, driving monocultures, one-sided trade relations, and land evictions. These dynamics, in turn, exacerbate small-scale subsistence farming, extreme exploitation of agricultural workers, poverty, hunger, environmental destruction, and rural maldevelopment. While the development of capitalist relations in agricultural technologies and science has unleashed significant potential for food production, this has clearly not been used to satisfy people’s most basic need for food.


Decades after the dissolution of the DDR, we look back at its achievements – and what is to be learned from its shortcomings – for answers. In the DDR’s mere forty-five years of existence, the conditions in rural areas changed fundamentally. This change took place in three stages:


The first stage (1945–1948) was during the shift in the balance of power in East Germany after the Second World War, which marked the decisive starting point for the DDR’s agricultural transformation. During this period, land reform was implemented that broke up the centuries-old land ownership structures in the countryside. This process of democratisation created the first framework for new relations of production based on cooperation.

title: La France Insoumise, le fascisme et la révolution [3/3]
content:
Troisième volet de l'enquête théorico-pratique de Lucas Amilcar qui tente de restituer et resituer l'hypothèse révolutionnaire dans la configuration militante actuelle

1

, à savoir la menace de l'accession au pouvoir de l'extrême droite et une adhésion diffuse et plus ou moins critique à l'idée que son rival social-démocrate, la France Insoumise, repousse ce péril et permette une plus grande marge de manœuvre pour les années à venir. Après s'être interrogé sur l'état du mouvement révolutionnaire en France

(Volet 1)

, avoir constaté une crise de la pensée subversive et le retour de l'une gauche autoritaire

(volet 2)

, l'auteur propose d'esquisser différentes stratégies selon les configurations politiques à venir.


« De la défaite surgissent des itinéraires »


Carmen Castillo


La croisée des chemins


Nous l'avons décrit dans les deux précédents volets, les différents soulèvements de la dernière décennie -portés par des idées telles que l'anarchisme, l'autonomie, l'horizontalisme, les féminismes, le mouvement queer, l'insurectionalisme- ont eu pour point commun d'avoir été poussés par une grande dose d'idéalisme. Mais l'idéalisme, contrairement à ce que les militants « chevronnés » tentent souvent de faire croire, n'est pas toujours une chose mauvaise. Toute politique révolutionnaire doit en être dotée d'une grande dose.


Cet idéalisme de début de siècle, au cœur d'une époque politique moribonde et sans perspectives, a été extrêmement porteur. Il a permi de démolir de nombreuses digues que les idéologies et formes fossiles du XX

e

 siècle avaient construites pour empêcher tout écart de leurs girons. Il a permis à la politique de reprendre contact avec la vie et d'expérimenter, d'inventer de nouvelles formes inspirantes pour des millions de personnes.


Mais rattrapé par les contradictions et la perte de vitesse de nos mouvements, un grand nombre d'entre nous - cette génération politique issues des soulèvements des années 2010 - a été amenée depuis quelques années à repenser ce que nous avions vécu et d'en tirer des constats pour orienter la suite de notre action.

 [

2

]

 Mais à partir de ces bilans, déjà différentes voies sont proposées par les uns et les autres :


La première

 (voir volets 1 et 2) est celle de l'obstination autour d'une partie des idées libertaires (horizontalisme dogmatique, absence d'organisation non-affinitaire, défense de l'idée de l'archipel comme horizon politique, etc.). Elle a conduit à cette « crise libertaire » que nous avons déjà évoqué ; une sorte de repli sur soi et d'enfermement sous la forme d'un milieu se préoccupant parfois plus de son « lifestyle »

 [

3

]

 radical que de l'impact de ses paroles et actes sur le réel. L'absence de pensée et de propositions stratégiques condamne souvent cette tendance à la faiblesse et à une certaine aigreur qui se traduit par une critique (voir un sabotage) constant des tentatives organisées et stratégiques qualifiés de façon simpliste comme forcément « autoritaire »

 [

4

]

.


La seconde

approche, (voir volets 1 et 2), a profité au contraire du moment de déroute et de repli de ces dernières années marqué par la recomposition et parfois la confusion, pour mener un assaut contre l'esprit des mouvements du début de siècle. Découlant parfois d'une expérience personnelle décevante, voire traumatisante, ce sentiment a été alimenté par des groupes et intellectuels (qui eux sont généralement passés à côté des révoltes récentes) issus depuis longtemps des différentes tendances de la gauche autoritaire (certains trotskistes, décoloniaux ou anti-impérialiste ou alors carrément staliniens et maoïstes). La spécificité de ces derniers est qu'ils fondent leur pratique sur une théorie autoritaire de la révolution (et l'assume en général, à savoir : éduquer les masses, imposer une direction par le « parti » ou l'organisation sur le mouvement et prendre le pouvoir central par les armes ou les élections).

title: Students Say Cornell Banning Frat Parties and Adding Investigators Insufficient
content:
“Nowhere among these measures is the institutional change that students demand,” said Students for a Democratic Cornell.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Cornell University has suspended parties and social events at fraternity houses for the remainder of the academic year, and will work with state police and their sexual assault investigators on future cases.

The changes came in response to outrage over a gang rape at the university in 2024 that has brought national attention to the issue of sexual violence on college campuses and the failures of administrations to address the problem.

Cornell’s President Michael Kotlikoff announced these changes on Tuesday, after weeks of protest against the administration’s mishandling of the 2024 case that have escalated into calls for Kotlikoff’s resignation.

In 2024, a Cornell student, known by the pseudonym Jane Doe, reported that she had been drugged and raped by seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity on campus. Her case was initially dismissed by the district attorney after university police “summarized” her complaint while omitting mentions of sexual violence and drugging. In mid-September, Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit against the university, the Chi Phi Fraternity, and the 7 men. Weeks later, NBC reported on court documents and text messages revealing conversations rife with the language of rape culture among the fraternity brothers. Subsequent reporting on the university’s mishandling of Jane Doe’s case prompted protests at Cornell and the reopening of her case by the district attorney.

“I have spent the past weeks listening to students, faculty, staff, parents, alumni, and trustees, who have shared their feelings of deep connection and sympathy with Jane Doe, anger and frustration that this could happen at Cornell, and outrage at the broader prevalence of sexual violence against women in our society,” Kotlikoff wrote in his announcement Tuesday.

In addition to suspending fraternity parties and working with New York State police “trauma-informed criminal investigators,” Koltikoff promised more staffing to support students who come forward with complaints of sexual assault.

But students at Cornell have called these measures insufficient.

Students for a Democratic Cornell (SDC), which organized a protest on campus on October 5 that was attended by thousands of students and faculty members, said that the measures demonstrate a refusal “to make institutional change on sexual violence.”

In a press release shared with Truthout, SDC explained that “Nowhere among these measures is the institutional change that students demand; specifically, there is no mention of reforming Cornell’s corrupt judicial system or an independent investigation not led by the Board of Trustees.”

The group contends that these measures allow the university to skirt the blame for its part in mishandling the 2024 case as well as its role in creating a “campus-wide epidemic” of sexual violence at Cornell.

Saya Taylor, a member of SDC, explained that the group “will continue to push until all of our demands are met – not just a select few that allow the administration to place blame on other parties.”

While the SDC does not view limiting fraternity parties as a useful measure in combatting sexual violence, other groups disagree – as was clear in the chants and slogans calling for banning frats entirely during the October 5 protest.

Kaori Quan of Cornell’s Graduate Student Union (CGSU) told Truthout that the barring of fraternity parties for the remainder of the academic year does not go far enough. “Stopping frat parties for a year does not address the systemic issues on campus that perpetuate rape culture,” she said, “namely, the intertwined nature of donor money and Greek life.”

“Until Greek life is off our campus entirely, Cornell will continue to prioritize the money it brings in over the health and safety of both students and workers.”

Referring to Cornell’s plan to work more closely with state police and investigators, Quan added that “so long as there is money in protecting Greek life, the campus police and the investigators they work with will answer to university administrators, not the students they supposedly protect.”

“CGSU’s stance is that working more closely with state police will do more harm than good,” Quan also told Truthout.

title: Aynur Sarıca: Women must play a founding role in the peace process
content:
Aynur Sarıca of the Jineolojî Academy drew attention to the role women must play in the Peace and Democratic Society Process, saying that pressure and attacks against the women's movement in Kurdistan were continuing.


Sarıca said women must not be confined to following the process or being represented on monitoring commissions, stressing that their participation in decision-making mechanisms was crucial to building a democratic society.


Sarıca said women had played an important role in shaping social life throughout history, but that the nation-state mentality and patriarchal structures continued to attack women's labour, identity and lives. She added that women's historical role had been pushed into the background in dominant narratives.


 


Sarıca said women had often been treated as spoils of war or as instruments for ensuring the continuation of a lineage during periods of war and conflict, but had fought throughout history to defend their existence against such attacks.


She said attacks on women's identity, children, labour and social life had continued through different methods as conflicts intensified in Kurdistan. She added that operations and detentions targeting the women's movement were intended to prevent the struggle for women's freedom from taking root throughout society.


Sarıca said: “Women have asserted their struggle for existence in every period by declaring, ‘We existed, we exist, and we will continue to exist.’ They have carried on this struggle through their identity, labour, way of life and social relationships. In the context of Kurdistan, as conflicts have intensified, we have seen attacks on women's identity, social life, children and labour increase through special warfare methods. The targeting of the women's movement, attempts to undermine its social foundations and attacks driven by a patriarchal mentality were intended to create a barrier preventing the struggle for women's freedom from spreading throughout society.”


‘Women must be active participants in commissions’


Aynur Sarıca said women's role in the Peace and Democratic Society Process needed to be reconsidered, stressing that women could not be confined to positions on monitoring commissions.


Sarıca emphasised that women were founding subjects of a democratic, ethical and political society.


Sarıca said: “The women's struggle and women's freedom are among the fundamental areas around which we organise. Drawing on this paradigm and ideology, we have organised, and continue to organise, around how women's existence, lives and struggles should take shape within society. In the course of a democratic struggle, women cannot simply remain observers or be limited to positions on monitoring commissions. On the contrary, women are the founding subjects of a democratic, ethical and political society. For this reason, we continue to insist that women establish commissions, participate in them and take an active role in decision-making mechanisms.”


Sarıca said commissions composed exclusively of men would lead to social problems being addressed once again through a patriarchal approach. She stressed that women's commissions needed to be considered in their legal, political and social dimensions.


Sarıca continued: “If the commissions to be established consist only of men, society will once again be shaped by codes that impose sexism. This would mean that provisions and laws concerning women, labour, children and society as a whole would once again serve the dominant mentality. This is why we insist and struggle for women to participate in commissions as active decision-makers. We approach this not merely as a legal or political issue, but as a whole, including its dimension of building social life. We do not adopt a fragmented approach; instead, we act on the basis of a comprehensive model of governance and democratic life.”


‘A democratic model of life must be developed as a whole’


Aynur Sarıca argued that addressing social problems in isolation created conditions for massacres, deaths and sexism, stressing the need to build a comprehensive democratic model of life.


Sarıca said women's role in the peace process should also be considered from this perspective and added: “We have seen that fragmented approaches lead to massacres, deaths, sexism and all forms of fascism. title: Imperial dominance has always been linked with sexual violence (Entertainment Labor for Palestine)
content:
A post shared by Entertainment Labor for Palestine (@entertainmentlabor4palestine)

Imperial dominance has always been linked with sexual violence. It shouldn’t be surprising, therefore, that those supporting genocidal settler-colonialism abroad would gladly resuscitate career casualties of the #MeToo movement at home. Our unions failed to unite against this dangerous merger. Now all we can hope for is vigilant protection for the thousands of entertainment workers who will be impacted by the fascist, patriarchal politics of this mega corporation. [See Umberto Gonzalez for @thewrap “Why is Paramount Hiring So Many Men With Troubled Pasts?”]
