title: Aile Bakanlığı “Devlet korumasında değiller” demişti: Edirne'de kayıp 13 mülteci çocuk bulundu
content:
Edirne'de, İlk Kabul Arda Çocuk Evleri Sitesi Müdürlüğü'nden izne çıktıktan sonra geri dönmeyen 13 mülteci çocuk bulundu.

Yurt dışına çıkış yapmak isterken yakalanan ve İlk Kabul Arda Çocuk Evleri Sitesi Müdürlüğü'ne teslim edilen çocuklardan 14'ü, 11 Ekim'de, kendilerine verilen market izninin ardından kuruluşa dönmedi. Çocuklar dönmeyince görevliler, emniyete gidip kayıp başvurusunda bulundu. Bu sırada çocuklardan 1'i kuruma döndü.

Güvenlik güçleri, çocukları için kapsamlı arama çalışması başlattı. Çocuklardan 11'i Edirne kent merkezi ve Yunanistan sınırına yakın bölgede, 2'si de gittikleri İstanbul'da bulundu. 13 çocuk yeniden kuruma teslim edildi.

Çocukların kaybolması sonrasında hiçbir kurum sorumluluk kabul etmemiş, Aile ve Sosyal Hizmetler Bakanlığı yaptığı açıklamayla çocukların ‘devlet koruması’ altında olmadığını söylemişti.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Ilya Kharkow - How to Ruin Statistics
content:
Author

: Ilya Kharkow

Title

: How to Ruin Statistics

Subtitle

: A Lesson from Ukraine

Source

: https://voidnetwork.gr/2026/07/07/how-to-ruin-statistics-a-lesson-from-ukraine-by-ilya-kharkow/


“Statistics likes to talk about people in large numbers, because that way it can’t see their faces.”


EXCAVATOR


 No one looks at an excavator and thinks:


 “What a shame it’s not destroying anything right now.”


 But the moment I refused to take part in a war, people suddenly appeared who were convinced I was wasting my life.


LANGUAGE


 I’m tired of having to justify the fact that I was born in Ukraine and consider Russian my native language. I grew up in a Russian-speaking mining town in eastern Ukraine. It wasn’t a political statement. It was my life.


 Before becoming president, Ukraine’s current president played a president in the popular Ukrainian TV series

Servant of the People

. The show was in Russian. If most Ukrainians had spoken Ukrainian back then, the show probably would have been in Ukrainian too. But for some reason it wasn’t. Neither were most of the films, music, books, TV programs, and everyday conversations I grew up with.


 Some people see language as proof of loyalty. I see it as a tool. A hammer doesn’t become guilty because someone used it to hit another person. Language doesn’t either.


DUTY


 Talk of duty begins precisely where volunteers run out.


 No one asks a hammer whether it wants to drive nails or crack skulls. Its value is measured solely by its usefulness. Conversations about a man’s duty to his country often work the same way.


 If I am expected to pretend to be a tool, then let me be neither a hammer nor a rifle. I’d rather be somebody’s vibrator.


UNITY


 On the first day of the war, I boarded a bus from Kyiv to Lviv. Back then, every missile seemed to be flying not just toward the city, but directly at you. At least that’s how it felt.


 Somewhere along the way came the news that men were no longer allowed to leave the country. A strange feeling. That morning you had still been a person. By evening, you had become a prohibited category.


 Then soldiers pulled me off the bus. They forced me to sign a document stating that I was volunteering for military service. Later, friends explained that such a thing couldn’t possibly have happened. Later, women on the street politely reminded me that all men were expected to report to the draft office. Later, taxi drivers stopped asking for my destination and started asking: “The draft office?”


 TV talked about national unity. In reality, the world was losing its mind faster than a morning erection appears. I’ve already used some of these stories in my fiction. The rest are still too dangerous to publish.


 Everyone kept saying the war would be over in a few days. Four years have passed. No, the last missile won’t change anything. Some wars end before they begin. Others continue long after the ceasefire.


BORDERS


 There it is again: another well-fed, comfortable person talking about the importance of borders. It’s strange hearing that from people who cross dozens of invisible borders every day.


 The border between work and home.


 The border between a friend and a lover.


 The border between a child and an adult.


 The border between the person you were a year ago and the person you are today.


 Everything good in my life began with breaking someone’s rules. So whenever I hear that borders are sacred, I remember that love, emigration, and growing up begin with crossing them.


NATURE


 I’m tired of hearing that sex between men is unnatural. That we should look to nature for guidance. Fine. Let’s take a look at what nature actually has to offer.


 As a child from a broken home, it pains me to write this, but nature is not particularly sentimental. A cuckoo chick dropped into another bird’s nest throws the other chicks out to monopolize the attention of its foster parents. Nobody calls that unnatural.


 I’ve been on many dates. Some of them were terrible, but none of my partners ever tried to eat me afterward, as female praying mantises and some spiders do.


 Ducks evolved complex reproductive anatomy to protect themselves from gang rape.


 Maybe we shouldn’t look to nature for moral guidance in every situation. Maybe we should just make love.


 If morality is determined by nature, then infanticide, cannibalism, and group violence must also be considered natural.


 Fortunately, people usually build ethics not …

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Anti-Migrant, Anti-Muslim Extremists Drive UK Terror Threat Level Increase
content:
Anti-migrant and anti-Muslim extremists are becoming increasingly likely to attempt terrorist attacks against mosques and asylum seeker accommodation, Britain’s spy chief has warned.


MI5 director general Sir Ken McCallum said cases where anti-immigration and anti-Muslim views had tipped into “terrorist intent” were the “most marked trend” of the past year. 


In comments made as part of

his annual threat update

delivered on Tuesday, McCallum also said the recent upgrade of the UK terrorism level to “severe” (which means an attack is highly likely) was “driven in significant part by extreme rightwing terrorism”. 


The MI5 boss noted the case of a teenager who

planned to set fire to Inverclyde Muslim Centre

 in a racially-motivated terror attack, and described the demographics most likely to be drawn into extreme rightwing terrorism as skewing young and “driven by the internet”.


One mosque in Britain is

attacked every five days

, according to data released in July by the British Muslim Trust, the government’s partner for monitoring anti-Muslim hatred. It had tracked and verified 78 attacks and incidents at Muslim places of worship in the last year. 


The UK has seen a spate of protests and violent disorder outside hotels and addresses  believed to house asylum seekers since the Southport riots in the summer of 2024. 


August saw

attacks on addresses believed to house asylum seekers

 in Thetford, Norfolk, with a senior police officer

 telling the i Paper

 that such disorder is becoming harder to predict due to a “growing narrative” that all asylum seekers are a threat.


Last month,

anti-migrant protesters targeted

 the Marriott in Portsmouth, believing migrants were inside. In reality, a visiting Pakistani cricket team was staying at the hotel. 


McCallum’s wide-ranging speech on threats to UK national security included a warning about the risks posed by AI’s potential to produce new bioweapons, along with individually tailored propaganda and radicalising material. 


He named Russia as “aggressor number one” and the most serious foreign state threat to UK security.

title: Migrationspakt und GEAS: Neuer Anlauf in der EU-Flüchtlingspolitik (???)
content:
Dossier


„… Die EU hadert und ringt spätestens seit der Flüchtlingskrise von 2015 mit ihren Regeln für Asyl und Migration. (…) Inzwischen hat sich die Diskussion verlagert. Wichtige Akteure wie

Bundesinnenminister Horst Seehofer (CSU) richten ihr Augenmerk stärker auf die EU-Außengrenzen

. Die Idee: Die Menschen werden schon dort einem Asylverfahren beziehungsweise einer sogenannten Vorprüfung unterzogen, die Anträge würden in beschleunigter Weise bearbeitet. Abgelehnte Bewerber würden direkt abgeschoben. Mit Blick auf die Aufnahme der übrigen Menschen, also der Schutzberechtigten, sind zudem schon lang Alternativen im Gespräch, etwa dass aufnahmeunwillige Staaten wie Ungarn Geld bezahlen. Entwicklungsländer wiederum könnten auf EU-Zahlungen hoffen, damit sie ihre Bürger schneller wieder zurücknehmen und deren Perspektiven verbessern…“


Beitrag von Phillipp Saure vom 19. Juni 2020 im Migazin


, siehe dazu nachfolgend:


GEAS-Verschärfungswelle der EU: Rückführungsverordnung mit Return-Hubs in Afrika, Abschiebungen ohne Asylverfahren und bald die Aussetzung des Rechts auf Asyl?


[GEAS-Verschärfungswelle der EU] 38 Organisationen fordern: Bundesregierung muss im Europäischen Rat die Aussetzung des Asylrechts in der EU verhindern


„

Vor der Tagung des Europäischen Rats am 15. und 16. Oktober warnen 38 Organisationen, darunter PRO ASYL eindringlich davor, das Recht auf Asyl in bestimmten Situationen auszusetzen. Gemeinsam appellieren sie an die Bundesregierung, den diskutierten Vorschlägen entschieden entgegenzutreten und auf europäischer Ebene für den Schutz des individuellen Asylrechts einzustehen: „Eine von der EU genehmigte Aussetzung des Asylrechts wäre ein folgenschwerer Bruch mit den europäischen Grundrechten.“

Erstmals wird der Europäische Rat über Ideen diskutieren, wonach das Asylrecht vorübergehend ausgesetzt werden kann, wenn zum Beispiel sehr viele Menschen auf einmal an einer Grenze ankommen und vermutet wird, dass ihre Ankunft von einem Drittstaat instrumentalisiert werden könnte. Das würde bedeuten: Schutzsuchende könnten an europäischen Grenzen zurückgewiesen werden, ohne dass überhaupt geprüft wird, ob ihnen Verfolgung, Krieg, Folter oder andere schwere Menschenrechtsverletzungen drohen

…“ gemeinsame

Pressemitteilung vom 14.10.2026 bei Pro Asyl

 


Weniger Asylsuchende, noch weniger Schutz: GEAS verschärft den Trend


„

Die Zahl der Asylerstanträge ist im ersten Halbjahr 2026 erneut gesunken, während die Schutzquote weiterhin erschreckend niedrig ist. Das reformierte GEAS verstärkt diese Tendenz, wie erste Zahlen zeigen. PRO ASYL befürchtet einen Einbruch der Schutzquote. Denn mehr beschleunigte Verfahren bedeuten auch: mehr Menschen, die durch das Raster fallen

…“

Meldung vom 02.10.2026 von Pro Asyl

 


Ein Fundament, auf das gebaut werden soll: Der Migrationspakt ist erst wenige Monate alt, doch die EU-Innenminister wollen es noch verschärfen. Sogar über die Aussetzung des Asylrechts wird nachgedacht


„Den ganzen Tag hatten die EU-Innenminister am Donnerstag in Luxemburg beraten, am Abend trat EU-Innenkommissar Magnus Brunner mit Jubelmeldungen vor die Presse. Es gebe ein „Rekordtief“ bei den Asylanträgen in Europa, die Zahl der irregulären Grenzübertritte sei in den vergangenen zwei Jahren um 55 Prozent gesunken, verkündete er strahlend. (…) „Das ist eine wirkliche Veränderung, die zeigt: Unsere Reformen funktionieren“, sagte der aus Österreich stammende Brunner. Mit den Reformen meinte er das von ihm „Pakt“ genannte EU-Asylsystem Geas, das nach neunjährigen Verhandlungen am 12. Juni in Kraft getreten war. Aus Innenministersicht also alles in Ordnung? Von wegen. Der Pakt sei natürlich nur das „Fundament“, meinte Brunner. Und mit einem Fundament „hört man nicht auf, man baut darauf“. Und deshalb standen bei der Innenministerrunde gleich drei neue Reformen auf der Tagesordnung, mit denen die EU-Grenzen noch stärker geschützt werden sollen. Zum einen nahm die Runde die neue EU-Rückführungsverordnung formal an. Dieses neue Abschiebegesetz gibt unter anderem den Behörden weite Spielräume für Razzien in Privatwohnungen und anderen „relevanten Räumlichkeiten“ bei der Suche nach Ausreisepflichtigen. Abschiebehaft ist für mehr als 24 Monate möglich. Vor allem aber ermöglicht sie den EU-Staaten, nach eigenem Ermessen Abschiebezentren in Drittstaaten einzurichten. In die sollen Ausreisepflichtige gebracht werden können, wenn die EU sie nicht in ihre eigenen Länder abschieben kann. (…) …

author: Madhavi Madhu
title: Malaysian PM's meeting with Myanmar coup regime leader condemned
content:
Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing visited Malaysia on October 7–8 and met with Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in Putrajaya. Madhavi Madhu, a member of the Socialist Party of Malaysia (PSM) and a longstanding refugee rights activist, explains why this move has prompted concern and protests from human rights and refugee rights groups.

Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim should have maintained a stance toward Myanmar similar to his stance toward Israel, as both leaders fall into the same category: that of war criminals.

A protest was held on October 8 and a joint statement issued unequivocally rejecting and condemning the visit.

The protest was called by the Anti-Imperialist Coalition Movement (Gerakan Gabungan Anti-Imperialis, GEGAR) and the socialist student group AKSI and supported by local human rights NGOs such as Beyond Borders, Suara Rakyat Malaysia (SUARAM), Mandiri, Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH) Youth, Malaysian Islamic Youth Movement (ABIM), and the Coalition for Clean and Fair Elections (BERSIH).

They urged the Malaysian government to stand in solidarity with the people of Myanmar and refuse all formal recognition of the junta leader. They also highlighted that this presidential-level reception for the Myanmar President violates the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Five-Point Consensus.

The joint statement demanded: The immediate cessation of violence in Myanmar and dialogue among all parties concerned; mediation by an ASEAN special envoy; humanitarian assistance through ASEAN mechanisms; and a visit by the ASEAN special envoy to meet with all parties concerned.

The Myanmar president stated again that the regime will only accept the deportation of "genuine citizens" of Myanmar (Rohingyans are not recognised by the regime as genuine citizens).

So while this diplomatic engagement was justified as an attempt to resolve the so-called "Rohingya issue", it has been reported that no Rohingyans have been sent back to Myanmar.

Nevertheless, the recent deportation of 1500 refugees to Myanmar and the planned deportation of another 5000 is a dangerous shortcut and a violation of the principle of non-refoulement — the international law rule that forbids returning people to a country where they face serious threats to their life or freedom.

The Malaysian Bar Association has sought the High Court's permission to challenge the government's repatriation plan.

It is important to be mindful that, apart from Rohingyan refugees seeking protection, there are other refugees from various countries in Malaysia.

A holistic, human rights-based approach is important, and a promised refugee right to work during the previous election is definitely a more dignified and humane solution for refugees and Malaysia.

The government could use readily available United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees expertise and services to manage refugees, while setting up the Dokumen Pendaftaran Pelarian (refugee registration documentation) with more transparency.

author: Unknown
title: Trabajadores de la salud de Iowa exigen el regreso de una compañera deportada
content:
Fatou Traore se dirigía a su trabajo como personal de limpieza en los Hospitales y Clínicas de la Universidad de Iowa (UIHC) en la mañana del jueves 24 de septiembre, cuando agentes de ICE la detuvieron.


A pesar de tener estatus migratorio legal en Estados Unidos, y sin antecedentes penales, fue deportada a Sierra Leone—un lugar con el que no tiene ningún vínculo—el 12 de octubre. Traore es una querida integrante de la comunidad de Iowa City, y del Local 12 del Consejo 61 de AFSCME. También es madre de cuatro hijos, el menor de los cuales tiene solo tres años.


Cuando aprendí que fue detenida en Septiembre, me indignó que ICE se había llevado a alguien del mero hospital donde yo trabajaba. Muchos de los trabajadores en el hospital no sabían de su detención, o temían alzar la voz. Les escribí a todos los flebotomistas con los que había trabajado en la sede principal; algunos quienes también habían sido personal de limpieza en algún momento, y habían trabajado con Fatou.


Escribí un artículo para un periodico local,

Little Village

. Compartí las noticias para crear conciencia sobre su detención a través las redes comunitarias; desde mis supervisores y la alta dirección en UIHC, el equipo de fútbol donde juega mi hijo; la comunidad de yoga a la que pertenezco; mi propia familia y sus comunidades de fé, y el Taller de Escritores de Iowa—del cual me gradué en 2022—en fin, a todas las personas que conocía.


SILENCIO POR PARTE DEL HOSPITAL


Luego, pensé que una petición seria buena manera para generar conciencia y fomentar la acción colectiva. Meses antes, había circulado una petición para cambiar una regla de estacionamiento impopular que quería implementar el hospital.


Esta vez, nuestra petición demandó que el hospital—y otras instituciones poderosas en la comunidad—se pronunciaran en contra de la detención de Traore. Sin embargo, el hospital se rehusó, respondiendo: “Puedes expresar tu opinión a título personal, pero nosotros no podemos hacer ningún tipo de declaración al respecto.”


Ese es precisamente el problema: los que tienen un mayor interés en protestar contra las acciones de ICE y lo que le paso a Fatou no pueden hacerlo sin correr riesgos. Es por eso que el hospital y tantas instituciones en Iowa deben alzar la voz y decir que esto no está bien. La detención y deportación de Fatou son una aberración. Necesitamos que regrese a casa.


Desde su detención, su familia y comunidad; el centro de trabajadores Escucha Mi Voz Iowa; el Iowa City Catholic Worker (Trabajador Catolico de Iowa City), y la Red de Bienvenida al Inmigrante han trabajado incansablemente para lograr su liberación; movilizando a la comunidad y llamando a los representantes estatales y a los líderes religiosos a denunciar a las acciones de ICE.


Durante los procedimientos legales iniciados en su nombre, se le negó a Fatou el debido proceso. El gobierno la deportó a un tercer país antes de que un juez pudiera pronunciarse sobre su solicitud de suspensión de deportación, y se ignoró su petición de una entrevista para establecer temor creíble.


“El debido proceso significa brindarle a las personas una oportunidad genuina para ser escuchado ante de que el gobierno tome una medida con consecuencias devastadoras,” afirmó Mazahir Salih, de la Red de Bienvenida al Inmigrante.


NO SOMOS DESECHABLES


Fatou es un pilar de nuestra comunidad y nuestro lugar de trabajo. Su labor en UIHC ha impactado a innumerables vidas, demostrando su compromiso con la salud y el bienestar de los demás.


Yo soy flebotomista y ella es personal de limpieza, así que estamos en roles similares de cierta forma en que entramos y saliendo de las habitaciones de los pacientes; realizamos nuestro trabajo sin que casi nadie lo note, y somos poco valorados.


Se nos considera desechables, y la gente tiene la impresión de que no importamos—si no estamos ahí para hacer nuestro trabajo, creen que nos pueden reemplazar con cualquier otra persona—y eso simplemente no es cierto. La gente que realiza estos trabajos están comprometidos con estar ahí. Ella tenía la resiliencia para seguir haciendo este trabajo durante más de una década.


Exigimos que las autoridades—el Departamento de Seguridad Nacional, los representantes locales, líderes comunitarios y UIHC—intervengan para traer a Fatou de vuelta de inmediato; asimismo, exigimos que la delegación del Congreso de Iowa busque respuestas sobre por qué fue deportada antes de que fuera resuelta su solicitud de suspensión de la …

author: Joel Mukisa
title: Jumuiya’s Arts Censorship and Resistance in East Africa
content:
Introduction | Coordinated Jumuiya transnational repression 


In the recent past, our Jumuiya’s democracy scales have been trembling with the impunity of human rights abuses and a worrying trend of

transnational repression

. One incident that chilled the conscience of all freedom-loving East Africans was the

brazen abduction

 of Ugandan opposition politician, Kizza Besigye, on 16 November 2024 in Kenya by unidentified assailants who bundled him into a vehicle together with FDC (Forum for Democratic Change) member Haji Obeid Lutale, and drove him across the border to Uganda without any formal extradition process. After suffering the ordeal of being held in incommunicado detention, Besigye was arraigned before the General Court Martial and charged with offences relating to security and the unlawful possession of firearms and ammunition, which could attract the death penalty. In July of the same year, 36 other members of the FDC party had been

arrested in Kisumu, Kenya,

 and forcibly deported to Uganda where they were charged with terrorism despite having lawfully entered Kenya with the necessary immigration permissions. 


The Boniface Mwangi and Agather Atuhaire Torture and Deportation


Six months after the kidnapping of Kizza Besigye from Kenya,

Boniface Mwangi and Agather Atuhaire

, who are prominent Kenyan and Ugandan human rights activists respectively, were abducted in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, while expressing solidarity with opposition leader Tundu Lissu. There is a thread of consistency in the way all these major East African nations (mis)treat their opposition politicians and Activists. Like Besigye, Tundu Lissu faces treason charges ahead of contentious elections in Tanzania. Agather and Boniface not only endured days of incommunicado detention just like Besigye, but also reported suffering

severe sexual torture

, including rape and beatings by Tanzanian security forces. 


Since the cross-border snatch-and-transfer operation happened almost a year ago, Besigye and his counterpart Haji Obeid have not received due process contrary to the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights. Similarly, the enforced disappearances and ill-treatment of Agather and Boniface breached the human rights protocols of the East African Community and the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, to which all three countries are signatories.


There is a complex historical origin of artistic censorship in Africa, partly stemming from colonial policy. The post-independence African states did not shake off the institutional legacy of colonialism, including the suppression of critical artistic expression.  Through the use of draconian laws, censorship boards, and internet restrictions, more East African countries have registered excesses against the freedom of artists. 


Across the region, from the early 2000s to the mid-2010s, there was a fusion of different forms of art, from graffiti and mural paintings to subversive visuals and performances by creative artists who defied authoritarianism. 


Art Meets Gen Z Maandamano


 In April 2025, the

Kenyan police fired tear gas

 to disperse the audience that had gathered to watch Kenya’s national high-school drama competition. This followed the staging of a play,

Echoes of War,

 by Butere Girls High School. Kenyan authorities could not stomach a play, produced by students, set in a fictional kingdom where the youth have lost faith in their leaders. The play’s author, Cleophas Malala, was also briefly detained by police. 


Additionally, Kenya published the 

Statute Law (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill 2020

 in June 2020, with proposed amendments to the

 

Film and Stage Plays Act 1962 (Cap 222)

. The intention behind this move is to increase the reach and grasp of the 

Kenya Films and Classification Board (KFCB)

 to bolster its capacity for censorship of artistic works deemed critical of the regime. The following month in the same year, Tanzania passed a new law, the 

Electronic and Postal Communications Act (EPOCA), on Online Content Regulations 2020

, to tighten state restrictions on freedom of expression under the pretext of “morality” and national security. What the foregoing laws do is impose criminal prosecutions against grassroots satirists and online artists, further curbing dissent.

political participation

 and democratic expression in the recent #GenZ protests in Kenya, when young people …

author: Anne Marxze Umil
title: Global day of action vs IMF-WB
content:
Photo courtesy of Asia Pacific Forum on Women Law and Development

We are really delegitimizing the IMF-WB.

BANGKOK – The People’s Global Campaign (PGC) against the International Monetary Fund and World Bank (IMF-WB) marked October 12 as the Global Day of Action against the two Bretton Woods institutions.

The Bretton Woods Institutions or the IMF-WB are financial institutions established in 1944 at a conference in Bretton Woods, New Hampshire in the United States. The goal was to establish a stable international economic system after the devastation of World War II. The IMF and World Bank have been criticized for imposing loan conditions that push governments to adopt liberalization policies, including deregulation and privatization.

In a press conference on October 12, representatives from the women, indigenous peoples, migrant workers as well as leaders in local organizations in Thailand spoke how the IMF-WB destroyed people’s lives through neoliberal policies implemented around the world.

“Today marks the start of the Annual Meetings of the IMF-WB, and for the next several days, behind closed doors, they will be deliberating on the next major neoliberal scheme as the world economy plummets into further crisis and the people slip into further destitution,” said Donna Denina, spokesperson from the PGC.

The press conference was also joined by the Thai People’s Movement (TPM) against IMF-WB.

October 12 was the first day of the Annual Meeting of the IMF-WB which ends on October 18. Thailand is the host of the said event which will be attended by more than 15,000 participants from 191 countries, including central bank governors, economic policy makers and business leaders to discuss the world economy.

Denina said that the Global Day of Action protests also happened in different parts of the world, including the Philippines.

In its 80 years of existence, the IMF-WB plundered land, exploited the people and destroyed the environment, said Emily during the press conference.

“Since 1970, the number of migrants has continued to surge. In 2026, the number of migrants reached 304 million or 3.7% of the world’s population. Meanwhile, the number of refugees reached 117.8 million. This number will continue to rise alongside the plundering of natural resources and repression,” said Emily of International Migrants Alliance (IMA).

She lamented how governments have failed to address the root cause of migration and have only complied with the IMF-WB’s labor migration and labor export policies. “In this scenario, migrants become the new commodity for export,” Emily said.

Now with the aging population in the developed countries, Emily stressed that more migrant workers would be further exploited. “Under the slogan ‘migration for development,’ the World Bank frames labor migration as a way to address labor shortages in developed countries caused by aging populations so the business will not lose profit. To generate super profits, migrants are exploited to an even greater extent and treated like modern-day slaves.”

She said that migrant workers are often granted fewer rights and they enjoy less protection than local workers. They also face discriminatory and degrading conditions, including extremely low wages, restricted residency rights, quota systems, and the denial of other labor rights. They would tend to be isolated through “live-in” arrangements, requiring them to live in their employers’ homes or on company or plantation premises.

“Restrictions on their freedom to settle, move, or change jobs further limit their autonomy. They are also stigmatized, prevented from organizing or speaking out, and made scapegoats during crises, as seen during the 2008 global financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020,” she said.

Indigenous People leader Celestine AkpoBari represented the Ogoni people of Nigeria and the International Indigenous Peoples Movement for Self-Determination and Liberation (IPMSDL) said that Indigenous People are the primary caretakers of the world’s last frontiers “and are more often than not sidelined in the political and economic conversations of our countries.”

“We have every reason to join the resounding call of the peoples of the world: ‘Shut down the IMF and the World Bank!’ Indigenous Peoples are among those most affected by these traps, loan conditionalities, and other forms of deceit,” he said. “Our lands, forests, and waters are first to be targeted for plunder, while we face displacement …

author: Mag
title: Wird der „Herbst der Gegenwehr – Sozialabbau verhindern“ im Sommer 2026 nachgeholt?
content:
Dossier


„…

statt der steigenden Armut entgegenzuwirken, will die Regierung Erwerbstätige mit durchschnittlichem oder niedrigem Einkommen gegen Erwerbslose, Rentner*innen und andere Menschen mit wenig Geld ausspielen und plant eine weitere Umverteilung von unten nach oben. (…) Wir lassen uns aber nicht gegeneinander ausspielen. Solidarität statt Spaltung! Denn in diesem Land ist Geld genug für eine armutsfeste Daseinsvorsorge da

…“ Der (zu wenig befolgte)

Aufruf des Bündnisses „AufRecht bestehen“ im Oktober 2025

 zu einem Herbst der Gegenwehr sah Vieles richtig voraus und doch kam es bis zum Sommer 2026 noch viel schlimmer, immer noch ohne ausreichende Proteste. Neben unserem

Dossier zur sozialpolitisachen Gegenwehr der Gewerkschaften

 werden hier Strategiedebatten und Aufrufe sowie

Terminübersichten

 der sozialen Bewegungen gesammelt:


Aufruf zu Aktionswochen des Bündnisses „AufRecht bestehen“ von Ende Oktober bis Mitte November: „Trotz allem nicht wehrlos!“


„

Liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen,


der Generalangriff auf den Sozialstaat ist in vollem Gange. Seit Juli ersetzt die „Neue Grundsicherung“ das Bürgergeld und beinhaltet eine Reihe von Verschärfungen, die die Lebensbedingungen von Leistungsberechtigten noch weiter bedrohen. Unabhängig von den Gesetzesverschärfungen schotten sich die Jobcenter immer weiter ab. Die Möglichkeit des analogen Zugangs bei der Beantragung von Leistungen, Abgabe von Unterlagen oder Klärung von Problemen wird immer weiter eingeschränkt. (…) Um dem nicht nur ohnmächtig zuzuschauen, sondern dem sozialen Kahlschlag Widerstand entgegenzusetzen, ruft das Bündnis „AufRecht bestehen“ zu bundesweiten dezentralen Aktionswochen von Ende Oktober bis Mitte November auf: Mit diesen Aktionswochen wollen wir vor Jobcentern über die rechtlichen Änderungen im SGB II informieren, Leistungsberechtigte über die eigenen Rechte aufklären und sie zur (kollektiven) Gegenwehr ermutigen. Dazu hat das Bündnis „AufRecht bestehen“ verschiedene Materialien erstellt

…“

PM vom 13 Okt 2026 bei der Koordinierungsstelle gewerkschaftlicher Arbeitslosengruppen


 zum Aufruf:


Aktionswochen des Bündnisses „AufRecht bestehen“ im Oktober und November


Trotz allem nicht wehrlos!


„

Der Generalangriff auf den Sozialstaat ist in vollem Gange. Unbeirrt von den Wahldebakeln in Sachsen-Anhalt und Mecklenburg-Vorpommern hält die Bundesregierung an ihrem sozialpolitischen „Reformprojekt“ eisern fest. Unter dem Beifall der Arbeitgeberverbände und auf Grundlage von Empfehlungen diverser „Expertengremien“ legt die Regierung die Axt an nahezu alle Bereiche des Sozialstaats. Rente, Gesundheitsversorgung, Pflege, Wohngeld und andere soziale Sicherungssysteme – kein Bereich sozialstaatlicher Errungenschaften bleibt von der Rotstiftpolitik verschont. (…) Einer der Pfeiler der als Reformen verbrämten Kahlschlagpolitik ist die „Neue Grundsicherung“, die seit dem 1. Juli das Bürgergeld ersetzt. Sie beinhaltet eine Reihe massiver Verschärfungen, die die sozialen Rechte von Leistungsberechtigten noch weiter einschränken, ihre Lebensbedingungen bedrohen und den Druck noch weiter verstärken. Zu befürchten ist, dass Armut, Ausgrenzung und Obdachlosigkeit in der Folge steigen werden.

Nebenbei schotten sich die Jobcenter immer weiter ab und versuchen immer häufiger, Betroffenen die Möglichkeit des analogen Zugangs zu nehmen und diese zu zwingen, Onlineportale wie „jobcenter.digital“ zu nutzen. Diese Praxis ist rechtswidrig und stellt für viele Menschen eine erhebliche Hürde dar.


Mit bundesweiten dezentralen Aktionswochen Ende Oktober/Anfang November 2026 wollen wir über die drastischen Veränderungen im SGB II informieren, Leistungsberechtigte dabei aber auch über ihre Rechte gegenüber dem Jobcenter informieren und zur kollektiven Gegenwehr ermutigen.


Hierfür wollen wir vor Jobcentern zum einen eine Handreichung mit Informationen und Tipps zur Neuen Grundsicherung des Bündnisses „AufRecht bestehen!“ verteilen, zum anderen Flyer und Musteranschreiben, die über das Recht auf analogen Zugang informieren bzw. dieses einfordern. (…) Wir fordern:


– Armutsfeste Existenzsicherungsleistungen, armutsfester Mindestlohn, armutsfeste Renten


– Hände weg vom 8-Stunden-Tag


– Mehr Qualifizierungen und Weiterbildungen


– Keine Kürzungen bei Gesundheitsversorgung und Pflege


– Gleichstellung von Menschen mit und ohne deutschen Pass


– Bezahlbaren Wohnraum


– Recht auf analogen Zugang zu Jobcenter und Arbeitsagentur


– Keine Kürzungen …

author: infolibre
title: Yδρογονοενέργεια. Κοινωνική απελευθέρωση και κοινωνική ισότητα σημαίνει ενεργειακή απελευθέρωση και ενεργειακή ισότητα
content:
Γράφει ο

Κώστας Λάμπος


Διδάκτωρ οικονομικών επιστημών

 του

FREIE UNIVERSITAET BERLIN


«Ανώτερο πράγμα κι’ από την αλήθεια είναι


το θάρρος να την πεις και να την γράψεις»


Αριστομένης


 

«Μπορεί να ανήκετε σ’ εκείνους τους ανθρώπους που νομίζουν ότι η ενέργεια του υδρογόνου είναι μια φαντασίωση κάποιων μελλοντολόγων ή κάποιων άλλων συγγραφέων επιστημονικής φαντασίας.


Ή, στην καλύτερη περίπτωση, μπορεί να την θεωρείτε ως μια πολλά υποσχόμενη μελλοντική τεχνολογία που, αν κάποτε εφαρμοστεί, αυτό θα γίνει στο μακρινό μέλλον. Εάν όντως σκέφτεστε μ’ αυτόν τον τρόπο, ξανασκεφτείτε το σοβαρά… Φανταστείτε έναν κόσμο στον οποίο η … (ανθρωπότητα) κέρδισε την ελευθερία της από το πετρέλαιο…


Μπορούμε να χτίσουμε αυτόν τον κόσμο μέσα σε δέκα χρόνια με την υπάρχουσα τεχνολογία… Φανταστείτε έναν κόσμο στον οποίο η (ανθρωπότητα) αποφάσισε να ξεπεράσει την ενεργειακή και την κλιματική κρίση που απειλεί την… (ύπαρξή) της. Μπορούμε να χτίσουμε αυτόν τον κόσμο σήμερα με συνειδητές επιλογές και πολιτική βούληση»

, αναφέρεται στο: 

Jerry Brown, Rinaldo Brutoco

και

 James Cusumano, Freedom From Mid-East Oil, Edition of World Business Academy, 2007


Καθημερινά ακούμε για το ενεργειακό πρόβλημα, από πολιτικούς, ‘ειδικούς ενεργειολόγους’, δημοσιογράφους, παπαγαλάκια της εξουσίας και λοιπούς ινστρούχτορες, χωρίς ωστόσο να τολμούν

να αναζητήσουν λύσεις, παρ’ ότι όλοι γνωρίζουμε πως ενέργεια από ορυκτά καύσιμα και απάνθρωποι και καταστροφικοί πόλεμοι αποτελούν την όψη του ίδιου νομίσματος, με το οποίο οι πλούσιοι γίνονται πλουσιότεροι και οι φτωχοί φτωχότεροι. Ανυπότακτοι, όμως επιστήμονες με ακέραιη την κοινωνική και επιστημονική τους συνείδηση έχουν εδώ και δεκαετίες δημιουργήσει την εναλλακτική μορφή ενέργειας με την συνδυασμένη συμπληρωματική συνεργασία των ανανεώσιμων πηγών ενέργειας, (ΑΠΕ), όπως ο ήλιος, ο άνεμος, η γεωθερμία, η δύναμη των κυμάτων κ.λπ κλπ. Αυτές οι πηγές ενέργειας μπορούν σε αποκεντρωμένη σε επίπεδο καταναλωτή ενέργειας να παράξουν φτηνή ηλεκτρική ενέργεια, με την οποία μπορεί, όπως λ.χ. με την ηλεκτρόλυση του νερού, να αποσπαστεί το υδρογόνο που είναι ανεξάντλητο στο περιβάλλον μας και στο Σύμπαν και ως καύσιμη πρώτη ύλη να δώσουν, καταργώντας τα πανάκριβα συγκεντρωτικά ενεργειακά μονοπώλια, να εξασφαλίσουν, στον κάθε αυτοπαραγωγό και ταυτόχρονα καταναλωτή ενέργειας, άφθονη, φτηνή, καθαρή και ασφαλή ηλεκτρική ενέργεια, με την οποία θα μπορεί να ευημερούν άτομα, κοινωνίες, χώρες και ανθρωπότητα χωρίς να αναγκάζονται να υποτάσσονται στα συγκεντρωτικά ενεργειακά μονοπώλια και στους πολιτικούς τους υπαλλήλους. Αυτός άλλωστε είναι και ο λόγος που κανένα κόμμα, όπως και κανένας ακαδημαϊκός, ή συστημικός διανοούμενος που σιτίζεται στο Πρυτανείο της εξουσίας του Κεφαλαίου δεν τολμάει να καταγγείλει τα ορυκτά καύσιμα και τα συγκεντρωτικά ενεργειακά δίκτυα που ελέγχουν τις οικονομίες των επιμέρους κοινωνιών και της ανθρωπότητας συνολικά. Γι’ αυτό κανένας δεν αναφέρεται στην υδρογονοενέργεια και κανένας δεν μιλάει για κοινωνική αλλαγή, αλλά όλοι μιλούν για ‘πολιτική αλλαγή’, που σημαίνει πως όλοι βάζουν υποψηφιότητα για διαχειριστές του κεφαλαίου, κι’ ας τάζουν λαγούς με πετραχήλια. Όμως όλο και περισσότερο, όλο και περισσότεροι αντιλαμβάνονται πως την λύση θα την δώσει η Ενιαία Κινηματική Κοινωνία και όχι τα δημιουργήματα της τακτικής του κεφαλαίου με το divinede et impera, δηλαδή τα νόθα συστημικά μικροκινήματα.


*


Το είδος και η ποσότητα των πηγών ενέργειας που κάθε φορά μπορούσαν και μπορούν να αξιοποιούν οι άνθρωποι καθόριζαν και καθορίζουν ακόμα την ποιότητα και την επάρκεια-ανεπάρκεια των μορφών ενέργειας που χρησιμοποιούν και σε συνδυασμό με το είδος και τον τρόπο κοινωνίας και επικοινωνίας των ανθρώπων καθόριζαν την εξέλιξη των επιμέρους κοινωνιών και διαμόρφωναν πάντα και συνεχίζουν να διαμορφώνουν το αποτύπωμα του ανθρώπινου πολιτισμού. Αυτή η διαδικασία βρίσκεται σήμερα σε κρίσιμη φάση.


Το κρισιμότερο πρόβλημα της εποχής μας είναι, χωρίς καμιά αμφιβολία, το ενεργειακό. Κι αυτό, γιατί το υφιστάμενο ενεργειακό σύστημα των ορυκτών καυσίμων δεν μπορεί να καλύψει ούτε τις βασικές ανάγκες της ανθρωπότητας, επειδή η ενέργεια αυτή:


Είναι πολύ ακριβή, με αποτέλεσμα να την στερείται απόλυτα ή σχετικά το μεγαλύτερο μέρος του ανθρώπινου πληθυσμού.


 

Ρυπαίνει επικίνδυνα το περιβάλλον και υποβαθμίζει τους όρους ζωής στον πλανήτη.


 

Πυροδοτεί αλλεπάλληλους καταστροφικούς πολέμους για τον έλεγχο των ενεργειακών πηγών.


Η τρέχουσα πολύμορφη, πολυεπίπεδη και πολυδιάστατη παγκόσμια κρίση του καπιταλισμού …

author: LCM-Redaktion
title: Die Bedeutung revolutionärer Kultur
content:
Im Folgenden veröffentlichen wir ein zweiteiliges Interview, das vom

Radio Résistance

 mit Carlos Manangan, einem Revolutionär der Nationalen Demokratischen Front der Philippinen (NDF) und der philippinischen Diaspora-Organisation „Compatriots-NDF“, geführt wurde. Manangan ist selbst Künstler und schafft revolutionäre Kunst in verschiedenen Formaten, darunter Video, Musik, Theater und Puppenspiel. In dem Interview geht es um nichts Geringeres als die Frage, was revolutionäre Kommunisten auszeichnen sollte

. Dies

 bettet Carlos Manangan in seinen Ausführungen zur Geschichte und Strategie der revolutionären Bewegung auf den Philippinen ein. Da er selbst viele Jahre als Migrant in den imperialistischen Zentren gelebt hat, stellt er zudem seine Sichtweise auf die Entwicklungen der kommunistischen Bewegung an diesen Orten wieder.


Wer bist du und welche Rolle spielst du in der revolutionären Bewegung auf den Philippinen?


Mein Name ist June. In den sozialen Medien bin ich unter dem Namen John bekannt. Ich bin ein politischer Flüchtling und Organisator von Migrant:innen. Ich habe einen Hintergrund als politischer Flüchtling. Ich bin Künstler – nicht von Beruf, aber ich nutze die Kunst als Mittel zur Organisation und auch als meinen persönlichen Ausdruck des Widerstands gegen Ausbeutung und Unterdrückung, insbesondere gegenüber der Arbeiter:innenklasse und speziell gegenüber philippinischen Wanderarbeiter:innen. Aber natürlich bin ich stets solidarisch mit der Bewegung der arbeitenden Menschen weltweit.


Zunächst wollen wir mit dir über die Kultur aus der Perspektive der revolutionären Strategie sprechen, damit wir Einblicke in die theoretischen Grundlagen deiner Arbeit gewinnen können. Welche Rolle spielt Kultur in revolutionären Bewegungen im Allgemeinen?


Als Erstes müssen wir natürlich definieren, was Kultur ist, und dann darauf eingehen, was reaktionäre Kultur und revolutionäre Kultur sind. In meiner Praxis betrachte ich Kultur als Spiegelbild der Interessen und Werte in der Gesellschaft. Aber natürlich ist die Gesellschaft keine homogene Gesellschaft. Insbesondere gibt es verschiedene Klassen. Es gibt unterdrückte und ausgebeutete Klassen, und es gibt diejenigen, die andere Klassen beherrschen, unterdrücken und ausbeuten. Sie sind die herrschende Klasse. Die vorherrschende Kultur wäre also ein Spiegelbild der Interessen und Werte der herrschenden Klasse. Und in der heutigen Zeit sind die vorherrschenden Werte der bürgerliche Individualismus und dieses wahnsinnige Verlangen nach Privateigentum, denn wir leben im Zeitalter des Kapitalismus. Und die Kultur des Kapitalismus spiegelt die Gier nach Profit wider. Und diese lässt sich nur durch Unterdrückung und Ausbeutung erreichen, insbesondere der Arbeiter:innenklasse. Wenn wir also von revolutionärer Kultur sprechen, ist dies das Gegenteil der derzeit vorherrschenden Kultur. Sie ist der Ausdruck des Strebens der Arbeiter:innenklasse nach Freiheit. Freiheit von Ausbeutung und Unterdrückung. Wir wollen also eine Gesellschaft schaffen, die frei von Ausbeutung und Unterdrückung einer Klasse durch eine andere ist. Das ist die revolutionäre Kultur: Unsere Bestrebungen und Werte, die wir vertreten, um Revolutionär:innen zu werden.


Gibt es eurer Meinung nach universelle Aspekte revolutionärer Kultur, die in jedem konkreten kulturellen Kontext gleich sind, insbesondere im Hinblick der Unterschiede zwischen imperialistischen Zentren und halbkolonialen Ländern?


Um unsere politische Arbeit zu leisten, ist es notwendig, tiefgreifend zu verstehen, was wir als Revolutionär:innen erreichen wollen. Es mag zwar einen globalen Traum von uns geben, aber es gibt auch lokale Realitäten, denen wir uns stellen müssen, sowie Probleme, die wir lösen müssen. Wir müssen wissen, wer unsere Feinde und wer unsere Freunde, unsere Verbündeten sind. Deshalb müssen wir eine umfassende soziale Analyse und Klassenanalyse durchführen und die Gesellschaft untersuchen, sei es auf globaler oder lokaler Ebene, unter Berücksichtigung der nationalen Gegebenheiten. Nur so können wir einen Speer zu haben, der wirklich scharf genug ist, die Rüstung unserer Feinde zu durchdringen. Er muss sehr scharf und nicht allgemein gehalten sein, und er muss im Bereich des Verständnisses der Massen liegen, die wir in eine revolutionäre Kraft verwandeln wollen.


Wir haben unterschiedliche Kontexte. Ob in der Schweiz, in den Vereinigten Staaten oder in anderen Ländern Europas – wir arbeiten in einem anderen …

author: Unknown
title: Beyond Polarity: For a Marxist Theory of the World Order
content:
Collage by Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research drawing from a Dymaxion map projection and Islamic, Mesoamerican, Ethiopian, and Chinese maps made between the twelfth and seventeenth centuries.


Images sourced from: Muhammad al-Idrisi, Tabula Rogeriana, 1154, 1929 reconstruction and transliteration by Konrad Miller via Wikimedia Commons; Matteo Ricci and Li Zhizao, Kunyu Wanguo Quantu (坤輿萬國全圖), 1602, Library of Congress Geography and Map Division via Wikimedia Commons; Códice Xólotl, Lámina 1, Tetzcoco, Mexico, c. 1541 via Wikimedia Commons; Tigrayan circular map from the Māshafā Aksum (Book of Aksum), pre-eighteenth century, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Collection Antoine d’Abbadie, via Wikimedia Commons; and Justinkunimune,

Blank World Map, Dymaxion Projection

, 2023, Wikimedia Commons, CC0 1.0.


The maps in this dossier trace how the hegemonic world order has organised and represented the world, from colonialism, the post-World War II international order, and Cold War bipolarity to internationalised capital, the North–South divide, and US unipolarity. More than representations, they distil concepts imperial and colonial powers have used to exercise power. Every dot of ink is a choice: what sits at the centre, which countries appear at the top, and which distortions are considered acceptable. The cover gathers cartographic traditions with different centres, orientations, and cosmologies, asking how, beyond poles and blocs, we might understand the unequal social relations that constitute the world order itself.


The Mercator projection was developed in 1569 for European navigation during the colonial period. During imperial expansion, it became the standard map projection, still used today.

This map, which shows the spheres of influence of the ‘great powers’ and their ‘possessions’, was created by H.E.C. Robinson in 1908. Sourced from the National Library of Australia via Wikimedia Commons.


The language of ‘unipolarity’ and ‘multipolarity’ – whether global power is concentrated in one dominant state or distributed among several major states – has become almost unavoidable in political debates. US and allied policymakers have often described the post-Cold War international system as a ‘liberal international order’ increasingly threatened by ‘revisionist powers’ such as China and Russia. Many governments and movements in the Global South, by contrast, welcome what they see as the emergence of a multipolar world in which Washington can no longer dictate the terms of international life. This aspiration is understandable. Any weakening of the United States’ capacity to impose blockades and unilateral sanctions, organise coups, and wage wars can open political space for sovereign development and for class struggles to advance.


‘Multipolarity’ may function as a slogan of resistance to US primacy and offer a rough description of how certain forms of state power are distributed. Its political appeal, however, should not be confused with explanatory power. The number of powerful states tells us little about the social relations that produce their power, the class interests organised within them, or the imperialist hierarchies that connect them. Multipolarity does not, by itself, provide a Marxist account of the world; when treated as such, it can mislead us into believing that a wider distribution of state power is inherently progressive.

1


Venezuela’s former President Hugo Chávez, who had every reason to welcome a world of many centres, was dissatisfied enough with the term ‘multipolarity’ to coin ‘pluripolarity’ against it – insisting that what mattered was not the number of centres but whether popular subjects were the agents of transformation.

2

 The need to specify this political content was itself revealing: the number of poles alone tells us nothing about the class forces or popular subjects shaping the resulting order.


A Marxist analysis must therefore replace the arithmetic of poles with the analysis of a chain: an unevenly developed system of social formations, each internally constituted by class struggle and externally bound to the others by relations of exploitation and dependence. The question is not how many poles there are but how the chain is held together and where it is most susceptible to being broken.


The problem, then, lies in the image of the pole itself. It asks us to picture the international system as a set of sovereign states treated as its decisive units, each …

author: Michael Albert
title: Liberating Theory: Vision and Strategy
content:
[This article ends the sequence from the seven author book Liberating Theory—by myself, Leslie Cagan, Noam Chomsky, Robin Hahnel, Mel King, Lydia Sargent, and Holly Sklar—published in 1986. This time the collective discussed vision and strategy. We here excerpt two chapters and their dialogues.]

So far, four sources of definition for society, not one or even two. A human center and institutional boundary, not an economic base and social superstructure. Accommodation, co-definition, and even co-reproduction between components all within an encompassing ecology and international relations. Social stability and/or social transformation. Three potential ruling classes, not two. Is all that and more just academic complex-ification or does it have simplifying implications for actual, worthy, workable vision and strategy?

Definitive evidence about the worth of these new concepts can only come from applying them to three critical questions: What features and dynamics characterize our society now? What is our vision of a more desirable future society? How do we expect to get from “here” to “there”?

Much has been written about the first question. While we hope that our holist principles will inform further analyses of contemporary conditions, we now focus our attention on the latter two questions.

Having argued so strenuously that societies are rarely if ever predominately determined by the characteristics of but one sphere, it follows that we should not limit our goals by visualizing a desirable future embracing less than all four spheres. Moreover, we should not label our vision for all of society with a concept that historically resonates with an emphasis on only one sphere.

“Socialism,” “feminism,” “intercommunalism,” and “participatory democracy” are appropriate names for different aspects of a desirable future society, but why use an economic concept to describe all of society unless one is economistic? And why use a kinship concept to describe all of society unless one is “kinshipist”? People justifiably distrust labels that reduce any of their priorities to peripheral concern. Thus, we will use the familiar labels as names for desirable ways of organizing particular spheres of social activity but we will use the more encompassing term—“humanist”—to describe the overall society we envision.

I interject from 2026: Names weren’t a strong suit for Liberating Theory. If you prefer, for the whole new society, perhaps the label “participatory society” would be better? Or maybe the name picked forty years ago will resonate? In any case it is the substance behind names that mainly matters.

The chapter continues: How does one elaborate a humanist vision? First, we need to decide what core characteristics we want in both the human center and institutional boundary. Second, we need to develop a vision of how social activity could be organized in each sphere so that our favored core characteristics would be generated. For example, what major governing institutions and decision-making systems could be expected to generate the core characteristics we desire? What community institutions and rules for community inter-relations would generate these desirable core characteristics? Third, we need to refine our vision of all spheres in light of an analysis of how the dynamics of each will affect the dynamics and characteristics of all the others. Here, we only outline approaches that will hopefully serve as a basis for further work by ourselves and others.

How does one justify the superiority of one set of core characteristics compared to another? Where do humanist values come from? What core characteristics embody humanist values? We know that human potentials are sufficiently broad that a number of different reasonably stable societal alternatives to our own are feasible. Moreover, since the behavior patterns, desires, and values of citizens in any society are in large part formed by the core characteristics of the institutional structures they encounter, we know that reproductive dynamics between any society’s center and boundary will promote values in their citizens that will tend to justify whatever core characteristics they daily encounter. It follows that if we ask merely whether people get what they seek in some society we will get a yes answer in many cases where the society is, nonetheless, oppressive. To have confidence in our evaluations we must ask, instead, in what society will people seek and attain the most. Unlike …

title: Effleurer l'avenir. Notes sur le technofascisme
content:
« L'avenir appartient à ceux qui savent perforer le présent »

 [

1

]

, écrit Cindy Coutant au début de son excellent

Pénétration terminale

, dernière publication des éditions Audimat. Perforer, c'est traverser ; mais traverser d'une façon bien particulière : traverser en vue d'atteindre, d'arriver – traverser

pour

 arriver. Perforer semble être cet impératif de l'époque que, il y a presque trente ans, un groupe d'auteurs anonymes décrivait ainsi « il faut supprimer le trajet ; il est impératif d'

arriver

 seulement »

 [

2

]

.


Perforer, c'est donc performer afin d'atteindre le plus rapidement, le plus efficacement possible, c'est trouer tout ce qui sépare de la fin, c'est performer l'atteinte. Cette performance ne va pas sans force, sans efficience, sans vigueur, elle est la promesse de la technologie, et des discours qui la sous-tendent relevant d'une « grammaire rigide de la perforation »

 [

3

]

. Il est question partout dans l'ouvrage de cette rigidité érectile comme imaginaire et cap du technofascisme. Seul un être rigide peut, en effet, « tout défoncer sur son passage »

 [

4

]

 – c'est-à-dire arriver à ses fins. Mais ce passage n'est pas infini, il ne peut être une dérive, liquide ou molle, un détour à jamais inachevé, figures du looser – de l'échoué – qui ne parvient pas. La perforation, la pénétration doivent être terminales. Coutant reprend l'expression à la balistique (une science des balles, une science

des projectiles

, donc,

une

science

 du projet

) :


La

pénétration terminale

 désigne la capacité opérationnelle de pénétration d'un projectile durant l'ultime phase de sa trajectoire : précision d'impact, capacité de percée, étendue des dommages selon sa nature anti-personnelle ou anti-matérielle. Si la balistique étudie les trajectoires sous tous leurs aspects, la balistique terminale est la branche scientifique qui étudie le moment où le projectile n'a plus d'options ; lorsqu'il ne corrige plus sa course, ne négocie plus sa vitesse, ne compose plus avec l'espace traversé. La trajectoire est verrouillée, l'horizon se referme en ligne d'impact : le projectile doit défoncer, et qu'il atteigne exactement sa cible ou qu'il la manque, il va le faire. La terminalité est tout à la fois une fin de parcours et le moment où l'action quitte le champ des possibles pour devenir exécutoire

 [

5

]


La balistique terminale s'intéresse donc au point de non-retour

 [

6

]

, qui porte mal son nom dans la mesure où ce moment est celui de l'impact, c'est-à-dire de l'arrivée : dans le projet, toute arrivée est un retour, puisqu'il s'agit d'atteindre ce qui a déjà été projeté au préalable, de parvenir là où on s'était imaginé aller,

de

retourner

 à

ce qui avait été projeté

. Et c'est ce qui explique, aussi, pourquoi l'imaginaire du technofascisme, qui est l'imaginaire de la projection par excellence, est un imaginaire nostalgique, réactionnaire : car, d'une certaine manière, tout projet est nostalgique, tout projet est une façon de retourner, retour en forme d'aller vers ce qui avait été prévu. La terminalité est le moment du passage à l'acte, en même temps que la preuve de la capacité à passer à l'acte, à être davantage qu'une pure puissance n'ayant pas éprouvé sa bravoure. La terminalité performe donc cette capacité à passer à l'acte – performance de son actualité en tant que, on va le voir, sujet masculin blanc occidental. La performativité/perforativité, que l'on pourrait à présent désigner par le syntagme perfor(m)ativité, peut apparaître alors comme une forme d'agentivité qui expliquerait certaines violences faites à tout ce qui est hors-norme, comme l'imaginent Véronica Gago et Luci Cavallero :


les féminicides, travesticides, transféminicides, lesbicides répandent l'idée d'un pouvoir absolu au niveau de la quotidienneté. Il n'est pas nécessaire d'avoir du « pouvoir institutionnel », il n'est pas nécessaire d'« être un grand homme », pour exercer ce pouvoir de tuer. Et, pour cela même, cet accès au pouvoir devient si attractif entre pairs. L'accès au gouvernement – au plus grand pouvoir institutionnel démocratique – d'une personne comme Milei, qui revendique de manière sinistre et efficace le pouvoir brutal de « ceux qui n'ont pas de pouvoir » (ceux qui ne sont pas la caste), « libère » un mode d'exercice du pouvoir que nous caractérisons comme passage à l'acte des « discours de haine » émis par l'État

7

]

While these words originally come from Social Anarchism and Organisation by the FARJ, this edited and abridged version represents our organizational understanding of this text which has been essential to the development of the Center for Especifismo Studies and the continuation of Militant Kindergarten. We have composed, numbered, and subtitled the following paragraphs by adapting our “Reading Guide” without page numbers or ellipsis to make for a smoother reading:

By especifismo, we refer to a conception of anarchist organization that has two fundamental axes: organization and social work/insertion. These two axes are based on the classical concepts of differentiated actuation of anarchism in the social and political levels (Bakuninist concept) and specific anarchist organization (Malatestan concept).

Synthesis advocates a model of anarchist organization in which are all the anarchists (anarcho-communists, anarchosyndicalists, anarcho-individualists etc.). So, it presents many of the characteristics that we criticize. We recognize that within synthesist organizations there are also serious militants committed to social anarchism, so we do not want the criticisms to seem generalized. Although we never question whether these organizations are anarchist (for us, they all are), they do not, in most cases, converge with our way of conceiving anarchist organization. There are diverse anarchist organizations that do not come out of the especifismo current. So, especifismo implies much more than to advocate anarchist organization. We understand anarchism as an ideology, that is, a “set of ideas, motivations, aspirations, values, a structure or system of concepts that have a direct connection with action – that which we call political practice”. title: Анархиста Алексея Григорьева избили во время этапа в Верхнеуральскую тюрьму
content:
Он ждал осмотра врача полгода и это время похудел на 20 килограммов. Ему нужна помощь адвоката, сообщает проект «Огни Свободы».

Григорьев осужден на 20 лет лишения свободы по обвинению в приготовлении к поджогу релейного шкафа и расклейку в Новотроицке Оренбургской области листовок с призывом к российским солдатам сдаваться в плен. В марте 2026 года Григорьева избили во время этапа из СИЗО-5 Екатеринбурга в Верхнеуральскую тюрьму (Т-1) — предположительно, за разговор с военнопленными на украинском языке. После этого у Григорьева образовалась паховая грыжа.

Осмотра хирурга в Т-1 анархист дожидался полгода. По его словам, за это время он похудел на 20 килограммов. Григорьев говорит о «вываливающемся кишечнике» (при паховой грыже содержимое брюшной полости выпячивается через паховый канал или рядом с ним) и постоянных болях в животе. Ему трудно есть и ходить в туалет. В Т-1 Григорьева поместили на строгие условия. С самого прибытия в тюрьму ему ограничивают переписку.

После осмотра 1 октября хирург выдал Алексею направление в тюремную больницу. Чтобы добиться лечения, ему нужны юридические консультации по вопросам условий содержания и оказания медицинской помощи. На работу адвоката, который будет посещать Алексея в тюрьме, нужно собрать 70 тысяч рублей.

title: Hatimoğulları'ndan Halk TV'ye dayanışma ziyareti: "Basını sansürlemekten vazgeçin"
content:
DEM Parti Eş Genel Başkanı Tülay Hatimoğulları, Parti Sözcüsü Ayşegül Doğan ve beraberindeki heyet, kayyum atanan Halk TV’nin Ankara temsilciliğine destek ziyaretinde bulundu.

Ziyaret sonrası açıklama yapan Hatimoğulları, kayyum atamasını kınadığını vurgulayarak şöyle konuştu:

"Heyetimizle birlikte sabahleyin aldığımız haber üzerine hızla buraya geldik. İstanbul'daki gelişmeleri takip ediyoruz. Halk TV'ye bir şafak operasyonuyla yüzlerce polisin baskın yapması asla kabul edilebilir bir şey değil. Kayyum rejimi bu ülkede parça parça tesis edildi. Belediyeler üzerinden başladı ve artık Türkiye'de kayyum atanmayan hiçbir şey kalmadı. Ticari kurumlardan tutalım da üniversitelere kadar ve bundan şu anda en çok muzdarip olan, gerçekten Türkiye'deki basın yayın kuruluşlarıdır, organlarıdır. Bunu kabul etmek mümkün değil. Halk TV'ye yapılan bu saldırıyı bir kez daha burada sizlerin huzurunda kınıyoruz.

Bir televizyonu yüzlerce polisle basmak demek, Türkiye'yi çok karanlık bir dehlize doğru hızla sürüklemek demektir ve biz buna defaatle tanıklık ettik. Bundan önce TELE1'de oldu ve son zamanlarda birçok kanalda gerçekleşti. Bugün şayet televizyonun sahibiyle ilgili başlatılmak istenen bir soruşturma varsa bu soruşturma televizyon kanalı kapatılarak yapılmaz. Burada televizyon kanalının kendi yayın akışına devam etmesine hiçbir şekilde müdahale etmeksizin bir soruşturma açılacaksa o soruşturma açılır. Ortada bir suç varsa onun gereklilikleri yerine getirilir. Ama ne yazık ki Türkiye'de artık bir şeye bahane üretmek için, basını sansürlemek, ekranları karartmak, kalemleri ve tuşları susturmak için önceden hazırlanmış olan hikâyeleri ortaya atıp, gerekçeler oluşturup toplumu böyle ikna edeceğini sanıyor bu iktidar. Ama yanılıyor. Bugün Halk TV'nin Türkiye'de milyonlarca izleyicisi var. Dolayısıyla milyonlarca izleyiciyi bu anlamıyla bu iktidarın yanıltamayacağını, bu şekilde bir karartmanın üstünün örtülemeyeceğini bilmesi gerekiyor. Bugün Türkiye'de tepkiler çok büyük. Bugün insanların duygusal olarak da siyasi olarak da toplumsal olarak da tepkileri son derece büyük."

Hatimoğulları, günlerdir Türkiye'nin gündemini meşgul eden fon kriziyle ilgili TBMM'de komisyon görüşmelerinin başladığına işaret ederek, şöyle devam etti:

"Böylesi bir zamanda televizyon ekranlarının karartılması aynı zamanda bu yolsuzlukların, yüzyılın fon vurgununun üzerini örtmek anlamına da geliyor. Çünkü bu anlamıyla muhalif olan bütün basını susturmak, mevcut olan iktidarla ilgili tek bir negatif yorum yapılmasına izin vermemek demek, bu dünyada görülmemiş bir basın sansürüdür. Kendi işlenen suçların üzerini örtmek için yargı yoluna başvurarak Türkiye'deki çeşitli kurumların, iktidarın elindeki kurumların devreye sokulmasıyla bu operasyonların gerçekleşmesi asla kabul edilebilir değildir. Buradan bir kez daha diyoruz ki Halk TV ekranlarını karartamazsınız. Yurttaşın haber alma hakkına müdahale edemezsiniz. Basının özgürce haber yapma hakkını elinden alamazsınız. Burada yapılan bu operasyon, şafak operasyonu ve yayın akışına doğrudan müdahale asla kabul edilemez. Bu müdahale Türkiye'deki milyonlarca yurttaşın haber alma hakkına yapılmış bir müdahaledir. Biz Halk TV'yle ve bütün Halk TV ailesiyle dayanışma içindeyiz. Sonuna kadar basın özgürlüğü için mücadele edeceğiz.

İnsanların ya da kurumların sosyal medya erişim hesaplarının engellenmesi, bu susturmaya eklenen yeni halkalar. Neredeyse her gün yüzlerce X hesabının engellendiğine, sosyal medya erişim engelinin olduğuna tanıklık ediyoruz. Bunları biz asla kabul etmiyoruz. Türkiye böyle manzaraları askerî darbe dönemlerinde görmüştür. Bu kadar ekranın karartıldığını, Kenan Evren'le bütünleşmiş olan 'gazeteler makas makas' dediği, böyle formüle edilen anlayışa biz şimdi ne yazık ki en ağır şekliyle bir kez daha tanıklık ediyoruz. Halk TV ailesine bir kez daha geçmiş olsun dileklerimizi iletiyoruz. Dayanışma içinde olduğumuzu bir kez daha ifade ediyoruz ve iktidara buradan net olarak sesleniyoruz. Basını sansürlemekten artık vazgeçin. Türkiye'yi karanlık bir tabloya sürüklemekten artık vazgeçin. Basını özgür olmayan bir ülkede özgürlükten ve demokrasiden asla bahsedilemez. Dayanışma içinde olmaya devam edeceğiz.

Şimdi biz burada bu konuşmamızı gerçekleştirirken arkadaşlarım aktardı. Polis şimdi Halk TV'nin Ankara ofisinin kapısına gelmiş durumda. Kuvvetle muhtemel İstanbul'da yaptıkları aramanın, taramanın, hukuki olmayan, yeri olmayan aramanın, taramanın birini daha galiba burada gerçekleştirecekler …

Одиннадцатое заседание. Четверг, 29 августа. Послеобеденное заседание.

Затем слово предоставляется товарищу Малатесте, который произнесёт в ответ Монатту одну из своих самых энергичных речей. В зале воцаряется глубокое молчание с первых же слов старого революционера, чья суровая и искренняя речь всеми единодушно любима.

ЭРРИКО МАЛАТЕСТА: Я хочу сразу заявить, что буду здесь развивать только те части своей мысли, в которых я расхожусь с предыдущими ораторами, и особенно с Монаттом. Поступить иначе означало бы подвергнуть вас тем праздным повторениям, которые позволительны на митингах, когда говоришь перед публикой из противников или равнодушных. Но здесь мы собрались как товарищи, и, конечно, никто из вас, слушая, как я критикую то, что заслуживает критики в синдикализме, не соблазнится принять меня за врага организации и действия рабочих; иначе он очень плохо знал бы меня!

Вывод, к которому пришёл Монатт, таков: синдикализм есть необходимое и самодостаточное средство социальной революции. Иными словами, Монатт заявил, что синдикализм сам по себе достаточен. И вот это, по моему мнению, доктрина радикально ложная. Борьба с этой доктриной и будет предметом данной речи.

Синдикализм, или, точнее, рабочее движение (рабочее движение – это факт, который никто не может игнорировать, тогда как синдикализм – это доктрина, система, и мы должны избегать их смешения) рабочее движение, говорю я, всегда находило во мне решительного, но не слепого защитника. Дело в том, что я видел в нём особенно благоприятную почву для нашей революционной пропаганды, а равно и точку соприкосновения между массами и нами. Мне нет нужды настаивать на этом. Нельзя не признать за мной одну заслугу: я никогда не принадлежал к тем анархистам-интеллектуалам, которые, после того как старый Интернационал был распущен, добровольно заперлись в башне из слоновой кости чистого умозрения; Я никогда не переставал бороться против этой позиции надменной отчуждённости – везде, где я её встречал: в Италии, во Франции, в Англии и в других местах; я никогда не переставал вновь толкать наших товарищей на тот путь, который синдикалисты, забыв о славном прошлом, называют новым, но который уже предвидели и по которому шли первые анархисты в Интернационале.

Я хочу – сегодня, как и вчера, – чтобы анархисты входили в рабочее движение. Я сегодня, как и вчера, синдикалист в том смысле, что я сторонник профсоюзов. Я не требую анархистских профсоюзов, которые тотчас же оправдали бы существование профсоюзов социал-демократических, республиканских, монархических или иных и были бы в лучшем случае годны лишь на то, чтобы ещё больше, чем когда-либо, разделить рабочий класс против самого себя. Я не хочу даже так называемых красных профсоюзов, потому что я не хочу так называемых жёлтых профсоюзов. Я хочу, напротив, профсоюзов, широко открытых для всех трудящихся без различия мнений, профсоюзов абсолютно нейтральных.

Итак, я за самое активное возможное участие в рабочем движении. Но я за него прежде всего в интересах нашей пропаганды, поле которой тем самым значительно расширилось бы. Однако это участие ни в коей мере не может равняться отказу от наших самых дорогих идей. В профсоюзе мы должны оставаться анархистами – во всей силе и во всём объёме этого слова. Рабочее движение для меня лишь средство, – очевидно, лучшее из всех средств, которые нам предлагаются. Это средство я отказываюсь принимать за цель, и я бы от него отказался, если бы оно заставило нас упустить из виду всю совокупность наших анархистских концепций, или, проще говоря, наши другие средства пропаганды и агитации.

Синдикалисты, напротив, склонны превращать средство в цель, принимать часть за целое. И так, в умах некоторых наших товарищей, синдикализм …

author: Joakim
title: Syndicalism With Extra Everything: How to Cut Through the Legal Thicket
content:
Article from Znetwork. Translated from the Swedish magazine Brand. The English version has been extended and modified for a wider audience. The Swedish article, in turn, is based on a more extensive education material. More articles in English here.

Illustration above by Stefan Ehn.

When workers organize and fight for their interests, they often encounter a complex legal framework – not least rules restricting strikes, blockades and other forms of industrial action. “As lawyers, we can help by getting the legal tangle out of the way, so that workers can focus on organizing.” This is how Rasmus Hästbacka, a lawyer at the Swedish union SAC, puts it. In today’s brutal labor markets, he advocates syndicalism with “Extra Everything”.

Even though workers are usually referred to in labor law as the weaker party, they are far from helpless. When workers come together in unions, they create the capacity to organize industrial action and win collective bargaining. When this happens on a broad front, unions become the vehicle through which the working class moves toward a brighter future.

Not even those workers who may appear the most vulnerable – migrant workers – are helpless. On the contrary, once the organizing gets going, they can become both an engine and a spearhead of class struggle.

In recent years, a small trade union in Sweden – the syndicalist union SAC, particularly its Stockholm Local – has distinguished itself by defending migrant workers against all kinds of crooks. A rambunctious Russian-speaking union shakes up Sweden’s labor movement, writes the freelance journalist Volodya Vagner. In Jacobin Magazine, he urges Swedish unions to wake up to new forms of exploitation and points to syndicalist examples of direct action.

But then labor law enters the drama offering help on the way as well as pitfalls and roadblocks. In 2019, the Swedish parliament introduced an anti-strike law. The law was pushed through by the Social Democratic government with support from top leaders of the three big union confederations – LO, TCO and Saco. The law entails certain amendments to the Swedish Co-Determination Act (abbreviated MBL). This has turned MBL into a legal thicket, a miserable mess.

At this point, the MBL framework may be difficult to grasp, but workers shouldn’t give up – for then employers have already won. Despite the anti-strike law, Swedish unions still have the right to launch so-called wage-extraction blockades to recover unpaid wages and take solidarity action in support of other workers. And this is just for starters – so join me for a closer analysis!

I will begin by discussing so-called soft pressure as a prelude to industrial action.

These are methods that don’t count as industrial action (in legal terms) and therefore aren’t covered by prohibitions against industrial action. This includes various forms of moral and psychological pressure, ranging from employees speaking with one voice to management at staff meetings to launching petitions and excluding bosses from workers’ social gatherings.

Soft pressure shouldn’t be underestimated. When employers aren’t receptive to arguments and facts, soft pressure can sometimes work wonders – simply because it creates a very uncomfortable situation for bosses.

Soft pressure also functions as a kind of union strength training. When a group of co-workers have successfully carried out soft pressure, they are soon ready for industrial action. Perhaps slowdowns, maybe an overtime blockade, perhaps even a strike. Once management has experienced industrial action, soft pressure too tends to become a sharper weapon. Management then knows that soft pressure may be followed by something even more uncomfortable. At that point, it might very well be deemed best to meet the staff’s demands.

Now, let’s proceed to industrial action and the legal framework in Sweden.

To get a clear picture of the MBL framework, we need to distinguish three types of situations. I start from the assumption that a syndicalist union wants to know if it has the right to take industrial action.

In the first type of situation, the syndicalist union is bound by a collective agreement (a union contract, as it’s called in the U.S.). This entails an almost total ban on industrial action (under Section 41 of MBL). In other words, a no-strike clause automatically follows every collective agreement. This contrasts with U.S. labor law, which allows union contracts without such clauses.

In the second …

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Lucia Mancini: The Woman
content:
from

The Transmetropolitan Review

, 04/10/2026


Click here for the full pamphlet version of

‘The Woman’


Lucia Mancini was likely born in or around Potenza, Italy in 1884. She immigrated to the US with her brother Eustacchio in 1900, eventually settling in Lynn, Massachusetts where she began to read and support the

Cronaca Sovversiva

 anarchist newspaper in 1905.


Lucia and her brother were members of the local anarchist Social Educational Club, which put on events and fundraisers, although Lucia left Lynn in 1907 to pursue work in Connecticut, likely as a seamstress. She rejoined her brother in Wakefield, Massachusetts in 1910 and it was here that she wrote her article ‘The Woman’ for the

Cronaca

 of July 1, 1911.


This text sheds light not only on the condition of women in the early 1900s, it likely explains why Lucia and her brother fled Italy without any other family members.


The Woman


When a mother, having endured the suffering and dangers of childbirth, brings into the world a female child, the members of the family consider themselves struck by a misfortune. And in this state of mind, one doesn’t even attempt to work. At times, the brutal husband goes so far as to openly express his displeasure at having become the father of a girl, and dares to upbraid the poor mother, even while she’s still suffering,

quasi

 reproaching her for having failed to conceive a male.


Thus, the woman is regarded as an inferior being, a useless and harmful encumbrance, and represents the family’s greatest source of anxiety, for they contemplate with terror all the troubles that might befall them on account of this being who had the misfortune of being born female.


Because, as is well known, the so-called “honor,” the prestige in other words, the reputation of the family, in accordance with the prevailing morality established upon the canons of the Church and sanctioned by the legal codes, is deemed to rest primarily upon the conduct of the woman.


A family is irreparably “dishonored” when a woman belonging to it, by breaking the bonds of bigoted morality and rebelling against the tyranny of the family itself, acts by heeding the impulses of her heart and the promptings of

her own

 intellect.


The education of women is therefore carried out under disastrous conditions. Her education, generally speaking, is limited just enough to enable her to read the hymnal, although without understanding much of it; absolute ignorance is the guarantee of her chastity.


And when the little girl becomes a young maiden, and her conscience is stirred by the first surprises of puberty, her mother will labor to explain the physiological reality to her with some tangled jumble of words from which she will learn nothing other than that “she has become a woman, and therefore is under an obligation to work harder and be more useful to the family.”


Later, the priest, to whom her bigoted mother entrusts the young girl for the completion of her education, takes care within the secrecy of the confessional to initiate her into the secrets of nature through a series of lewd questions pertaining specifically to sexual life and relations with men. And it is the beginning of the moral perversion that is destined to cloud the purity of conscience, the innocence of the young girl. While she learns from the priest that the male is an insidious creature, one to be shunned until the time of marriage, she will likewise discover that in fact there is a way to satisfy “certain natural needs” without the dangerous intervention of a male, and that one can enjoy oneself even more, and much better.


And from the tyranny of the family which measured her steps, counted and regulated the beatings of her heart, scrutinized and analyzed her thoughts, the young girl will seek to free herself through marriage.


But her husband imposes upon her a far heavier yoke, a fiercer tyranny from which she will be unable to escape save through death, unless she possesses the strength to rebel.


To rebel then, even outside the marital sphere, even within the family, against everything and everyone, is the path to follow in order to achieve emancipation.


When a woman has fully grasped her mission in life, when she knows how to liberate her mind from inherited prejudices and the unfortunate consequences of her upbringing; when she has convinced herself that she is not, as social injustice would have it, inferior to men, only then will the woman

know

 she can be …
