author: EDRi
title: EDRi-gram, 8 October 2026
content:
What has the EDRi network been up to over the past few weeks? Find out the latest digital rights news in our regular newsletter. In this edition: Turning up the heat – Commission backs social media bans, Apple held accountable, summer to-dos, & more!

This EDRi-gram edition includes a real snapshot of the disconnect between the kind of technology and protections people and communities around the world need, and the kind that are being pushed at us by lawmakers and companies either for the sake of profits, as easy fixes to structural societal issues or more sinister reasons.

Take the EU’s recently announced KIDS ACT. We unpack the many shortcomings of the proposal which is a missed opportunity to address the root cause of why online platforms are harmful to children – and everyone else. We also look at the Cloud and AI Development (CADA) Act, a part of the EU’s Tech Sovereignty Package announced earlier this year. What was sold as a way to jumpstart the EU’s “sovereign AI” ambitions seems to be set to hurt digital rights and environmental protections instead, while also imposing an unreliable technology onto us.

Elsewhere, Austria will soon get to find out what happens when AI systems are allowed to issue legally binding government decisions without any human oversight. EDRi-member epicenter.works detail the draft proposal and all the ways it could backfire.

None of the above is without resistance from those of us working to protect your rights. Dutch EDRi-member Bits of Freedom have launched a new campaign demanding a ban on Meta’s “pervert glasses”, aka, AI glasses which can be used to film people without them knowing. Meta was clearly paying attention – their viral satirical video on these glasses was removed from Instagram.

From critical campaigns, and urging EU countries to not treat data protection and “competitiveness” as opposing goals as they discuss the Digital Omnibus, to legal action against Big Tech corporations preying on our minds – we’re fighting back.

Next week, at our flagship annual event #PrivacyCamp26, we’ll be asking the real questions – where does technology come from? Who shapes it? And what would self-determination look like if it were defined by the people, not dictated by profits or a state’s agenda? We hope to see some of you attending!

author: Brian Hioe
title: What Did China Intend to Accomplish Through Surveilling Lai Ching-te’s Son?
content:
THE FBI HAS arrested a woman, Wanying “Heather” Zhang, for acting as an unregistered foreign agent of China. In particular, Zhang’s arrest occurred because she was apparently conducting surveillance on Lai Ting-yu, the son of President Lai Ching-te.

Lai’s family generally keeps a low public profile. Lai, who is in his 30s, is thought to work for electronics manufacturer Philips and to have a young child. Zhang is accused of traveling to Seattle from Los Angeles and renting a vehicle to surveil Lai’s home along with an accomplice.

Zhang is accused of being in contact with a Chinese handler through WeChat, as well as other individuals she knew were Chinese government officials. Zhang worked as a real estate agent and was detained as she was about to board a flight for Shanghai. It is possible, then, that Zhang could be a civilian recruited by China, or that the Chinese government has continued with its practice of employing “disposable” agents.

It is unclear what China hoped to gain from surveilling Lai, who was not likely to have any sensitive government information. Nevertheless, one aim could be to threaten, by putting Lai and his family members living abroad on edge, and to warn of the potential repercussions of going against China. If China wished to broadcast that it was aware of Lai Ting-yu’s whereabouts and could potentially threaten him, this could be used for leverage over Lai, or to blackmail him. China might also seek to project power, in suggesting that it is omnipresent and all-reaching, such that it can surveil and threaten relatives of Taiwanese politicians abroad.

Otherwise, it is possible that China aimed to obtain political ammo from surveilling Lai’s son. The presence of Lai’s son in the US, for example, could be used to suggest that Lai himself may push for strengthening defense against China, but that his own children live in the US, and that Lai would potentially abandon Taiwan in wartime.

Indeed, even if the daughter of Chinese President Xi Jinping is also thought to live in the US, the presence of Lai’s children in the US has been used as a political attack for some time by the KMT. More generally, Taiwanese politicians who have children in the US, or who may have potentially held Green Cards or US passports in the past, have been used to attack them with the allegation that they plan to abandon Taiwan in wartime.

More generally, one notes that the Chinese government has been increasingly willing to target relatives of Taiwanese politicians. DPP legislator Puma Shen’s father has been sanctioned, for example, due to owning a car parts company in China. It is possible that there are other cases in which relatives of Taiwanese politicians have already been threatened, but which have not necessarily come to light.

author: Isaac Nellist
title: Lizzie O’Shea: ‘Surveillance technology is a threat to democracy’
content:
Lizzie O’Shea, a writer, lawyer and founder of Digital Rights Watch, told the New South Wales Council for Civil Liberties’ (NSWCCL) annual fundraising dinner and journalism awards on October 1 that rapidly developing surveillance technology is throwing up many challenges.

Digital technology and democracy are in a “significant amount of tension”, O’Shea said. She added that defending civil liberties is not about “clever people working to impose civil liberties on everybody else”, but that campaigners “have to convince a critical mass that they have to defend their own rights”.

Referencing the origins of professional policing in London in the late 18th century, she described it as “a period of immense technological disruption”, as the Industrial Revolution was reshaping society.

The new police force, O’Shea said, was used to “monitor, enforce and impose the new conditions of social order”. Specifically, it ensured merchants’ profits and prevented dockworkers from supplementing their wages by pilfering stock. The idea was to get the state and industry to collaborate, with a “form of surveillance of everyday people”.

“Policing was talked about as a new science in the detection and prevention of crime,” she said. The spectacle of force “offered an economical and effective way of maintaining order”.

O’Shea said it helps explain the state’s decisions in the digital age. “Like their historical counterparts, modern police understand the power of surveillance in enforcing a form of discipline.

“‘Safety’ is about preserving social order, rather than reducing harm. By allowing law enforcement and intelligence agencies to tell us what is safe, we allow them to use technology in increasingly oppressive ways.

“Rapid technological advances have been accompanied by disruptive transformations in social relations, and an acceleration of policing has often been a response.”

O’Shea described advances in technology in the 21st century as being “a fundamental threat” to democracy. She said more than 100 “security” bills have been passed over the past two decades, connected to surveillance, national intelligence agencies and law enforcement, and 875 new offences have been created.

Many have sought to repurpose existing systems of corporate surveillance for state surveillance, while surveillance technology companies receive lucrative government contracts.

O’Shea also said Labor has “effectively abandoned” regulation of artificial intelligence (AI) and facial recognition technology.

“Less than 10% of Australians think it’s reasonable for a retailer to ask for your biometric information to access their services, but on an almost daily basis they will experience this.

“Everyone is telling us that AI is fundamentally important — politicians, the financial markets, a media that takes industry sources as truth — but a study by the University of Melbourne found that Australians are among the least optimistic in the world about artificial intelligence.

“More people are concerned about the negative outcomes than the benefits … 87% would be more inclined to trust and use AI products if international standards were in place to protect them.”

O’Shea pointed to the campaign to remove Palantir from Coles stores and the defeat of a data centre proposal in Lane Cove as examples of where most people’s attitudes lie.

“The hand of power is seeking to crush us, but we have the capacity to land a counterpunch,” she said. “This is the time for organisers, agitators, lawyers, ratbags and policy nerds to work together to build an alternative future where civil liberties are protected and our democracy can flourish.”

NSWCCL president Timothy Roberts told the gathering that the NSWCCL aimed to be an “ever-watchful guardian” of civil liberties, noting the huge challenges. He referenced last year’s March for Humanity, across the Sydney Harbour Bridge, when 300,000 people marched to protest Israel’s genocide in Gaza and demand that Labor act.

“It felt like the flame of liberty could not burn brighter or stronger — we must continue to celebrate that occasion as an example of the collective exercise of our human rights,” Roberts said.

The NSWCCL’s journalism awards went to Guardian journalists Ariel Bogle and Nino Bucci for uncovering the use of “less-lethal” weapons by police. Star Observer journalist Jacques Nieuwoudt won the young journalist award for his coverage of police raids of LGBTIQ spaces on Oxford Street.

author: Redazione_web
title: Fermiamo la propaganda di guerra, inceppiamo la macchina bellica, disertiamo gli eserciti
content:
La propaganda militarista continua a crescere ogni giorno sia a livello nazionale che internazionale.


Il messaggio delle istituzioni veicolato dai media è sempre più chiaro: dobbiamo prepararci alla guerra per difendere la nazione. L’aumento delle spese militari e delle missioni all’estero, il rafforzamento del potere del complesso militare-industriale, la capillarità della penetrazione dell’esercito nelle scuole e nelle università, la sempre maggior presenza dei soldati nelle strade delle città sono tutti segnali chiari della direzione in cui si sta andando.


In questo quadro si inserisce la questione della reintroduzione della leva militare in vari paesi europei. Se in Germania questo processo è già in fase avanzata, nel nostro paese, per ora, il modello scelto è quello di un rafforzamento dell’arruolamento, aumentando la propaganda soprattutto negli istituti scolastici, preparando così il terreno per il futuro ad un’eventuale reintroduzione della leva militare.


In questo scenario è di vitale importanza continuare a praticare l’antimilitarismo in tutti gli ambiti sociali e in tutte le occasioni possibili.


Sosteniamo lo sciopero internazionale contro la guerra indetto dalla CIT Confederazione Internazionale dei lavoratori per il 30 ottobre e le manifestazioni del 31 ottobre.


Indichiamo nel 4 novembre, giornata delle forze armate e dell’unità nazionale, una data significativa per sviluppare iniziative sui vari territori.


Appoggiamo le mobilitazioni che si stanno sviluppando a livello studentesco e territoriale contro il reclutamento per l’esercito e contro ogni ipotesi di reintroduzione della leva.

author: Rafael Custódio
title: No meio do caminho tinha uma norma – o que explica mortes causadas por policiais da Bahia
content:
No Carnaval de Salvador deste ano, Itamar de Assis da Cruz subiu ao trio elétrico do Samba Curuzu City como todos os anos. Aos 59 anos, ele reverenciava tanto a simbologia da festa quanto o bloco, os músicos, o repertório e o público alvoroçado na rua. Quando a banda começou a tocar

Na Areia de Itapuã

, uma canção autoral que fala sobre uma paixão platônica por Iemanjá, Itamar quase desmaiou. A música lhe trouxe memórias do irmão mais novo, Ivonei de Assis da Cruz, que seis meses antes fora morto por policiais militares no Curuzu, bairro da periferia da capital baiana. Ele tinha 42 anos.


Ivonei era produtor cultural, presidente de blocos carnavalescos e líder da comunidade onde foi assassinado em 1º de agosto de 2025. Naquela noite, ele havia feito um show pelo bairro. Por volta das 22h, após comprar um pastel para a namorada, ele cruzou com policiais militares da 37ª Companhia Independente de Polícia Militar (CIPM), que buscavam por suspeitos armados. “Calma, eu sou morador”, ele teria dito aos agentes. A frase não foi suficiente para evitar que os policiais atirassem em sua direção pelo menos duas vezes. Mesmo socorrido, ele não resistiu aos ferimentos e morreu no hospital.


O produtor cultural Ivonei de Assis da Cruz foi morto ano passado por policiais na comunidade do Curuzu, em Salvador


A morte do líder comunitário foi uma das 1.570 causadas pelas polícias da Bahia no ano passado, segundo o Anuário Brasileiro de Segurança Pública. Foram mais de quatro mortes por dia, média que dá ao estado o título de campeão brasileiro onde as polícias mais matam. O número é quase o dobro do registrado no estado de São Paulo, o segundo colocado no ranking da letalidade policial, com 835 mortes.


Nem sempre foi assim. Antes de 2019, os mortos por policiais na Bahia não haviam superado a marca dos 800 por ano. Foi justamente nessa época que a letalidade policial explodiu, fechando o ano de 2020 com 1,1 mil mortos em ações policiais – um salto de 47% ante os 773 do ano anterior. No mesmo período, o aumento da média nacional foi de 0,3%.


A

Agência Pública

 mergulhou no problema para entender o que está por trás desse vertiginoso aumento da letalidade das polícias baianas. Apuramos que, além do aumento da presença de facções criminosas no estado – usada muitas vezes como justificativa para agressivas operações policiais em comunidades –, uma norma editada pela Secretaria de Segurança Pública (SSP) em conjunto com quatro órgãos de segurança jogou gasolina na fogueira.


Em julho de 2019, uma Instrução Normativa dificultou que policiais militares fossem investigados pela Polícia Civil por mortes em ações e operações. A partir de sua publicação, os delegados só poderiam abrir inquérito sobre esses casos com requisição do Ministério Público ou ordem da cúpula da segurança pública.


Mapa interativo: clique no município para saber o número de mortes decorrentes de ações policiais


Além disso, a instrução normativa também determinou que, se o PM envolvido em morte durante um confronto comunicar “espontaneamente” o fato em serviço, a conduta vai ser considerada “justificada, salvo prova em contrário”. E também passou a definir o conceito de confronto como “ato hostil, especialmente mediante disparo de arma de fogo”.


O efeito da norma foi praticamente imediato. Desde então, o estado tem registrado mortes causadas por policiais em sequências estarrecedoras, que destoam do restante do país. 


A instrução normativa esteve em vigor por quase quatro anos.

 A pedido do Ministério Público estadual, a Justiça anulou em março de 2023 seis artigos da instrução normativa, considerando-os inconstitucionais, conforme

revelou A Ponte

. A letalidade policial, no entanto, já estava em patamares elevados, acima dos mil casos anuais, e nunca voltou aos níveis pré-2019. As vítimas são majoritariamente homens, jovens, negros e moradores de comunidades.


Muitas das violentas ações da polícia da Bahia nas periferias das grandes cidades se dá sob o argumento de guerra às drogas e guerra às facções. Entretanto, a maior presença das facções no estado não se traduz em mais violência: assim como no Brasil, os homicídios estão em queda na Bahia. Enquanto a letalidade policial mais que triplicou na última década no estado, os homicídios caíram 40% no período.


“A instrução normativa foi parte das decisões políticas para ‘proteger a institucionalidade militar’, mas o que de fato se verificou foi, até a sua derrubada, um processo de absoluto …

author: Sicilia Libertaria
title: La libertà si difende con la libertà
content:
Da tempo gli stati e il capitale attentano alla libertà degli umani, lo vediamo quotidianamente nel continuo attacco alle condizioni di vita in ogni angolo del mondo e nel nostro paese. Nei paesi del cosiddetto “primo mondo” si assiste ormai ad un’erosione continua dei residui di welfare e di stato sociale, con un impoverimento costante della stragrande maggioranza della popolazione a fronte di una minoranza di persone sempre più ricche. Il paradigma neoliberale ha vinto da tempo, imponendo massimi profitti per pochi e miseria continua per molti; lo stato sociale è stato sostituito dall’assistenzialismo mascherato da finto welfare. Nei cosiddetti paesi del nuovo capitalismo, quali India e Cina, prevalgono fortissime disuguaglianze ed un costante disciplinamento della popolazione, con un fortissimo sviluppo tecnologico che pone queste due nazioni come motori di un forte rinnovamento tecnico scientifico, portandole ad essere due entità imperialiste di primo livello, in particolar modo il “celeste impero”, che si sta candidando ad essere la nuova guida economica mondiale: stati che cercano in modo sempre più stringente di fare un’adeguata redistribuzione dei redditi nei confronti di una popolazione sterminata che esprime non poche conflittualità. Riusciamo ad avere più notizie in merito alle lotte dei lavoratori indiani, ma sappiamo che anche in Cina la conflittualità sociale non è sempre silenziata, sebbene la libertà delle persone venga quasi sempre repressa o scambiata con un relativo benessere sociale, utile ad addomesticare alla servitù e all’obbedienza.


Abbiamo poi

 innumerevoli masse umane come quelle che si trovano impegnate nelle estrazioni delle terre rare, disposte a morire tutti i giorni affinché il sistema di dominio globale possa continuare a perpetuarsi. Questo scempio di umanità subisce il disastro climatico che sta segnando in maniera sempre più ineluttabile il nostro pianeta: perché sì, l’umanità corre seriamente il rischio di scomparire. Non è un caso infatti che alcuni non facciano mistero di voler creare colonie in altri pianeti o di affidare all’intelligenza artificiale le sorti della nostra stessa esistenza.


Forse in questo momento come non mai il concetto di umanità è messo in discussione e la sua idea più alta, ovvero l’idea di libertà, rischia di scomparire. Gli Stati Uniti governati da un’élite suprematista e l’Europa con una dirigenza liberale ormai diventata conservatrice e post-fascista, con un ritorno prepotente di realtà partitiche che si rifanno al nazismo; la Russia tornata imperialista e autocratica, con una forte componente religiosa e tradizionalista; la politica fondamentalista islamica portatrice di un falso e pericoloso internazionalismo reazionario contrapposto ad un millenarismo ebraico che nella catarsi genocida ritrova la sua purezza primigenia; l’Africa e le Americhe portatrici di profonde trasformazioni telluriche ci rassegnano un’umanità al bivio della storia. Sappiamo bene che la guerra mondiale in atto accelera tutto quanto, ma sappiamo anche che il disordine può diventare tanto, le rivolte a questo ordine possono essere dietro l’angolo, proprio dove meno ce l’aspettiamo. La libertà non è uno spettro ma qualcosa che ancora scalpita. Chi fa la guerra e chi vuole un mondo di automi lo sa, così come lo sanno i potenti di ogni dove.


L’amministrazione Trump

 il 16 luglio ha organizzato un incontro internazionale contro i movimenti di sinistra ed in modo particolare contro gli anarchici. Non dobbiamo dimenticare che nella storia statunitense la guerra contro gli anarchici non è una novità, non ci siamo dimenticati l’attacco al sindacalismo e al sovversivismo messo in campo nel Novecento, i massacri contro le IWW e la morte di Sacco e Vanzetti in risposta all’incompatibilità degli operai e dei reietti nei confronti del mito americano, in continua lotta e sperimentazione sociale contro il capitale. In tempi più recenti osserviamo invece la messa fuorilegge delle organizzazioni animaliste come l’ALF o di radicalismo ecologista come Earth First, definite terroristiche. Adesso i golpisti di Capitol Hill al governo mettono fuorilegge gli antagonisti e in particolar modo gli anarchici. Non dobbiamo dimenticare che in questi ultimi anni i suprematisti si sono dovuti scontrare con un forte movimento antirazzista, di cui gli anarchici hanno costituito la parte più avanzata, distinguendosi in azioni a sostegno dei latini che tentavano di bucare i muri federali alla frontiera …

author: Joe Sandler Clarke
title: More US Soldiers Have Died in Iran War Than Pentagon Previously Admitted
content:
The Pentagon has quietly revealed that more US troops have been killed and wounded in the Iran war than it

previously admitted

. 


Twenty-one service members have been killed during the conflict and 865 wounded, according to data released without an announcement last Friday on an

official US military website

. 


A previous data release in August showed 18 killed and 757 wounded, while another last month listed 18 deaths and 820 wounded. 


As fighting has lulled for many weeks, it seems unlikely that the casualties are the result of fresh combat. The Intercept, which has been investigating undercounted casualties in the war for months, reported that one of the newly acknowledged deaths was on 6 March. 


An anonymous defence official told the outlet earlier this year that the US military was engaging in a “casualty cover-up”.


The latest change to the tally was made after

US politicians highlighted

 “a discrepancy in the Pentagon’s reporting of casualty numbers”.


US war secretary Pete Hegseth has furiously denounced journalists who previously reported that casualties from the war are higher than the military admits. In response to a

Washington Post story

 last month, he

posted

: “This is DISGUSTING and FAKE. A complete LIE.” 


Now, American politicians are demanding greater transparency over how many people have been killed or injured. 


Two Democratic house members, Adam Smith and Chrissy Houlahan, said they uncovered a discrepancy in the casualty numbers. “There is no excuse for a mistake of this magnitude,” they said in a

joint statement

 on Friday.


The US has given out little information about civilian casualties in the conflict. In September a US airstrike in the city of Kuhestak hit a wedding party, killing two people and injuring 70, the

New York Times reported

.


In February, a US airstrike on a school and sports facility killed 120 children, an action described by

UN investigators as a war crime

. A US inquiry found the strike was the result of outdated intelligence which said the school was

part of an Iranian military base

. President Donald Trump

attempted to blame

 the Iranian government for the incident.

author: hsa_oryx
title: A LOT HAS HAPPENED IN A SHORT SPACE OF TIME
content:
It’s hard to believe that it was only the 23

rd

 of September that we published an article with updates of what had happened during the hunting season so far, when so much has happened since then. Below we take a look at what has happened in the last few weeks of September.


Plymouth and West Devon Hunt Sabs announced that the Dartmoor Hunt have been issued with a Community Protection Warning (CPW). This follows on from continual complaints about anti-social behaviour, out of control hounds and trespass by the hunt.


The Dartmoor Hunt preparing to dig out a fox that has sought refuge underground.


In January 2026 the HSA released a

compilation video

 of the hunt, comprising of two separate incidents filmed by sabs and a third filmed by a member of the public. The incidents included terrier men preparing to dig out a fox, hounds tearing a fox apart and finally the horrifying site of hounds chasing a fox and killing it in front of a member of the public. Let’s hope this CPW is actually enforced as it should be, and the hunt is held to account for their despicable actions.


The Warwickshire Hunt, who were previously issued a Community Protection Notice (CPN), only to have it controversially removed by Warwickshire Police, are continuing to terrorise local residents. On Thursday the 24

th

 of September West Midlands Hunt sabs released a

video

 of hounds rampaging across land they have consistently been told they’re not allowed on. The landowner, who filmed the incident, can be heard shouting “oh god” and she is clearly in distress.


Warwickshire Hunt hounds allowed to tear through land they are not permitted to be on.


With mink hunts becoming more and more elusive as their numbers dwindle and they try to conceal their illegal activity it was welcome news that Suffolk and Essex Hunt Sabs reported that they’d caught the Eastern Counties Mink Hunt on the 26

th

 of September, thanks to a tip off.


Not long after arriving at the scene a mink was shot by a member of the hunt who then proceeded to try and stuff the dead animal in his hat in an attempt to try and prevent sabs from seeing it. Support were unhappy at this turn of events as they exclaimed sabs had ruined their “entertainment” because they hadn’t witnessed the mink being killed.


Sick supporters gather round to peer at the dead mink stuffed in Bennett’s hat.

© Suffolk and Essex Hunt Sabs.


The last week of September saw the opening meet of the Quantock Staghounds Autumn stag hunting season. The hunt met with less than 20 riders, hidden away on Fire Beacon Hill.


Unfortunately, a stag was selected and killed, but not before he was forced to endure being hunted down into Paradise Combe. Mendip Hunt Sabs reported that the hunt has begun behaving in an unusual manner, trying their best to conceal their sadistic activity. Quad riders confirmed the kill but tried to use the excuse that the stag, who had only that day been forced to participate in a drawn-out chase, was killed because he was lame.


Stag hunters, a dying breed, as numbers drastically dwindle at the Quantock Staghounds.

© Mendip Hunt Sabs


Even more disturbing reports have emerged from the south west as on the 26

th

 of September the Devon and Somerset Staghounds, not content with killing one, killed two majestic stags. Both stags were forced to endure a chase and we can only imagine the terror and pain they suffered. There have also been reports that some hunt followers were appalled at this behaviour, complaining that such magnificent animals were targeted.


One of the 2 stags targeted by the DSSH, exhausted and desperately trying to hide.

© North Dorset Hunt Sabs


On the 30

th

 of September, while sabbing the Beaufort Hunt with Bristol Hunt Sabs, Cirencester Illegal Hunt Watch came across another illegal hunt operating in the area, the RAC Beagles. The student run pack are from the Royal Agricultural University in Cirencester and like all beagle packs, profess to be hunting rabbits.


As we’ve seen recently with the conviction of Phillip Kennedy, the

Stowe School

 Games Coach, these packs are a way to indoctrinate youngsters into the organised crime world that is hunting. The Stowe Beagles pack housed at the aforementioned school, have come under the spotlight recently when the HSA released the footage that led to Phillip’s conviction and took a deep dive into the world of

school beagle packs.


Sabs took the RAC Beagles by surprise.

© Cirencester Illegal Hunt Watch …

author: PETA-Team
title: Tote Rehe für Wortwitz verhöhnt: „Speziesismus des Monats“ an smile Versicherungen
content:
Speziesismus ist in unserer heutigen Gesellschaft noch weit verbreitet, aber ethisch nicht gerechtfertigt: Bei diesem Denkmuster unterscheiden wir Menschen andere 

fühlende Tiere

 nach ihrem vermeintlichen Wert und Nutzen für uns – wir stellen uns über andere Spezies: Wir diskriminieren sie, beuten sie milliardenfach aus, lassen sie leiden und töten sie. Wir von PETA Deutschland vergeben regelmäßig den „Speziesismus des Monats“ als Negativpreis für Unternehmen, Prominente und Behörden, die mit speziesistischen und tierfeindlichen Aussagen und Aktionen auffallen.


Eine Werbekampagne der Versicherungsfirma

smile

 mit Sitz in Österreich und der Schweiz nimmt Wildunfälle zum Anlass, einen Wortwitz auf Kosten von Rehen als Slogan zu verwenden: „Reh umgefahren. Halb so wild.“ Aus unserer Sicht werden Rehe damit zu bloßen Hindernissen degradiert und ihr Tod für eine Werbebotschaft bagatellisiert. Für diese speziesistische Darstellung verleihen wir smile Versicherungen den Negativpreis „Speziesismus des Monats“ im Oktober 2026. Denn Speziesismus ist die Diskriminierung von Lebewesen aufgrund ihrer Artzugehörigkeit.


„Reh umgefahren. Halb so wild.“: Negativpreis für smile Versicherungen

 


Wildunfälle

 können für Tiere und auch für Menschen tödlich enden oder schwere Verletzungen verursachen. Die Werbekampagne von smile macht aus diesem Leid einen Wortwitz: „Reh umgefahren. Halb so wild.“ Aus unserer Sicht wird der Tod von Rehen damit verharmlost und für Werbezwecke instrumentalisiert. Die Tiere werden in diesem Zusammenhang zweitrangig als Objekte hinter dem finanziellen Schaden dargestellt – und ihr Tod als nicht so schlimm, weil der finanzielle Schaden ausgeglichen wird. Dass es sich um fühlende Lebewesen handelt, die durch einen Unfall ein schweres Schicksal erleiden, wird ausgeblendet.  


Für diese Darstellung verleihen wir smile Versicherungen den Negativpreis „Speziesismus des Monats“. 


„Die Kampagne von smile verharmlost das Leid der unzähligen Rehe, die jedes Jahr im Straßenverkehr auf grausame Art ums Leben kommen. Ihren Tod als vermeintliche Pointe eines Witzes zu benutzen, ist geschmacklos und hinterlässt den Eindruck, dass sie von den Verantwortlichen als reine Objekte angesehen werden. Es ist bedauerlich, dass die Texter:innen der Werbekampagne keinen Slogan gefunden haben, der sich für Mensch und Tier einsetzt.“

Peter Höffken, Fachreferent bei PETA Deutschland 


In einer von PETA angefragten Stellungnahme erklärt das Unternehmen, dass sie mit dem Slogan „halb so Wild“ ausschließlich den finanziellen Schaden am Fahrzeug darstellen wollten, der durch eine Versicherung reguliert werden kann. Ausdrücklich nicht gemeint sei das Tier selbst oder das Unfallgeschehen. Man empfinde Wildunfälle ebenso als schreckliche Ereignisse. Die Werbekampagne sei nun beendet.    


Millionen Wildtiere sterben jährlich im Straßenverkehr

 


Unter den größeren Tierarten fallen in Deutschland

Rehe

 besonders

häufig Wildunfällen zum Opfer. Im Jagdjahr 2023/24 waren es über 204.000 Tiere. Hinzu kamen unter anderem mehr als 15.000 Wildschweine. [1, 2] 


Doch die erfassten größeren Wildtiere sind nur ein Teil der Opfer des Straßenverkehrs. Jedes Jahr sterben auch unzählige kleinere Wildtiere wie Igel, Marder, Kaninchen, Vögel oder Kröten auf deutschen Straßen. Allein bei

Igeln

 wird die Zahl der jährlich überfahrenen Tiere auf 500.000 bis eine Million geschätzt. [3] 


In der Schweiz sterben jedes Jahr Hundertausende Wildtiere im Straßenverkehr.

Unter den größeren Tierarten fallen auch dort Rehe am häufigsten Wildunfällen zum Opfer. Im Jahr 2025 waren es 7651 Tiere. [3] Auf Schweizer Straßen sterben jedes Jahr schätzungsweise Hunderttausende weitere Wildtiere bei Wildunfällen, beispielsweise über 6000 Füchse im vergangenen Jahr. Besonders häufig sind Kleintiere wie Igel, Marder, Kaninchen, Vögel oder Kröten betroffen, von denen viele statistisch nicht erfasst werden. 


Wildtiere brauchen sichere und unberührte Lebensräume

 


Inmitten von Kulturlandschaften, Straßen und dicht bebauten Siedlungsbereichen wird der

Lebensraum für Wildtiere

 immer knapper. Dort, wo einst Rast- und Nahrungsgebiete waren, gibt es heute vielerorts kaum noch Platz. Insbesondere die auf Profitmaximierung ausgerichtete industrielle Land- und Forstwirtschaft trägt zum Verlust von Lebensräumen bei. 


Tierarten, die versuchen, in Koexistenz mit Menschen zu leben, werden vertrieben,

gejagt

 oder zu sogenannten „Schädlingen“ degradiert.  …

author: Sophie Lemcke
title: So ist es, als weibliches Rind in der Milchindustrie zu leben
content:
Die Milchindustrie ist ein grausamer Kreislauf des Leids und endet mit einem gewaltvollen Tod.


Wie fühlt es sich an, in dieses System hineingeboren zu werden, ohne die Möglichkeit, dem zu entkommen?


Der einzige Grund, weshalb die Industrie dich „produziert“ hat: Auch du sollst Kinder gebären, immer wieder, damit du Milch produzierst. Milch, die dann von Menschen, statt von deinem Kalb konsumiert werden kann.


Du wirst fixiert, während jemand das Besamungsgerät in deine Vagina sowie seinen Arm in deinen Anus einführt. Wenn die Zwangsbefruchtung nicht beim ersten Mal zur Trächtigkeit führt – was oft der Fall ist –, wird dieser Vorgang mehrfach wiederholt.


Neun Monate – wie bei uns Menschen – wächst dein Kalb in dir heran. Du spürst eine Verbindung, merkst, wie es sich bewegt und immer größer wird. Je schwerer du selbst wirst, umso stärker werden deine Gelenkprobleme. Die rutschigen und harten Spaltenböden, auf denen du fast dein ganzes Leben verbringst, führen oft zu Verletzungen.


Dann bringst du dein Kalb zur Welt. Um dich herum riecht es extrem nach Kot und Ammoniak, von den Ausscheidungen der Tiere.


Endlich ist es da, noch ganz nass und schwach. Du leckst ihm über das Fell, um es zu wärmen. Es sucht deine Nähe und will an deinem Euter die für ihn so wichtige Erstmilch trinken. Sie stärkt sein noch schwaches Immunsystem und gibt ihm Kraft. Doch dann kommen die Arbeiter*innen.


Sie zerren dein noch ganz wackelig stehendes Kalb weg von dir. Es ruft nach dir. Du versuchst, bei ihm zu bleiben, aber du hast keine Chance. Die Menschen haben es weggebracht – du wirst es wahrscheinlich nie wiedersehen und nach nur zwei Monaten direkt wieder gewaltvoll befruchtet.


Du wirst nach der Geburt monatelang mehrmals täglich in den Melkstand getrieben – und die meiste Zeit davon bist du bereits wieder schwanger. Dein Körper muss gleichzeitig ein neues Kalb versorgen, das in dir heranwächst, und täglich über 22 Liter Milch produzieren. Dein Euter und deine Zitzen schmerzen. Aufgrund der extremen Überzüchtung produzierst du viermal so viel Milch, wie du es natürlicherweise für dein Kind tun würdest.


Die Prozeduren und Haltungsbedingungen zehren stark an deinem Körper. Dein Euter ist entzündet und schmerzt bei jeder Berührung. Andere Tiere humpeln, weil ihnen jeder Schritt wehtut. Viele sind schwach und ausgelaugt.


Wenn du nicht schon vorher stirbst oder getötet wirst, weil dein Körper nicht mehr kann, dann wirst du voraussichtlich nach nur fünf Jahren getötet – obwohl du unter natürlichen Bedingungen 25 Jahre alt werden könntest.


Dann kommt der Tag, an dem du als nicht mehr profitabel giltst. Du wirst aus dem Stall getrieben – das erste Mal nach Jahren verlässt du ihn, aber das ist kein Grund zur Freude.


Zusammen mit anderen erschöpften „ausgedienten Milchkühen“ wirst du auf einen Transporter verladen. Du hast Mühe, über die Rampe zu gehen. Deine Gelenke schmerzen vom jahrelangen Stehen auf Spaltenböden. Im engen Transporter stehst du dicht an dicht mit den anderen Tieren, der Lkw wackelt. Manche fallen hin und werden versehentlich getreten. Eure Fahrt in den Schlachthof dauert mehrere Stunden, ohne Wasser, ohne Nahrung, ohne Pause.


Angekommen erwartet dich ein brutaler Tod. Überall riecht es nach Blut, du bekommst Panik, aber es gibt keinen Ausweg. Dann ein Bolzenschuss in deinen Kopf. Wenn die Betäubung korrekt durchgeführt wurde und wirkt, brichst du zusammen. Wenn nicht, kann es sein, dass du bei Bewusstsein und unter extremen Schmerzen erlebst, wie dir deine Kehle aufgeschnitten wird und du verblutest.


Es ist unvorstellbar, was Mutterrinder in der Milchindustrie erleiden müssen.


Der wahre Preis von Milch


Ein Ermittler von Animal Equality hat mehrere Monate undercover in einem deutschen Milchgewinnungsbetrieb gearbeitet und den Alltag der Tiere dokumentiert. Was unsere Undercover-Recherche zeigt, ist der wahre Preis von Milch: Ausbeutung, Gewalt, Schmerz, Leid und Tod.


Auf unserer Webseite erfährst du mehr und kannst die Stellungnahme des Betriebs nachlesen:


Zur Undercover-Recherche


Unterstütze dieses grausame System nicht!


Entscheide dich konsequent für pflanzliche Lebensmittel. Im Supermarkt findest du zahlreiche Alternativen zu Milch, wie:


Hafermilch – mild, cremig, perfekt für Kaffee und Müsli (oft die günstigste Option!)


Sojamilch – proteinreich, ideal zum Kochen und Backen


Mandelmilch – leicht nussig, besonders lecker in Smoothies


Reismilch – süßlich und gut verträglich …

title: Solidarität mit nichtmenschlichen Tieren im Klimakollaps
content:
Am 2. November ist Friederike Schmitz zu Gast in Leipzig. Ihr Vortrag beschäftigt sich mit der Frage von Solidarität mit nichtmenschlichen Tieren im Klimakollaps.

Plaque, Industriestraße 101, Leipzig

Orga: tierbefreier*innen Leipzig

Die Erderhitzung schreitet voran und wir müssen damit rechnen, dass Wetterextreme und Katastrophen unsere Gesellschaften massiv unter Druck setzen werden. Es ist daher realistisch, von Kollapsszenarien auszugehen – das bedeutet nicht zwingend ein einmaliges Ereignis, das plötzlich alles verändert. Es kann auch bedeuten, dass etablierte Systeme und Sicherheiten zunehmend instabil und unverlässlich werden.>

Die Kollapsbewegung fordert, dass wir uns gemeinsam darauf vorbereiten und solidarische Strukturen aufbauen, denn wer gegen Umweltzerstörung und Faschismus kämpft, kann sich auf den Staat nicht verlassen. Doch inwieweit sind nichtmenschliche Tiere dabei eingeschlossen? Und wie könnte es aussehen, wenn die Solidarität nicht an der Speziesgrenze haltmacht? Der Vortrag liefert einen Einstieg in diese Fragen und lädt zu Austausch und Diskussion ein.

Friederike Schmitz ist eine deutsche Philosophin und Publizistin mit dem Schwerpunkt Ethik und Politik der Mensch-Tier-Beziehung. Zu ihrem Schwerpunkt gehört die Klimagerechte Transformation von Landwirtschaft und Ernährung. In dem Podcast “Was zu retten ist?” thematisiert sie zusammen mit Annemarie Botzki (Campaignerin und Aktivistin) Klima, Kollaps und Ernährung.

author: L214
title: Végétalisation des menus des cantines scolaires : l’état des lieux de L214
content:
Au lendemain de la rentrée scolaire 2026, L214 dresse l’état des lieux de la végétalisation des menus des cantines scolaires dans 40 villes de France. Ce bilan, le premier depuis la prise de fonction des nouveaux élus à l’issue des élections municipales de mars 2026, révèle des situations contrastées : là où certaines villes se contentent du minimum imposé par la loi, d’autres font preuve de plus d’ambition, indépendamment de leur couleur politique.

La végétalisation des menus dans les cantines scolaires constitue un levier puissant et efficace à disposition des maires pour contribuer à réduire le nombre d’animaux tués pour l’alimentation en France. C’est pourquoi L214 propose trois mesures de végétalisation dans sa charte d’engagement du Sauvetage du siècle à destination des maires : instaurer une option végétarienne quotidienne, deux journées végétariennes hebdomadaires et un plat végétalien hebdomadaire.

Ce début d’année scolaire révèle de fortes disparités d’une ville à l’autre sur la mise en place de deux journées végétariennes par semaine. Sur les 40 villes de plus de 100 000 habitants étudiées par L214 :

14 villes proposent deux journées végétariennes par semaine ou plus,

12 villes proposent 5 à 7 journées végétariennes par mois,

14 villes se contentent d’une journée végétarienne par semaine, le minimum légal imposé par la loi EGalim.

Concernant la mise en place d’une option végétarienne quotidienne, le tableau est là aussi très contrasté : 11 villes proposent déjà cette option, alors que 24 villes proposent une option « sans viande » ou « sans porc » pouvant contenir du poisson, une alternative qui n’est donc pas végétarienne. Cinq villes ne proposent aucune alternative végétarienne quotidienne.

Certaines villes comme Bordeaux, Grenoble, Lyon, Montpellier et Paris font figure de bonnes élèves en cumulant d’ores et déjà une option végétarienne quotidienne et deux journées végétariennes hebdomadaires. D’autres villes vont même au-delà des mesures portées par L214, à l’image de Saint-Denis, qui propose 3 journées végétariennes chaque semaine dans ses cantines, ou de Montpellier, qui propose deux plats végétaliens chaque mois.

À l’inverse, Boulogne-Billancourt, Limoges et Le Mans notamment se limitent à une journée végétarienne par semaine, le minimum prévu par la loi.

→ Découvrir la charte d’engagement du Sauvetage du siècle

Cet état des lieux montre que la volonté de végétaliser les menus dans les cantines scolaires n’est pas portée par un seul parti politique. Parmi les cinq villes qui cumulent une option végétarienne quotidienne et deux journées végétariennes hebdomadaires, Bordeaux est dirigée par une majorité du centre, Grenoble et Lyon par des majorités écologistes, et Montpellier et Paris par des majorités de gauche.

Plusieurs villes affiliées à droite renforcent elles aussi la végétalisation de leurs cantines. Aix-en-Provence propose désormais deux journées végétariennes une semaine sur deux, et Metz en propose 5 à 7 par mois.

Pour Erwin Goeller, chargé d’affaires publiques de L214 : « La végétalisation des menus dans les cantines scolaires est un choix politique concret à la portée de chaque maire. L’enjeu a été pris au sérieux par plusieurs municipalités, mais les efforts restent très disparates selon les villes. Nous appelons les nouveaux élus à se saisir pleinement de ce sujet pour contribuer, à leur échelle, à réduire de moitié le nombre d’animaux tués pour l’alimentation en France ! »

title: Dixon Mink Farm in Bluffdale, Utah will be Forced to Close
content:
Dixon Mink Farm at 15028 Pony Express Road in the town of Bluffdale, Utah will be forced to close.

The city council of Bluffdale has eliminated fur farming as a permitted use. Fur farms will be unable to operate in Bluffdale.

The councilperson who pushed for the change said:

“I saw the serious issue the mink farm had on the lives of our residents. As I knocked on doors of our independence area there were so many flies people couldn’t open their door to talk to me. Because of this ordinance change the city can not approve the business license for this or any other mink farm.”

All nine are being lovingly looked after and tended to. None were released into the wild.


The lab chosen was that of Christopher Harshaw, who subjects mice and rats to experiments that purportedly aim to study autism, body temperature regulation and social behavior. This includes injecting them with drugs (including acetaminophen to induce neurodevelopment disorders), shutting them into small lighted cabinets overnight, and putting poisonous chemicals into their water like aniline (known to cause blood disorders and spleen tumors in rodents).


Moreover, Christopher Harshaw and his research assistant Anna are personally responsible for the killing of hundreds of animals per year, sometimes as many as 30-50 in a single day, as noted in Harshaw’s “Euthanasia Log” notebook, which on a previous visit was removed, had its pages photocopied (along with other documents related to animal research) and then put back. His death tally: 323 in 2023 (rats and mice), 575 in 2024 (rats and mice, including one wild mouse caught in a live trap and killed on the premises), and 363 in 2025 (all mice). His method: gassing them to death with co2.


Extensive video was also taken documenting the decrepit conditions of the lab as well as Roberto Refinetti’s animal room full of cages formerly housing squirrels (empty at the time of filming).


As should be clear: the purpose of this action wasn’t to vandalize, nor was it mere opportunism. This was a carefully planned and orchestrated live liberation of mice from Chris Harshaw’s lab. Its only purpose was getting the animals to safety as quickly as possible, therefore no equipment was damaged and no messages left at the scene. The whole operation, from entering the building to exiting with the animals, took ten minutes.


It should also be noted: This action was carried out using a minimum number of tools (none) and a minimum number of personnel (one).


This proves not only that lab raids can still be completed in 2026 but that one person, working alone, can successfully accomplish them.


To Chris Harshaw: Accessing your lab was child’s play, and with the hammer and drill on site it would have been only too easy to decommission every piece of equipment you own. Consider this a warning. In the end you were shown more mercy than the animals you hold captive.


And a word to all you would-be liberators out there: These facilities are not the fortresses you think they are. They are not impregnable. In fact the animal abusers in white coats have become so secure in their belief that no one is watching that they sometimes don’t even bother locking their doors! Use this negligence to your advantage. And while they sleep, go and do your work.


THE LAB RAID IS BACK.


Nine go free…


Another victory for the animals,


ALF”

author: Animal Rising Press
title: Guilty Verdict For King’s Sheep Rescuers In Theft Trial
content:
After a four-day trial at Norwich Crown Court, Rose Patterson, Sarah Foy, and Rosa Sharkey have all been found guilty of theft after the rescue of three lambs from King Charles III’s Sandringham Estate in May 2023. Sentencing to follow today.

Despite the verdict, Animal Rising claims that the rescue and subsequent trial have helped to put a spotlight on the reality behind animal farming in the UK, with over 10 million sheep being slaughtered yearly [1].

The controversial rescue made front-page news across the UK and headlines around the world [2]. It captured the attention of the British public, questioning how we relate to animals in the food system and if it’s a rescue or a theft to take them from farms.

Animal Rising director Rose Patterson, alongside Rosa Sharkey and Sarah Foy, rescued the lambs - Sammy, Sunny and Sooty - before informing police the following day. The women held signs outside Windsor Castle reading “I rescued the King’s sheep” before reporting what they had done to police. They each face up to 7 years' imprisonment.

Earlier this year, Patterson was found not guilty by a jury over another Animal Rising open rescue, after helping to rescue beagle puppies from MBR Acres, a facility breeding animals for testing [3].

Animal Rising director Rose Patterson, one of the three defendants found guilty today, said:

Sammy, Sunny and Sooty remain safe and are now fully grown.

The trial followed a series of open-rescue trials relating to Animal Rising’s rescue of beagles from MBR Acres. In January this year, Animal Rising made history by securing the UK’s first-ever not-guilty verdict in an open-rescue case [4]. The lambs were rescued from Appleton Farm, which forms part of the Sandringham estate.

Defendants Patterson and Foy are available for comment or broadcast interview upon request.

For further information, comment, or to arrange an interview, please email press@animalrising.org or call +44 1225 29 6691

Rose Patterson, 37, is the Director of Animal Rising. An advocate for animals since 2012, she holds an MSc in Animal Welfare Science, Ethics, and Law and previously worked with World Animal Protection before joining Animal Rising in 2020.

Sarah Foy, 26, has been involved in a range of campaigns advocating for a just and sustainable food system that works for animals, farmers, and the planet. She brings a practical, hands-on approach to her advocacy, with real-world experience caring for rescued farm animals at sanctuaries and protesting alongside farmers.

author: socialmedia
title: Newcomers to Trail Hunting Week: A Very Awkward Recruitment Drive.
content:
After last year’s embarrassing

Farcical Friday

, the pro-blood sports lobby group, the British Hound Sports Association (BHSA), has somehow managed to surpass itself in the ridiculousness stakes – and it’s not even

Smokescreen Saturday

 yet!


By now, you might have thought the hunting fraternity would have learned to exercise a little more care when selecting which hunts to showcase in its desperate attempt to maintain the smokescreen of trail hunting.


But no, you actually couldn’t make this up if you tried.


Erm, awkward. Trail Hunting is banned in Scotland.


Just days after a

Lauderdale Hunt huntswoman

 was convicted of illegally hunting a fox with hounds, the Lauderdale is advertising an event encouraging newcomers to discover the joys of ‘trail hunting’. The event poster was uploaded onto the Lauderdale Hunt’s social media and quickly spotted by Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs.


In Scotland. Where trail hunting is banned.


The Lauderdale’s joint meet with the Berwickshire Hounds is seemingly delighted to support

Newcomers to Trail Hunting Week

 in Wedderlie, Gordon, on Saturday 17 October.


Saturday also happens to be the annual smokescreen performance day, when a carefully selected (or perhaps a not-so carefully selected) handful of hunts are wheeled out to put on a display for Tory MP’s and other indignitaries. If they are lucky, GBeebies and the Torygraph might even dispatch a tea-boy masquerading as a journalist to cover the spectacle.


The since-deleted poster promises a warm-welcome courtesy of the Tilson family, a chance to meet the hounds and follow on horseback or foot. No previous experience is necessary.


Clearly, no previous knowledge of Scottish hunting legislation is needed either.


So-called trail hunting has been banned in Scotland since 2023.  Under the Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023, following an animal-based scent laid for hounds is prohibited.


As if that weren’t awkward enough, the Lauderdale Hunt was in the news recently for illegal hunting. 


On 05 October 2026, Claire Bellamy, former master and huntswoman of the Lauderdale Hunt, was convicted in Paisley Sheriff Court of deliberately hunting a fox with dogs outside the area permitted by a NatureScot licence.


In fact, it was reported that she wasn’t even named on the NatureScot licence in any case!


Convicted huntswoman Claire Bellamy wasn’t even named on the licence.

 Image: Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs


The poster invites the public to “Come and discover more about trail hunting and our community”.


Perhaps they first ought to discover what the law says.


The poster forms part of the wider campaign organised and promoted by the Countryside Alliance’s propaganda wing,

Future for Hunting

 and the British Hound Sports Association (BHSA) – itself a rebrand of the disgraced Hunting Office.


As if that wasn’t farcical enough, another participating hunt has managed to make this public relations disaster even more awkward.


Three Counties Hunt Saboteurs reported this week that The Worcestershire Hunt – one of the four hunts selected to put on a trail demo on Saturday – was filmed by a member of the West Midlands Badger group in an incident involving a fox and a badger sett.


The incident was said to have occurred in the Wilmcote/Aston Cantlow area of Warwickshire. Sabs say that an officer from the Badger Group who had been in the area in relation to a swan rescue, witnessed the hunted fox run past them near a canal.


She noticed two men in the corner of a nearby wood and approached them telling them that police were on their way. The men scarpered and the large badger sett where they had been was discovered to have freshly blocked entrances.


One of the two men by the freshly blocked badger sett at the Worcestershire Hunt meet.


After last year’s Farcical Friday, you might have expected the BHSA to be a little more selective, but then again, finding a hunt that actually lays a trail must certainly be quite a challenge for hunting’s propaganda unit.


A HSA spokesperson said


“It is no surprise to see this poster advertising what is essentially an illegal activity, made even worse by the Launderdale’s recent conviction. Sometimes they drop the ball and tell us exactly who they are, whereas other times they put up the smokescreen and invite pro-hunt MP’s and media to report on it once a year.


No one is fooled.


The government needs to get on with the job now and ban it properly”.

author: PETA-Team
title: Luchs aus Naturwildpark Granat entkommen und erschossen: PETA erstattet Strafanzeige | Update
content:
Update vom 13. Oktober 2026


Nach Ausbruch und Tötung von Luchs: PETA erstattet Strafanzeige gegen Verantwortliche


Nachdem Ende Juli 2026 Luchs Mikaesch aus dem

Naturwildpark

 Granat entkommen konnte und etwa zwei Wochen später erschossen wurde, haben wir von PETA Deutschland nun Strafanzeige gegen den Betreiber sowie gegen die für den Abschuss verantwortlichen Personen der Unteren Naturschutz- und Jagdbehörde erstattet.


Grund dafür ist ein offensichtlicher Widerspruch bei der Begründung des Abschusses: Einerseits hieß es, der Luchs habe nicht aus ausreichender Nähe betäubt werden können. Andererseits habe Mikaesch wenig Scheu gegenüber Spaziergänger:innen gezeigt, die ihn wiederholt aus kurzer Distanz beobachtet und sogar fotografiert hätten können.


Bereits kurz nach dem Ausbruch habe ein Radfahrer den Luchs in der Nähe des Tierparks gesehen und den Park informiert. Dieser Hinweis sei nach uns vorliegenden Informationen zunächst nicht ernst genommen worden. Der Wildpark habe stattdessen angegeben, dass dort kein Luchs fehle. Der Ausbruch hätte möglicherweise deutlich früher entdeckt und das Tier somit zeitnah eingefangen werden können. Erst nachdem es Anfang August zu einem Zwischenfall mit einem Hund und dessen Halter gekommen sei, seien umfangreichere Maßnahmen eingeleitet worden.


Möglicherweise könnte ein Ausfall des Elektrozauns den Ausbruch des Tieres ermöglicht haben. Laut Informationen des Landesamts für Natur, Umwelt und Klima Nordrhein-Westfalens (LANUK) und der Kreisverwaltung Recklinghausen sei es bereits 2014 und 2019 zu Luchsausbrüchen aus dem Naturwildpark Granat gekommen. Damit verdichten sich Hinweise auf grundlegende Sicherheitsdefizite im Tierpark. Wir fordern daher auch eine Überprüfung des Sicherheitskonzepts des Tierparks.


Unserer Auffassung nach wäre die Tötung rechtswidrig gewesen, wenn das Tier stattdessen hätte eingefangen werden können. Aus diesem Grund fordern wir auch eine umfassende Prüfung der Umstände des Abschusses.


Jetzt lesen


Tiere in der Unterhaltungsindustrie


6 Gründe, warum Wildparks nicht „besser“ als Zoos sind


Wildparks sind nicht besser für die Tiere als Zoos – auch hier leben sie ihr Leben lang in Gefangenschaft. Jetzt hier informieren!


Jetzt lesen


Update vom 10. August 2026 


Luchs entflieht aus dem Naturwildpark und wird von Jäger erschossen 


Nachdem Luchs Mikaesch Ende Juli 2026 aus seinem Gehege im Naturwildpark Granat entkommen war, wurde er am 8. August, rund zwei Wochen später, von einem

Jäger

 getötet. Berichten zufolge soll der Luchs den Hund eines Spaziergängers bedroht haben. Luchse gelten jedoch als sehr scheu und meiden Menschen in der Regel. Wie Mikaesch

aus seinem Gehege fliehen

 konnte, bleibt bislang unklar. 


Der Vorfall wirft erneut Fragen zur Haltung von Tieren im Naturwildpark Granat auf. Erst im März 2026 haben wir von PETA Deutschland Strafanzeige gegen den Betreiber wegen des Verdachts auf Vernachlässigung einiger Tiere erstattet. Die Haltung von Luchsen und anderen Tieren in Zoos und Wildparks muss endlich beendet werden. 


„Erst eingesperrt, dann ausgebrochen und schließlich erschossen: Mikaesch hat die Sehnsucht nach Freiheit mit dem Leben bezahlt. Immer wieder kommt es in Zoos zu Unfällen und Ausbrüchen, die für die Tiere tödlich enden können und auch Menschen und andere Tiere in Gefahr bringen. Kein noch so großes Gehege kann den natürlichen Bedürfnissen von Wildtieren gerecht werden. Wer verhindern will, dass die Gefangenschaft für weitere Tiere tödlich endet, muss aufhören, fühlende Lebewesen für die Schaulust von Menschen auszustellen.“ 

Dr. Yvonne Würz, Biologin und Fachreferentin bei PETA Deutschland 


Update vom 20. März 2026

 


Aktuelle Fotos deuten erneut auf Vernachlässigung hin 


Ende Februar 2026 erreichte uns bei PETA Deutschland eine Whistleblower-Meldung mit aktuellen Fotos, die ein Mufflon im Naturwildpark Granat mit überlang gewachsenen, sogenannten Schnabelhufen zeigen. Aufgrund von Fehlstellungen kann dies mit erheblichen Schmerzen für das Tier verbunden sein. Wir haben das Kreisveterinäramt Recklinghausen darüber verständigt und aufgefordert, die Tierhaltung umfassend zu überprüfen. 


Bereits im Herbst 2025 wurde uns und der Veterinärbehörde durch einen Augenzeugen von einer ähnlichen Beobachtung berichtet. Wenn Tiere möglicherweise über Monate hinweg mit schmerzhaft überlangen Hufen leben müssen, ist das ein klares

Zeichen für Vernachlässigung

. Daher werden wir nun erneut Strafanzeige …

author: Amy Goodman
title: Regulation Should Target AI’s Current Harms, Not Superintelligence Possibilities
content:
A mix of science fiction and delusion distracts from the real harms that we’re seeing, says tech journalist Paris Marx.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

We speak with tech journalist Paris Marx about his new book, Hyperscale: The Ambition and Excess of Big Tech’s Data Empires. In the book, Marx exposes the deceptive ways tech companies are taking resources from vulnerable communities in order to build massive AI data centers. “We have seen the tech companies that, back in 2019, 2020, wanted us to see them as climate leaders … completely throw their targets out the window in order to pursue generative AI and this data center buildout,” says Marx. He notes that after failing to connect to electrical grids in the locations where they were building data centers, some AI companies have pivoted to building “on-site gas plants,” further increasing dependency on fossil fuels.

Tech companies “want us to believe” that AI models are “starting to become so powerful that within 10 years they could decide that they want to wipe out humanity or a significant chunk of humanity,” says Marx. “That is a mix of science fiction and delusion … and it is also a very effective way to distract from the real harms that we’re seeing from these generative AI products.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now! I’m Amy Goodman, with Nermeen Shaikh.

NERMEEN SHAIKH: With the midterms less than three weeks away, we continue to look at how AI data centers have emerged as a political flashpoint.

AMY GOODMAN: We’re joined now by the Canadian journalist Paris Marx, host of the award-winning Tech Won’t Save Us podcast, writes the Disconnect newsletter, author of the new book Hyperscale: The Ambition and Excess of Big Tech’s Data Empires. He’s joining us from St. John’s, Newfoundland.

And we just talked to Justin Pearson, taking on Elon Musk’s xAI data centers in Memphis. In fact, though, the largest concentration of data centers is in northern Virginia, as you write about. And Nermeen and I are speaking to you from New York, which has the only state moratorium on the building of data centers. Can you give us — can you put that battle in Memphis in the global picture? Why northern Virginia, for example, is there this massive concentration of data centers? It’s not one of the poorest areas in the country.

PARIS MARX: No, certainly not. It’s much more for historical reasons, right? Because a lot of that early work on the internet was happening in northern Virginia, you know, obviously, a lot of military spending that went into that. And, of course, for that reason, a lot of infrastructure, a lot of, you know, fiber infrastructure, connectivity infrastructure, data centers, certainly, over time, were built out in that area. And that, you know, kind of — that legacy continues to this day.

And so, you know, the people who live there in northern Virginia have really felt the effects of all of these data centers having been built out. And especially, you know, they have had data centers for a long time — right? — but one of the things I try to get to in the book is really the shift from data centers as they used to be, you know, in industrial areas, maybe not so much larger than other tenants that would be in those, you know, kind of industrial parks and things like that, to the hyperscale data centers that are just on a whole other scale. You know, the resource demands are just immense, as, of course, you know, Representative Justin Pearson was just talking about in Memphis, where they have really been feeling this firsthand. And I think, you know, because Elon Musk was involved, this really brought it to the attention of a lot more people, seeing the effects that come with one of these major data centers. But, obviously, in northern Virginia, people are feeling a lot of that.

But as we have seen this significant escalation in the construction of these hyperscale data centers, particularly in the past four to five years, and certainly since the generative AI boom really started to take off in 2023, we have seen not just many more communities in the United States seeing data centers planned or being constructed next to them, and feeling, you know, what comes with that, whether that is the increases in their electricity prices, the pressures on their water system, or just, you know …

title: Court overturns environmental approval for Birsu hydroelectric power plant in Bingöl
content:
The Administrative Court in Bingöl has overturned the environmental approval for the planned Birsu hydroelectric power plant on the Sarim River. The judges unanimously ruled that the positive environmental impact assessment (EIA) decision was unlawful. The ruling was based on an expert report that identified significant scientific and technical deficiencies in the project’s assessment.


The hydroelectric power plant, planned by the company Silvan Elektrik Üretim, is to be built on the Sarim River in the border area between the districts of Lice and Kulp in Amed (Diyarbakır) and the district of Genç in Bingöl. Villagers have been challenging the project through legal channels for several years. They fear serious consequences for the region’s water resources, biodiversity, and agricultural livelihoods.


River flow and dry periods incorrectly assessed


According to the court, the deficiencies in calculating the available water volumes are particularly serious. The river flow data used in the project are not based on measurements taken within the affected river basin. Furthermore, the average river flow was overestimated, contradicting relevant scientific findings.


Accordingly, the pronounced dry periods between June and September were not adequately taken into account in the environmental impact assessment (EIA). As a result, there is no reliable basis for determining how much water could be diverted from the river by the operation of the power plant.


According to the experts, potential impacts on the groundwater system, as well as risks associated with geological faults and blasting operations, were also not examined using appropriate calculations and models. In addition, the region’s particular topographical conditions pose further challenges. Despite the steep slopes, the environmental impact assessment does not include adequate protective measures against landslides, erosion, and avalanches.


Habitat of rare fish species under threat


The Sarim River system is of particular ecological importance. The affected area is home to the Batman loach (

Paraschistura chrysicristina

), a fish species long believed to be extinct before it was rediscovered in the region. The protected Eurasian otter also inhabits the area. According to the experts, the minimum residual water flow planned for the operation of the power plant would be insufficient to preserve aquatic habitats, particularly during the dry summer months.


Furthermore, damage to forests and ground-level vegetation could harm regional beekeeping. Honey production is an important source of livelihood for the local population. The destruction of vegetation and nectar-producing areas could significantly undermine this source of income.


The expert report also criticizes the environmental impact assessment for failing to include a comprehensive examination of the cumulative impacts on the entire river basin. As a result, the combined effects of individual interventions were not adequately assessed. The court accepted the experts’ findings and ruled that the positive environmental decision was incompatible with both legal requirements and the public interest.


Years-long legal battle over the Birsu project


The latest ruling follows several years of legal proceedings. In January 2023, the Turkish Ministry of Environment initially decided that the project did not require a comprehensive environmental impact assessment. Villagers challenged this decision in court. In March 2024, the Administrative Court in Bingöl overturned a positive environmental decision. Following further appeals by the ministry and rulings by higher courts, the case was reviewed again.


In June 2026, another on-site inspection was conducted. The expert report submitted on August 11 concluded that the project was based on insufficient scientific evidence and should not be implemented in its proposed form. It had already emerged in June that the Turkish State Hydraulic Works (DSI) had terminated the water rights agreement for Birsu after the Energy Market Regulatory Authority (EPDK) revoked the project’s preliminary license because the company had failed to fulfill its obligations.


The Environmental and Urban Law Commission of the Diyarbakır Bar Association had described this as an important victory for the years-long resistance. With the latest ruling, the project’s environmental approval has now also been overturned by the court.

author: Bart Hawkins Kreps
title: Infrastructure, Finance, and the Sale of the Future
content:
Imagine yourself as a housing developer – an entrepreneur, a big-time player, a real deal-maker. Your people devise a plan to borrow money, buy land, design and win approval for a new subdivision, and sell 1,000 new housing units. Then, perhaps years before the houses are completed and decades before the initial mortgages are repaid, you sell your shares in the venture for a tidy profit. A neat trick, this, cashing in today on bills that others will pay long into the future.

You have become wealthier, but have you been a “wealth creator”? For that matter, are you contributing to “economic growth”? Where does the money come from for this venture: is it capital accumulated from the past, or is this money newly created the moment credit is extended by banks and off-setting debts are recorded on balance sheets?

These are among the many questions addressed by Timothy Mitchell in his new book The Alibi of Capital, out on March 10 from Verso.

Mitchell works his way through a profound rewriting of economic history and economic theory. He wants us to think carefully about who pays for what is labelled “economic growth.” Is the earning of interest some natural property of money? Why was the phrase “the economy” almost never used until the mid-20th century, while today the economy is routinely invoked as the determinant of what is politically, socially, or environmentally acceptable? Why do banks continue to invest in new fossil fuel infrastructures, in full public knowledge that these infrastructures are robbing future generations of a stable climate?

Let’s begin with a simpler question: is “financialization” an adequate term for the process by which a housing developer turns still-unbuilt houses into immediate profit? Mitchell doesn’t think so. While the creation and swapping of financial instruments is one essential part of the process, two others are equally essential. First, the process depends on the manufacture of long-lasting infrastructure. Second and equally important, there must be a legal and political framework that ensures holders of the financial instruments can enforce their claims to ongoing revenues five, ten, or even fifty years in the future.

What is often termed financialization, Mitchell, argues is really a technopolitical “apparatus of capture.”1 Mitchell writes:

“The apparatus is neither fully public nor private but combines aspects of both; is made up of both materials and ideas; deploys both law and violence; and depends upon both careful calculation and the imaginative construction of prospective worlds.” (The Alibi of Capital, page 30)

The use of an “apparatus of capture” to secure present profits from future events did not begin recently. Mitchell traces the process back hundreds of years to early joint-stock companies engaged in long-distance commerce.

Shipowners typically required credit to finance long voyages in which revenue from the sale of products would only come many months later. The letters of credit, which were also “letters of debt plus interest,” were sometimes traded, with the seller accepting a discount so that they could be paid immediately, while the buyer would receive the principal plus interest perhaps a year or more later.

The infrastructure was not very durable – ships often sank – and the time frames were short, just a few months to perhaps a couple of years. This commerce didn’t provide much scope for capturing revenue from the future. That changed in the nineteenth century with the development of railroads, which Mitchell describes as a turning point.

Railroads were large-scale durable infrastructures – and required major investment up-front. Once built they offered the promise of revenues coming in for decades. They were often built as colonial enterprises, requiring imposition of governance and military/police power to protect that revenue. The prospect of strikes also grew in importance, as workers increasingly organized against dangerous conditions, long hours, and inadequate wages; the realization of future profits required the suppression of organized labour power.

If the technical and the political factors were aligned, however, the issuance of the credit/debt associated with new railroads gave financial markets a way to buy and sell the future, earning profits immediately on services which workers would provide and customers would pay for decades later.

Railroads were followed by many other large-scale and durable infrastructures: bridges, wharves …

content:

Huang’a a’ka, pang’a’anang naka pang’a’u yu, huang’a a’taka, a’anatirma, naka kirstinuga pás, huang’a sivunga rumi. I come from St. Lawrence Island. I’ve been with IEN since 2021, and I work on organizing against climate geoengineering.

Kweyanaipaplusi maunga, huang’a a’akaluk, ungelaksirmiu runga, angayukang maktaklu Charlie. I a’anukwa’apu’a makigaklu anaktiyuk asii, janililu Charlie, chinirmiu, ungelaksirmiu. Thank you everyone for welcoming us here today.

I’m Adrienne A’akaluk Blatchford. I’m from Unalakleet, Alaska, which is up on the Northwest Coast in the passageway to the Arctic. We’re right on the coast of the Bering Sea in the heart of the Norton Sound.

And I work with Indigenous Environmental Network as a geoengineering outreach organizer with a focus on Alaska and the Arctic. Hello, thank you for having us as the host.

My name is Thomas Joseph. I’m a Hoopa Valley tribal member from the Six Rivers National Forest in Northern California. I am also Shoshone Paiute from the Sierra Nevadas. Paiute is what we call it, the land of flowing water.

I’m down there by Yosemite and the Half Dome area. I am here with the Indigenous Environmental Network as their carbon pricing educator. And again, thanks for having us.

Yá’át’ééh. My name is Talia Boyd. Older women from my community who love to have the time of their lives shared with me.

Greetings, everyone. My name is Talia Boyd. I’m the mining organizer for IEN.

I’m based in New Mexico, originally from Arizona, and I hail from the Navajo Nation in the Southwest. And I’m very honored to be here with y’all and share this space and time. Thank you.

Awesome. And a little bit about me for any of you who don’t know me. My name is Isla.

I’m originally from Wales and I’ve been living here in Iceland for over five years and I’m the education representative for the Icelandic Young Environmentalists. So how about we just go straight into things and you guys can give us a little bit of an oral presentation about your work and everything that you do and then we’ll get started with the panel Q&A afterwards. Sounds good.

Thank you. So I want to kind of do a little bit of an introduction on who is the Indigenous Environmental Network. Over 30 years ago the United States, we’re kind of seeing that return back to that, was having a really hard time addressing the mining operations of uranium in the southwest and the Indigenous people came together as they were the ones that were being directly affected by these mining operations that was being used for the production of uranium for the purpose of war.

And so the Indigenous peoples from that region rallied together to try to protect their communities against the high rates of cancers and other issues that was plaguing their communities to no avail. The state governments wouldn’t listen to them. The national governments wouldn’t listen to them and so they seen that it was in their best interest to take this fight to the international space of the United Nations and that’s when the Indigenous Environmental Network was formed with the purpose and intent of taking the struggles of the mining and the struggles of the health impacts of mining to a global positioning.

The Indigenous Environmental Network has been active in the United Nations space since then and in various different causes pertaining to the Paris Climate Agreement, water issues, mining issues, also very active in the Convention on Biological Diversity and we continue to play a role of Indigenous networks across Turtle Island. So we come from impacted communities of Indigenous peoples. Frontline community is another term that’s often used from across Turtle Island of communities that are faced with deforestation, faced with dams, faced with any type of harm that we see against our Mother Earth.

In these past 30 years IEN has now expanded its network to be globally and so we have Indigenous organizations that we work with across the globe and in North America we have a strong positioning on mining operations which is Talia Leeds and geoengineering and carbon pricing which I do but we also do a lot of other work pertaining to just transition and many other things that you can find on our website at IENEarth.org. Thank …

author: Kay Pacha / Equipo Pueblos Originarios del SERPAJ
title: Lecko Zamora: una voz Wichí por el 12 de octubre
content:
Y llegamos una vez más al 12 de octubre, fecha muy simbólica y oportuna para hacer recordar que significó y significa para los pueblos originarios, que fue el comienzo de una invasión, un genocidio y un sistema colonizante en todo sentido.


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/12-de-octubre.mp3


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/12-de-octubre.mp3


Descargar archivo


Pero ahora, a pesar que se quiera volver al Día de la Raza, los hermanos y hermanas aprovechan la oportunidad para hace oír sus voces, sus reclamos y en general denunciar la situación de racismo, violencia y despojo territorial que vienen sufriendo.


Por eso en esta oportunidad han tenido lugar a lo largo y ancho de nuestro país, numerosos actos, movilizaciones  y marchas en donde se manifestaron las denuncias y reclamos por estas situaciones.


Uno de los reclamos urgentes en estos momentos es el cese de los desalojos de comunidades de diversos pueblos y territorios. Todos los documentos que se conocieron por estos días difunden ampliamente la difícil situación que están atravesando varias comunidades, como ser la Lof Melo en la Provincia de Neuquén.


Afortunadamente la existencia de estas movilizaciones revela el espíritu de resistencia y lucha de las comunidades, que utilizan todas las herramientas necesarias en su defensa y contra un aparato jurídico y represivo que  responde a los intereses de quienes ambicionan sus territorios para sus ambiciones de lucro y de explotación de sus bienes naturales.


Todas estas situaciones denunciadas son bien conocidas y siempre las difundimos, pero en esta oportunidad queremos compartirle algo diferente, algo que si bien es una denuncia en general, está hecha con una hermosa y poética presentación.


Presentamos la voz de Lecko Zamora, escritor, artista, gestor cultural y referente de la cultura wichí, quien expresa en forma muy personal lo que todos venimos denunciando sobre el 12 de octubre.


El Micro Kay Pacha se realiza con el apoyo de la organización Otto per Mille-Chiessa Valdense.
