author: Kodao Productions
title: Alex Cabrera unmasks Sara
content:
Lawyer Alexander “Alex” Cabrera, whom the Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio defense panel wanted to be banned from the witness stand of the Senate impeachment court, delivered what amounts to a

coup de grace

, delivering a forensic financial analysis that shot down the daily pablum of the defense that the mountain of evidence culled by the prosecution was fabricated, including the ones admitted by the defense and never controverted in the course of the trial.


Cabrera, a certified public accountant (CPA) from the Philippine School of Business Administration (PSBA) who later took his law degree from the Ateneo de Manila University (AdMU), undertook a systematic assessment of the tax filings, Statements of Assets and Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs), corporate documents from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), documents from the Anti-Money laundering Council (AMLC) and 30 bank accounts in eight banks, including joint accounts with the detained ex—president Rodrigo Duterte and Sara’s joint accounts with her husband, Manases Carpio.


Despite being notified by the prosecution that it would present Cabrera, the defense still objected, arguing that the forensic was not supposed to take the stand that day. The trial court brushed aside the defense’s protest. At the outset, the Sara lawyers may have known the record of Cabrera, former chairman of a big accounting firm and who had analyzed thousands of corporate records, tax filings and passed judgment on dubious documents covering inward remittances, contested checks and financial statements in 37 years. He certainly was known to Sara since she signed an agreement with Cabrera’s company to assess the Davao City Investment Code. This was probably the reason why the defense got goose bumps upon learning that Cabrera was going to present his forensic analysis.


The defense ended up less than *“maisug” when Cabrera took the witness stand. As a lawyer, he was bound by the Code of Professional Responsibility and Accountability (CPRA) with its 37 Canons. As an accountant, he was bound by the Code of Ethics for Professional Accountants in the Philippines (CEPAP) and international standards. Most of all, he was bound by the rules and regulations of the Alpha Phi Omega fraternity. All told, Cabrera was answerable to two professional organizations and his fraternity and the people at large who have been monitoring the conduct of the impeachment trial and weighing the evidence proffered to convict Sara. His role was to show vividly why Sara is being made to answer allegations of ill-gotten wealth.


Given the mishmash of weak defenses advanced by the 16 defense lawyers, from the illegal disbursements of “confidential funds” that Sara sourced from the Contingent Fund of the Palace, for which she was accountable, as argued by former Executive Secretary Lucas Bersamin, it was inevitable that Cabrera would find the rot in the paper trail, in the bundles of documents he had examined, the financial statements he had assessed, and the discrepancies in tax filings, SALNs and bank papers from 2007 to 2025.


Sara did not prepare to be confronted by an expert witness like Alex Cabrera and neither did she believe that she would be slapped with impeachment charges after throwing the kitchen sink at President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. All along, Sara and her handlers, perhaps with foreign advisers in tow, never for a moment thought that a weak leader would make launch a counteroffensive rather than throw in the towel. Call it megalothymia, or the idea that she is superior to the rest of mankind, that provided her with the delusion that she is immune from suit, from impeachment and from being kicked out from her perch. This megalothymia is the reason why she thinks appearing before the Senate impeachment court is beneath her dignity.


So, Alex Cabrera ruled the day. He discovered assets that were never included in Sara’s SALNs, saw the tax returns (ITRs) that did not include the money that flowed through her gravy train. Upon questioning by Rep. Chel Diokno, Cabrera stressed that the financial lacunae would eventually be filled up by comparing data, rechecking bank accounts, the P96-million in manager’s checks that secreted away the money in the joint Sara-Digong accounts, and corporate earnings hidden in Cale88 Foods, Metro City and GenCorp. For 2022, Cabrera said there was ₱60.21 million in undeclared cash, ₱80.70 million the following year, ₱23.17 million in 2024 and ₱43.61 million in 2025 …

author: Andrew Crocker
title: We’re Asking the Wisconsin Supreme Court to End Warrantless ALPR Searches
content:
Today, EFF joined the ACLU of Wisconsin in filing a

petition

 to the Wisconsin Supreme Court, asking it to rule that the state’s constitution requires a warrant for retrospective searches of ALPR databases used by law enforcement in four cities: Milwaukee, Racine, Kenosha, and Green Bay. We represent a religious organization, the Wisconsin Council of Churches, as well as an individual pastor in Green Bay.


As the petition explains:


Right now, Automated License Plate Readers (“ALPRs”) are recording the movements of vast numbers of Wisconsin drivers as they seek medical care, attend 12-step recovery meetings, attend religious services, participate in protests, attend political meetings, and engage in many other private, sensitive activities. Law enforcement entities throughout Wisconsin collect, store, share, and aggregate this ALPR data. Then they search it, retrospectively tracking the movements of individuals and entire communities in ways that would have been prohibitively costly, if not outright impossible, before the advent of ALPR technology.


We all deserve to be free of warrantless mass surveillance. We all deserve to live in a country where surveillance vendors cannot help police upend our system of individualized suspicion. Religious organizations and officials like our clients have a heightened interest in protecting their location privacy because of the range of expressive associations their work entails, including facilitating gatherings for religious worship, as well as offering pastoral care, confidential counseling, and community support. Likewise, the people who visit houses of worship have a strong right to privacy against police monitoring of when they pray, seek addiction counseling, or attend a domestic violence survivor meeting.


This is our second lawsuit challenging warrantless ALPR searches, following

SIREN v. San Jose.

 Earlier this month, a federal court in Oklahoma became the first to

rule

 that ALPRs are a “type of indiscriminate mass surveillance” and suppress evidence from a warrantless ALPR search. We hope the Wisconsin Supreme Court will agree.


Read the Wisconsin Supreme Court

petition


Read the

press release


Related Cases: 

Wisconsin Council of Churches v. Milwaukee, Racine, Kenosha & Green Bay

author: Ethieny Karen
title: Um quarto dos senadores que apoiam a PEC da Flexibilidade têm antepassados escravocratas
content:
A proposta que defende o fim da escala 6×1 sempre teve um contraponto: o argumento de que o trabalhador deva receber por horas trabalhadas e possa “negociar” diretamente com o patrão sobre como será sua jornada de trabalho.


Essa é a proposta central da chamada PEC da Flexibilidade, que foi apresentada pelo senador e coordenador de campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro à Presidência, Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), como uma alternativa ao fim da escala 6×1. Segundo o líder do PL na Câmara dos Deputados, Sóstenes Cavalcante (RJ), essa é a proposta que o candidato à presidência, Flávio Bolsonaro, deve defender mesmo se a PEC do fim da escala 6×1 for aprovada. “Na nossa mentalidade, nós nunca vamos mudar o conceito, a melhor relação é hora trabalhada, hora recebida”,

disse

 Sóstenes ao G1.


Críticos à PEC da Flexibilidade – entre eles, a própria deputada federal Érika Hilton, autora da proposta mais recente que defende o fim da escala 6×1 (

PEC 8/2025

) –

chamaram

 o projeto de “escravidão moderna” e “PEC da escravidão”.


A

Agência Pública

 apurou que dos

40 senadores

 favoráveis à PEC da flexibilização em maio, ao menos 10 têm antepassados diretos que foram donos de pessoas escravizadas ou se beneficiaram da escravidão. A proposta que flexibiliza a jornada de trabalho, bem como os salários,

está parada

 no Senado, mas sua tramitação pode ser retomada caso Flávio seja eleito.


Esse é o

caso

 dos antepassados do senador Rogério Marinho, mais especificamente do seu sétimo avô, o Capitão-mor Bento Freire, que viveu no Rio Grande do Norte entre 1727 e 1803. Segundo documentos analisados pela

Pública

, o capitão foi senhor de engenho e um rico proprietário de terras, e teria utilizado mão de obra de pessoas escravizadas.


A reportagem procurou o político para esclarecer os achados sobre sua árvore genealógica e a relação do antepassado com a escravidão, assim como fizemos com todas as autoridades citadas no

Projeto Escravizadores

, publicado em novembro de 2024. O senador não respondeu até a publicação do especial.


Já o senador Jayme Campos, que faz parte de uma das famílias mais poderosas e tradicionais na política mato-grossense. Tem como quinto avô Antonio José Pinto de Figueiredo, que foi um mestre de campo (patente militar da época, que hoje corresponde a posição de coronel), em Cuiabá.


E, segundo documentos, ele era dono de uma grande fazenda, composta de 83 escravos.


Em 2008, mais de dois séculos depois, 15 trabalhadores relataram condições degradantes de trabalho na fazenda Santa Amália, em Alta Floresta (MT), pertencente a Jayme Campos. Após as denúncias, o senador assinou um Termo de Ajustamento de Conduta com o Ministério Público do Trabalho na época para assinar a carteira de trabalho dos funcionários, garantir alojamento adequado, oferecer água potável e permitir descanso remunerado, entre outros.


Campos negou as irregularidades, disse que sofria perseguição política e que aceitou assinar o TAC porque “não tinha nada a temer”. Nós procuramos o político na época da publicação do

especial

, mas ele não respondeu.


A história se repete com outros nove senadores, veja a lista:


Efraim Filho (UNIÃO-PB)


O senador tem como tataravô Manoel De Araújo Pereira II. Registros indicam que ele teria possuído pessoas escravizadas em Santa Luzia, Paraíba, entre os anos de 1858 e 1888.


Tereza Cristina (PP-MS)


O tataravô da senadora foi Antonio Côrrea da Costa I, nascido em 1782 e falecido em 1854, no Mato Grosso. Segundo registros, ele herdou de seu pai o engenho Bom Jardim e, posteriormente, em 1805, adquiriu o engenho da Glória. Em 1821, tornou-se o segundo presidente da Província de Mato Grosso e, posteriormente, deputado. Em seus engenhos, produzia milho, arroz, feijão, açúcar e aguardente. Ele também teria possuído 8 mil cabeças de gado, 10 casas em Cuiabá e 194 pessoas escravizadas.


Marcos Pontes (PL-SP)


O sexto avô do senador foi o alferes Joaquim da Silveira Leite, nascido em 1758 no interior do estado de São Paulo e falecido em 1823. Oficial subalterno do corpo de milícias, ele era senhor de engenho, dedicando-se à produção de açúcar e aguardente. Segundo registros, o alferes teria possuído cerca de 10 pessoas escravizadas.


Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI)


O senador tem como tataravô o ex-presidente da província do Piauí por quatro mandatos, Simplício de Sousa Mendes, nascido em 1823 e falecido em 1892, e como quinto avô o tenente-coronel Antônio de Sousa Mendes, nascido em 1793 e falecido em 1871 …

author: Unknown
title: Ephéméride des luttes : 15 octobre
content:
Le 15 octobre de l'éphéméride des luttes est le genre de journée où nos mort-e-s passé-e-s continuent à vivre dans les flammes des révoltes d'aujourd'hui et de celles à venir.


1840 :

 A Paris, l'ouvrier Marius Darmès, proche des idées de ce qui deviendra l'anarchisme, tire au pistolet sur la voiture du roi Louis-Philippe sur le quai des Tuileries, mais le pistolet lui explose dans la main, sauvant la vie du roi. Darmès sera condamné à mort le

29 mai

 de l'année suivante.


1920 :

 A Milan, la police perquisitionne les locaux du journal anarchiste L'Umanità Nova et arrête les personnes présentes.


1940 :

 En Espagne, le président républicain de Catalogne Lluís Companys est exécuté par Franco et son régime fasciste.


1965 :

 Aux USA, la première carte d'appel pour le service militaire est brûlée en public, ce qui donnera lieu à un grand mouvement antimilitariste.


1966 :

 Aux États-Unis, première parution du

programme en 10 points

 du Black Panther Party.


1971 :

 A Belfast, l'IRA abat deux membres des troupes armées Irlandaises loyales à la couronne d'Angleterre et qui collabore avec son armée d'occupation.


1974 :

 En Irlande du Nord, une révolte a lieu dans la prison de Maze, où des prisonniers de l'IRA incendient plusieurs cellules.


1977 :

 A Lucca en Toscane, le groupe 'Lutte Armée pour le Communisme' fait sauter des explosifs contre le palais de justice de la ville.


1979 :

 En Irlande du Nord, un sondage révèle que près de 22% des Irlandais-es soutiennent l'action de l'IRA (ce qui est deux fois plus élevé que le taux d'approbation porté en ce moment à François Hollande ou Manuel Valls).


1981 :

 Au Salvador, la guérilla du FMLN fait sauter le pont Puente de Oro.


1984 :

 A Ixelles, près de Bruxelles, les Cellules Communistes Combattantes (CCC) font sauter la Fondation Internationale Jean Rey / Centre Paul Hymans. Il s'agit de l'institut de recherche politique et idéologique de l'Internationale Libérale (dont le Centre Paul Hymans est la section belge). Lire le communiqué conjoint avec leur action deux jours plus tard

ici

.


1987 :

 Au Burkina Faso, assassinat de Thomas Sankara, qui avait donné un nouveau souffle au pays en prenant toute une série de mesure économiques et politiques socialistes et très largement dirigées vers les classes les plus populaires du pays.


2005 :

 A Toledo, en Ohio, des antifascistes (composés en grande partie des anarchistes et des militant-e-s antiracistes locaux) organisent une contre-réunion contre un rassemblement néonazi. Cette situation débouche sur quatre heures d'affrontements entre les antifascistes et la police, qui arrêtent plusieurs douzaines de personnes. Un bar de policiers est incendié.


2008 :

 En Val Susa en Italie, plus de 400 pneus sont incendiés, provoquant le blocage de l'autoroute pour plus de trois heures.


2011 :

 A Rome, grande journée d'affrontements au cours de la 'journée mondiale des indignés'. Une annexe du ministère de l'Intérieur, des voitures de luxe et une fourgonnette de police sont incendiées ('Carlo Vive') et des banques et agences d'intérim attaquées sur tout le parcours.


2016 :

 Près de Des Moines dans l'Iowa, une pelleteuse et trois bulldozers

sont incendiés

 pour protester contre la construction du pipeline du Dakota Access, faisant 2 millions de dollars de dégâts. L'entreprise offre 100.000$ à qui balancera les auteurs de l'attaque. Espérons que ça n'arrive jamais.


2018 :

 A Besançon, huit véhicules d'Enedis (ex-Edf), qui promeut largement le développement de l'industrie nucléaire,

sont incendiés

 en pleine rue.


Voir

l'éphéméride anarchiste

 du 15 octobre.

title: Kurdish Conference at European Parliament Begins with reception: Abdullah Öcalan must be released
content:
The 20th conference, organized by the European Union Turkey Civic Commission (EUTCC) and patronized by Nobel Peace Prize laureate and Iranian human rights advocate Shirin Ebadi, human rights activist Bianca Jagger, and Kurdish politician Leyla Zana, recipient of the European Parliament’s Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought, began with a reception.


The reception, held at the European Parliament on the evening of 14 October, was attended by numerous people, including Pervin Buldan, a member of the Imralı Delegation; European parliamentarians such as Shirin Ebadi, Martin Schirdewan, Andreas Schieder, and Leoluca Orlando; politicians and activists such as Hisyar Özsoy and Sebahat Tuncel; and lawyer Raziye Öztürk of the Asrın Law Office, representing the legal community. The conference will continue tomorrow, 15 October.


The 20th conference marks a turning point


Opening the reception, Dersim Dağdeviren, a member of the EUTCC Board and affiliated with Kurd-Akad, said the 20th conference marked a turning point for the EUTCC. “At the same time, it is an opportunity to pause and ask ourselves: What have we achieved? What have we failed to accomplish? And, most importantly, what responsibility do we bear for the future?” he said.


Noting that the EUTCC had spent two decades providing a space for critical dialogue on relations between the European Union and Türkiye, the Kurdish question, democracy, human rights, and the pursuit of peace, Dersim Dağdeviren said: “There is a motto that captures our collective work in a special way: When one person dreams, it is only a dream. When many people dream together, it is the beginning of a new reality.”


International support is necessary for the process to succeed


Dersim Dağdeviren said that this reality was reflected in the 20-year history of EUTCC conferences held at the European Parliament. He then drew attention to the ongoing Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey.


Describing it as an important opportunity to resolve the Kurdish question on a political basis, Dersim Dağdeviren said: “A successful process cannot be sustained solely through the efforts of the parties directly involved. It also requires sustained international support. The European Union and its member states must actively support dialogue, encourage talks between the parties, and create the political conditions necessary for a lasting, democratic solution.”


Shirin Ebadi: Abdullah Öcalan must be released


Nobel laureate and lawyer Shirin Ebadi then addressed the gathering in Persian, greeting Öcalan and stating: “Abdullah Öcalan has shown the courage necessary for peace and must be released. I demand the immediate and unconditional release of Abdullah Öcalan.”


Adding that “the courage Abdullah Öcalan has demonstrated shows that he deserves to be one of the pioneers of the peace process,” Shirin Ebadi continued: “In my view, the time has now come for him to be freed. I see this platform as an opportunity to call for Abdullah Öcalan’s release without any preconditions.


The Kurds have the capacity to pursue their struggle through a political party in Turkey and to continue fighting for democracy and their legitimate rights. They can secure their rights within Turkey’s borders through democratic politics. Believe me, this is the path that will enable you to achieve your goals more effectively. My wish is for all ethnic groups in Turkey and elsewhere in the world, including Iran, to enjoy human rights and the right to live as equals, free from discrimination.”


Schirdewan said Europe must address two issues, Palestine and Kurdistan


Martin Schirdewan, a Member of the European Parliament and Co-Chair of The Left group, said: “As European lawmakers, we can develop a better understanding of what is needed to achieve lasting peace in Kurdistan and the Middle East.”


The co-chair of The Left added: “We also believe there are two fundamental issues that European politicians need to address. First, there is the issue of Palestine. We need to discuss a Palestinian state and the right of the Palestinian people to statehood. Second, there is the issue of the Kurds’ national status and their right to determine their own future.


Ultimately, it is up to you to decide what you want. What we can do, and what we can offer you, is support in building a society founded on democracy and equality. You must make the decision, not someone else. No one who oppresses the Kurdish people should make that decision …

title: ABD'de yargıç, Trump yönetiminin Washington'daki golf sahasında yaptığı ağaç kesimini durdurdu
content:
ABD Bölge Yargıcı Ana C. Reyes, daha önce geçici tedbir kararı aldığı, başkent Washington D.C.'de Donald Trump yönetimi tarafından yaptırılan bir golf sahasındaki ağaç kesimini 26 Ekim'e kadar durdurdu.

Yargıç Reyes, "East Potomac Golf Links" isimli golf sahasındaki ağaçların bu kadar hızlı kesilmesinin, Trump yönetiminin konuyu bir "oldu bittiye getirmek" istemesinden kaynaklandığını söyledi.

Konuyla ilgili 21 sayfalık rapor hazırlayan Reyes, salı günü verdiği geçici tedbir kararını resmileştirerek, güzergahı kalıcı olarak değiştirecek herhangi bir çalışma için "72 saat önceden bildirimde bulunulmasını" şart koştu.

Reyes, Trump yönetimini, tarihi golf sahasında çalışma yapılmaması yönündeki tekrarlanan taleplerini görmezden geldiği için sert bir dille eleştirerek, "Bunun hiçbir bahanesi yok" dedi.

Yargıç, hükümet avukatlarına, bu konuda "cehaletin mazeret olarak kabul edilemeyeceğini" ifade etti.

Kadın yargıç, daha önceki bir duruşmada söz konusu sahada, "önceden haber verilmeksizin 10 ağacın bile kesilemeyeceğine" dair yaptığı uyarıyı hatırlattı.

Yönetimin avukatları ise duruşmada, hafta sonu yaklaşık 430 ağacın kesildiğini ve 299 ağacın daha kesilmesinin hedeflendiğini aktardı.

Duruşma, halka açık golf sahasında yeni ağaç kesimi yapılmasını istemeyen sivil toplum kuruluşlarının pazar günü geç saatlerde yaptığı acil bir başvurunun ardından gerçekleşti.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: İBB: İstanbul'da yağış, 1985'ten bu yana kaydedilen en yüksek değerlerden birine ulaştı
content:
İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyesi (İBB), 14 Ekim günündeki yağışlarda 1985 yılından bu yana kaydedilen en yüksek değerlerden birine ulaşıldığını belirterek, kentin bazı noktalarında metrekareye 242 kilogram yağış düştüğünü bildirdi.

İBB'den yapılan açıklamaya göre Beykoz'da metrekareye 242 kilogram, Eyüpsultan'da 190,5 kilogram, Sarıyer'de ise 187,9 kilogram yağış düştü.

Özellikle Boğaz çevresi ile Avrupa Yakası'nın kuzey ve orta kesimlerinde metrekareye düşen yağış miktarı 100 ila 230 kilogram olarak ölçüldü.

İstanbul'un birçok noktasında metrekareye düşen yağış miktarı ise 100 kilogramı aştı.

Kaydedilen yağış miktarı, 1985 yılından bu yana görülen en yüksek değerlerden birine ulaştı.

Yağış nedeniyle İBB birimlerine toplam 6 bin 937 ihbar ulaştı. İhbarların 5 bin 711'i İSKİ'ye, 528'i Çözüm Merkezi'ne, 498'i itfaiyeye, 200'ü ise yol bakım ekiplerine iletildi.

AKOM'un meteorolojik değerlendirmelerine göre, yağışların özellikle Anadolu Yakası ve Boğaz çevresinde etkisini sürdürmesi bekleniyor. Bugün sabah saat 10.00'a kadar bazı bölgelerde metrekareye 50 ila 75 kilogram ilave yağış düşebileceği, rüzgarın ise saatte 50 ila 80 kilometre hıza ulaşabileceği tahmin ediliyor.

Vatandaşlara zorunlu olmadıkça özel araçlarıyla trafiğe çıkmamaları, mümkün olduğunca toplu ulaşımı tercih etmeleri, dere yataklarından ve su baskını riski bulunan alanlardan uzak durmaları çağrısında bulunuldu.

İBB, olumsuz hava koşulları nedeniyle vatandaşların güvenli alanlarda dinlenebilmesi için tüm sosyal tesislerini sabaha kadar açık tutacak. BELTUR'un 6 noktası da gece boyunca hizmet verecek. Vatandaşların ulaşımını kolaylaştırmak amacıyla 15 raylı sistem hattında seferler saat 02.00'ye kadar uzatıldı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Rizomatica
title: Mogekonmen regresa en Kurarewe: tres días para encontrarse con la gastronomía Mapuche y los saberes territoriales que la sostienen
content:
El 30 y 31 de octubre y 1 de noviembre de 2026 se realizará la 2° versión del Festival de Gastronomía Mapuche MOGEKONMEN, un encuentro que reunirá a cocineras, cocineros, recolectoras, huerteras, cultores e invitados de distintos territorios para compartir experiencias en torno a la alimentación, la cultura y la memoria mapuche.


Después de su primera versión en 2025, el Festival de Gastronomía Mapuche se prepara para recibir nuevamente a quienes quieran conocer, compartir y disfrutar de una cocina profundamente vinculada con el territorio y sus formas de vida.


Durante tres jornadas (viernes, sábado y domingo), Kurarewe será escenario de un encuentro que busca ir más allá de las preparaciones y los sabores. MOGEKONMEN propone conocer las historias que existen detrás de los alimentos: cómo se cultivan, dónde se recolectan, quiénes conservan las semillas y de qué manera estos conocimientos continúan transmitiéndose entre generaciones.


El festival es autogestionado y surge del trabajo que cocineras y cocineros de Kurarewe que realizan durante todo el año. Detrás de estos tres días hay meses de organización, encuentros y esfuerzos compartidos, sostenidos por el compromiso de quienes creen en la importancia de mantener vivos los conocimientos alimentarios de su territorio.


Una cocina que comienza mucho antes de llegar a la mesa


En los territorios mapuche cordilleranos, muchos conocimientos alimentarios se mantienen a través de prácticas cotidianas: el trabajo en las huertas, la recolección de hongos y frutos, el cuidado de las semillas, la preparación de alimentos de temporada y el aprendizaje junto a las personas mayores.


 Estas experiencias forman parte de lo que MOGEKONMEN busca compartir con sus visitantes, reconociendo que la cocina no comienza cuando se enciende el fuego, sino mucho antes, en la relación que las personas mantienen con la naturaleza y su territorio.


Tres jornadas de cocina, conversación y encuentro


La segunda versión de MOGEKONMEN contempla actividades que permitirán acercarse a la gastronomía mapuche desde diferentes experiencias: seminario interdisciplinario de saberes, encuentro con personas dedicadas al resguardo y transmisión de conocimientos alimentarios, cocina en vivo, una feria gastronómica y artesanal de productores y productoras locales, música, cine indígena, astroturismo y espacio dedicado especialmente para niños y niñas.


En esta segunda versión nos encontraremos con destacadas cocineras y chef de los pueblos aymara, huilliche, lafkenche y también desde Perú. Todos ellos compartirán sus experiencias desde la cocina, la investigación y el trabajo desarrollado en sus respectivas zonas.


Junto con acercar estos conocimientos al público, MOGEKONMEN busca contribuir al fortalecimiento de la economía local y dar visibilidad al trabajo de cocineras, recolectoras, huerteras, productores y artesanos que forman parte de la vida del territorio de Kurarewe, actual Región de la Araucanía.


Kurarewe vuelve a abrir su despensa al mundo

.


Este año, el festival vuelve a abrir sus puertas para compartir preparaciones, escuchar historias y conocer a las personas y territorios que hacen posible esta cocina.


MOGEKONMEN es también un escenario para hablar de las implicancias de las nuevas políticas y decisiones sobre el uso de los territorios. Queremos hablar sobre el rol fundamental de las mujeres en la transmisión de conocimientos en los pueblos originarios, el futuro de los bosques, las aguas y la biodiversidad, creemos necesario escuchar a quienes han convivido y cuidado estos espacios por generaciones. Porque hablar de nuestros alimentos también es hablar de los lugares que permiten que sigan existiendo.


Esta segunda versión cuenta con el apoyo del área Küme Mogen (vivir bien y en armonía) de la iniciativa Füta Mawiza, cuyo trabajo busca contribuir al resguardo del territorio y fortalecer la gobernanza local para proteger las formas de vida y la naturaleza de las cabeceras de cuenca.


El 2° Festival de Gastronomía Mapuche MOGEKONMEN se realizará los días viernes 30 y sábado 31 de octubre y domingo 1 de noviembre de 2026, en Kurarewe, a aproximadamente 140 kilómetros de Temuco, hacia la cordillera.


La programación completa y otras novedades estarán disponibles en las redes sociales oficiales del festival.


Esta información se publicó en

Radio Kurruf

.

author: Unknown
title: İzmir Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri’nden Halk TV’ye destek: “Haber alma özgürlüğü engellendi"
content:
İzmir – İzmir Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri, Halk TV’ye kayyım atanmasına tepki göstermek için basın açıklaması düzenledi. Alsancak Türkan Saylan Kültür Merkezi önünde düzenlenen açıklamada sık sık “Karanlığa teslim olmayacağız”, “Özgür basın susturulamaz”, “AKP gidecek, biz kalacağız” sloganları atıldı. Basın metnini KESK İzmir Dönem Sözcüsü Savaş Candemir okudu.

AKP iktidarının sürdürdüğü baskı ve sindirme politikalarını yaşamın her alanına yaymaya devam ettiğini belirten Candemir, “Belediyelerden demokratik kurumlara, dijital mecralardan muhalif basına uzanan kayyım, sansür ve yasak politikalarının son hedefi Halk TV oldu” dedi.

Halk TV’ye yönelik polis operasyonunun, kanala kayyım atanmasının ve yayınların durdurulmasının yalnızca bir televizyon kanalına yönelik müdahale olarak değerlendirilemeyeceğini vurgulayan Candemir, “Bu uygulama, basın özgürlüğü, halkın haber alma hakkı ve demokratik toplumun temel değerleri açısından son derece ciddi bir gelişmedir. Bunun bir başka örneğini TELE 1’de de yaşadık. TELE 1’e sadece kayyım atanmamış, adeta TELE 1 yok edilerek haber kanalı belgesel ve magazin kanalına dönüştürülmüş, halkın haber alma özgürlüğü engellenmiştir” diye konuştu.

Bugün Halk TV’ye yönelik müdahalenin, ülkemizde uzun süredir yaşanan demokratik gerilemeden, seçilmiş iradelere yönelik kayyım uygulamalarından, gazetecilere dönük baskılardan ve toplumsal muhalefetin sesini sınırlayan politikalardan bağımsız değerlendirilemeyeceğini söyleyen Candemir, “Bu saldırılar birbirinden bağımsız değil; tek merkezden yürütülen, toplumsal muhalefeti susturmayı, halkın iradesini gasp etmeyi ve haber alma hakkını ortadan kaldırmayı, demokrasinin asgari kurum ve kurallarını ortadan kaldırarak otoriter tek adam rejimini kalıcı hâle getirmeyi hedefleyen politikanın parçalarıdır” ifadelerini kullandı.

Son dönemde milyarlarca dolarlık fon yolsuzluğu, Mekke Anlaşması kapsamında Yemen’e müdahale etme ihtimali ve bugün başlayan Ekrem İmamoğlu savunması gündemdeki yerini korurken, muhalif basına yönelik bu müdahalelerin söz konusu yolsuzluğun ve hukuksuzlukların üzerinin örtülmek ve muhalif medyada tartışılmasının engellenmek istendiğini gösterdiğini belirten Candemir şunları söyledi: “Siyasi iktidarın, toplumsal muhalefetin sesini kısmaya ve farklı görüşlerin kamuoyuna ulaşmasını engellemeye yönelik uygulamaları kabul edilemez. Basın kuruluşlarının bağımsızlığına yönelik her türlü müdahale, yalnızca gazetecilerin çalışma koşullarını değil, toplumun doğru ve özgür bilgiye erişim hakkını da doğrudan hedef almaktadır.”

Basın özgürlüğünün demokratik bir toplumun vazgeçilmez bir unsuru olduğunu vurgulayan Candemir, “Gazetecilerin özgürce haber yapabildiği, farklı görüşlerin baskı görmeden ifade edilebildiği, medya kuruluşlarının siyasi müdahalelerden bağımsız çalışabildiği bir ülke istiyoruz. Hukukun üstünlüğü, ifade özgürlüğü ve demokratik haklar herkes için güvence altında olmalıdır. Hiçbir güç, basın özgürlüğünü ortadan kaldırmanın veya halkın haber alma hakkını sınırlandırmanın aracı hâline getirilmemelidir. Hukuk, herkese eşit uygulanmalı; adalet, siyasi hesaplaşmaların aracı hâline getirilmemelidir” dedi.

Yargıyı, kolluğu, kayyımları ve dijital sansürü birer baskı aracına dönüştürerek ülkenin her geçen gün daha koyu bir karanlığa sürüklendiğini vurgulayan Candemir, “Bilinmelidir ki bu çabaları beyhudedir. Tarih sayısız kere göstermiştir ki hiçbir iktidar baskıyla, yasaklarla ve zorbalıkla ömrünü sonsuza kadar uzatamamıştır” diye konuştu.

İzmir Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri olarak Halk TV emekçileriyle dayanışma içinde olacaklarını vurgulayan Candemir, “Tüm emek ve demokrasi güçlerini bu hukuksuzluğa karşı ortak mücadeleyi büyütmeye çağırıyoruz. Çünkü biliyoruz ki bu örgütlü kötülüğü dağıtacak olan ortak mücadele ve dayanışmadır. Emeğin, barışın, özgürlüğün ve demokrasinin kazandığı bir geleceği mutlaka birlikte kuracağız” ifadelerini kullandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Meteoroloji'den yağış alarmı: 48 ilde sarı, 5 ilde turuncu kodlu uyarı
content:
İçişleri Bakanı Mustafa Çiftçi, Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğü'nün son değerlendirmelerine göre 14-16 Ekim tarihleri arasında 48 il için sarı, 5 il için turuncu kodlu uyarı verildiğini açıkladı. Çiftçi, özellikle Marmara Bölgesi’nde yağışların yer yer çok kuvvetli olmasının beklendiğini bildirdi.

İçişleri Bakanı Mustafa Çiftçi, olumsuz hava koşullarına karşı yürütülen hazırlıklara ilişkin açıklamasında şu ifadeleri kullandı: "Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğümüzün son değerlendirmelerine göre, 14-16 Ekim tarihlerinde 48 ilimiz için sarı, 5 ilimiz için turuncu kodlu meteorolojik uyarı verilmiştir. Özellikle Marmara Bölgemizde yağışların yer yer çok kuvvetli olması beklenmektedir. Muhtemel olumsuzluklara karşı Afyonkarahisar, Tokat, Muğla, Kütahya ve Eskişehir’den ilave ekip ve ekipman desteği sağlanmıştır. Yarın yoğun yağış beklenen Sakarya ve çevresinde de olası müdahale ihtiyaçları için hazırlıklarımızı tamamladık. Yaşanan olumsuzluklar sırasında elektrik çarpması sonucu bir vatandaşımızın hayatını kaybettiğini derin bir üzüntüyle öğrendim. Hayatını kaybeden vatandaşımıza Allah’tan rahmet, kederli ailesine ve yakınlarına başsağlığı diliyorum. Tedbir hayat kurtarır. Bu süreçte vatandaşlarımızdan, yetkili kurumlarımızca yapılan açıklama ve yönlendirmelere riayet etmelerini, gerekli tedbirleri almalarını önemle rica ediyorum. Rabbim ülkemizi ve milletimizi her türlü afetten korusun."

author: Sharon Zhang
title: New Lawsuit Seeks to Oust Kushner From Envoy Position Amid Profit-Seeking
content:
The lawsuit comes as Trump’s son-in-law faces scrutiny over conflicts of interest related to his diplomatic efforts.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

A government watchdog has filed a lawsuit seeking to prohibit Jared Kushner from serving as special envoy for the Trump administration amid reports of conflicts of interest related to his role as a top Middle East negotiator.

The complaint, filed by Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (CREW) on Wednesday, argues that courts should block Kushner from his role because he has not been subject to Senate approval and financial disclosure requirements that are required for people with his level of power.

CREW argues that such requirements, set out by the Constitution’s Appointments Clause and the Ethics in Government act of 1978, were instituted to ensure that government officials who wield such power as Kushner are properly vetted by lawmakers and the public. Kushner holds his position “in clear violation of these protections,” the lawsuit states.

“Jared Kushner is required to follow the Constitution and federal law, and if he has nothing to hide, he should welcome the opportunity to go through the Senate confirmation process and show the public everything is above board,” said CREW president Donald K. Sherman in a statement. “Instead, he has decided to act as though he is above the law and ignore it.”

The lawsuit comes after recent reports revealed overlapping interests between his private equity firm and the Middle Eastern parties that he negotiates with as a White House representative.

Earlier this month, CNN found that Kushner’s firm, Affinity Partners, holds the largest stake in a Tel Aviv-based company that has significant stakes in arms makers that supply the Israeli military.

Additionally, The New York Times reported that Kushner has been trying to raise $5 billion or more for Affinity from Middle Eastern states this year while he was representing the U.S. in negotiations in the region. This spring, Affinity reported $6 billion in assets, with 99 percent belonging to foreign investors such as Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates.

As President Donald Trump’s “special envoy for peace,” Kushner has led or been involved with numerous high-level diplomatic missions to the Middle East, including talks with Iran prior to the launch of the 2026 U.S.-Israeli war on the country, alongside fellow special envoy Steve Witkoff.

“The interplay and overlap between his government role and private business interests present a heightened risk of financial conflicts of interest,” CREW’s lawsuit states. “Nonetheless, Kushner continues to exercise significant government power while circumventing the very protections put in place to guard against such conflicts.”

The lawsuit also requests that the court requires Kushner to file financial disclosures covering his time as special envoy for peace.

title: İstanbul'u sel aldı: 1.277 su baskını, bir ölüm, 15 heyelan, binlerce yardım çağrısı
content:
İstanbul Valiliği, 14 Ekim günü sabah 06:00 ile 20:00 arasında kesintisiz süren olağanüstü yağışların 1.277 su baskınına yol açtığını, kentte 15 heyelan, 47 mahsur kalma, 13 ağaç devrilmesi ve iki çatı uçması kaydedildiğini bildirdi. Ayrıca 808 konut, 280 iş yeri ve 76 araçla ilgili ihbarlar alındı. 


Valilik açıklamasında şu bilgilere yer verdi:


“AFAD, İBB, İlçe Belediyeleri başta olmak üzere tüm kurumlar 8 bin personel, 2 bin araç ve iş makinası ile sahada yağış nedeniyle oluşan olumsuzluklara müdahale etmektedir.”


Kent genelinden alınan 2 bin 518 ihbarın ilgili müdahale ekiplerine yönlendirildiği bildirildi. 


Beykoz'da metrekareye 194 kilogram yağmur


İstanbul'un ilçeleri arasında yağış miktarı farklılık gösterdi.


Valiliğin verilerine göre Beykoz-Ömerli'de metrekareye 193,84 kilogram; Arnavutköy'de 125,9, Sarıyer-İTÜ Maslak istasyonunda 124,72, Çatalca'da 75,2 kilogram yağış kaydedildi.


Buna karşılık Kartal'da 14,3, Bakırköy'de yalnızca 6,8 kilogram yağış ölçüldü.


Yağış özellikle İstanbul'un bazı kuzey ve batı ilçelerinde yoğunlaştı. 


Yollar ve alt geçitler sular altında kaldı


Sağanak, özellikle Esenyurt, Başakşehir, Sultangazi ve Bayrampaşa'da ciddi su baskınlarına yol açtı.


Esenyurt Haramidere Sanayi Bölgesi'nde iş yerlerini su bastı. Başakşehir İkitelli'de araçlar suyla dolan yollarda ve alt geçitlerde mahsur kaldı.


Sultangazi'de yolların göle dönmesi nedeniyle yayalar yürümekte zorlandı. Bayrampaşa'da iş yerlerini korumaya çalışan esnaf, biriken suları kendi imkânlarıyla tahliye etmeye çalıştı.


Alt geçitlere ve bazı metro istasyonlarına su girmesi ulaşımda aksamalara neden oldu. Trafikte kalan araçlar ve toplu taşıma duraklarında biriken yolcular, yağışın günlük yaşam üzerindeki etkisini artırdı. 


Fatih'te 14 yaşındaki çocuk elektrik akımına kapıldı 


Sel felaketinin ilk ölüm haberi akşam saatlerinde geldi. Fatih'in Balat Mahallesi'ndeki Çukurbostan Parkı'nda 14 yaşındaki M.I., bir su birikintisine bastığı sırada elektrik akımına kapıldı. Bilinci kapalı olarak hastaneye kaldırılan çocuk, tüm müdahalelere rağmen kurtarılamadı.


İstanbul Valiliği olayla ilgili soruşturma başlatıldığını açıkladı. 


Sel sularında sürüklenen kadın kurtarıldı


Esenyurt'un Dereyolu Hürriyet Mahallesi'nde suya kapılan bir kadın, metrelerce sürüklendikten sonra çevredekilerin yardımıyla kurtarıldı. 


Sarıyer Ayazağa'da ise saat 19.00 sıralarında bir İETT otobüsü sel sularında sürüklendi. Mahsur kalan yolcular otobüsün tepesine çıkarak yardım bekledi. 


Perşembe günü okullar tatil, motosikletler trafikten men edildi


İstanbul Valiliği, 15 Ekim Perşembe günü kent genelindeki resmi ve özel eğitim kurumlarında yüz yüze eğitime bir gün ara verildiğini duyurdu.


Valilik ayrıca kamu kurumlarında çalışan hamile ve engelli personelin, gazilerin ve belirli koşullarda sekiz yaşından küçük çocuğu bulunan kadın çalışanların idari izinli sayılacağını açıkladı.


Motosiklet ve benzeri iki tekerlekli araçların trafiğe çıkışı da 14 Ekim saat 21.00'den başlayarak ikinci bir talimata kadar yasaklandı.


İstanbul Valiliğinin 19.49'da yayımladığı resmi açıklamada özellikle bodrum katlarında oturan yurttaşların su baskını tehlikesine karşı önlem almalarını ve zorunlu olmadıkça dışarı çıkmamalarını istendi. 


Felaketin boyutları


İstanbul'da birkaç saat içinde felaket boyutlarına bürünen olağanüstü yağışın etkisi, yalnızca su baskınlarıyla sınırlı değildi. Heyelanlar, elektrik çarpması tehlikesi, sürüklenen araçlar ve toplu taşıma sistemindeki aksamalar kent altyapısının farklı kesimlerinde sorunlara yol açtı. 


İstanbul'un sel tarihinde yeni bir felaket


14 Ekim'de Beykoz-Ömerli'de metrekareye düşen 193,84 kilogram yağış, İstanbul'un ekim ayı ortalaması olan 66,3 kilogramın yaklaşık üç katı. Bu miktar, kentin tarihsel yağış rekorlarına yaklaşırken bazı istasyonlarda kaydedilen en yüksek günlük değerleri de aşıyor.


İstanbul daha önce de benzer felaketler yaşadı. Eylül 2009'da Ayamama Deresi ve çevresindeki selde 31 kişi hayatını kaybetti. Temmuz 2017'de Silivri'de 2 saat içinde 118 kilogram yağış ölçüldü. Eylül 2023'te Arnavutköy ve Başakşehir'de 125 kilograma ulaşan sağanakta 2 kişi yaşamını yitirdi. 2026 felaketi, şiddetli yağış açısından istisnai boyutlara ulaşmış olsa da, İstanbul'un sel geçmişinde benzer felaketler yaşanmıştı. 


1.277 su baskını, 15 heyelan ve sel sularında sürüklenen araçlar ve Fatih'te 14 yaşındaki bir çocuğun su birikintisinde elektrik akımına kapılarak ölmesini içeren 14 Ekim bilançosu …

author: Lilli Akpaleeapik
title: Man dies after altercation in Iqaluit
content:
RCMP are treating the death of a man involved in an altercation in Iqaluit last week as a homicide.


Police responded to calls about an altercation at around 9:55 p.m. on Oct. 6, according to a press release issued Wednesday by Sgt. George Henrie.


Two people were transported to the Qikiqtani General Hospital with life-threatening injuries.


“Despite life saving measures, one male succumbed to his injuries,” Henrie wrote.


RCMP identified the man who died as 38-year-old Robert Kipanik.


The other person, who has yet to be identified, was medivaced to Ottawa, where he is in stable condition.


The RCMP’s Major Crime Unit is investigating.

author: Sophia Cope
title: DHS Inspector General Finds That TSA is Not Properly Safeguarding Passenger Facial Recognition Data
content:
EFF legal intern Gabrielle Ladun was the principal author of this post.

The Department of Homeland Security Office of Inspector General (DHS OIG) has published a summary of findings from its audit of the Transportation Security Administration’s (TSA) facial recognition technology. While the detailed findings are classified, the summary states that the OIG’s audit uncovered a “significant weakness” in the technology’s ability to protect the privacy of passenger data. This has massive privacy implications for the millions of passengers who travel and don’t opt out of the TSA’s biometric surveillance technology verification process.

TSA uses facial comparison technology for identity verification of airline passengers. A camera takes a photo of passengers to verify that their provided identification matches their live photo. Although TSA states that it is “committed to protecting traveler privacy,” the audit highlights that this has not been the case.

The OIG found that TSA’s Credential Authentication Technology 2’s (CAT-2) vendor “was able to access and extract sensitive passenger information, including driver’s license and passport images, during system troubleshooting and enhancements, without TSA’s knowledge.”

The OIG further admonished the agency:

TSA lacked clear policies, did not track when this data was extracted, could not verify that extracted information was properly deleted, and did not notify passengers when their biometric and biographic information may have been stored. As a result, although passenger information was generally protected during routine operations, weaknesses in vendor oversight created a risk that sensitive personal information could be retained or exposed.

We hope the TSA will fix these issues. The OIG summary states:

We issued one finding and three recommendations to strengthen controls, improve oversight, and ensure transparency and the proper handling of passenger data. TSA concurred with all three recommendations. Two recommendations are open and resolved, and one remains open and unresolved.

EFF has a long history of opposing governmental use of facial recognition technology. As the OIG’s audit underscores, this technology presents privacy risks associated with unsecured data, unauthorized access, and data breaches. The government’s use of this technology also creates a mass surveillance system and facilitates the creation of warrantless biometric records for unconsenting parties.

The biometric data captured by this technology is not without errors. There have been multiple instances of law enforcement agencies using facial recognition technology to misidentify and arrest innocent individuals.

Given that facial recognition technology is prone to mistakes, combined with the OIG’s audit revealing significant privacy weaknesses, it is imperative that travelers remember that opting out is possible. TSA’s own website emphasizes that travelers who wish to decline to have their photo taken for facial comparison can do so without any delay, disruption, or recourse.

Considering the data protection weaknesses exposed by the OIG’s audit, EFF will continue to oppose this governmental system of mass surveillance and spread awareness to ensure that no one is forced to relinquish their biometric data without consent.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Most Americans Say Trump’s Presidential Profits Are Illegal or Unethical
content:
Meanwhile, Trump reportedly ousted Guilfoyle because he was upset that she was making money off his presidency.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

A strong majority of Americans believe that President Donald Trump is profiting illegally or unethically from his presidency, polling finds.

AP-NORC poll results released Tuesday find that 41 percent of U.S. adults say that Trump has acted illegally in personally profiting from his position, while another 18 percent say that those actions are unethical, for a total of 59 percent. In contrast, only 18 percent of people say that he has done nothing wrong.

Even a sizable proportion of Republicans, at 32 percent, believe that Trump has acted illegally or unethically in seeking private gain, the poll found.

Meanwhile, an even larger proportion believe that Trump is prioritizing his personal profits while acting as president. Fifty-six percent said he is prioritizing his profits “a lot,” while 19 percent said “some.” This stands in stark contrast to only 23 percent of people saying that he is prioritizing the country “a lot” and only 11 percent saying he’s focusing on “people like me.”

Corruption allegations have become rather common during Trump’s second term.

Trump has disclosed making $2.2 billion in income in 2025. Much of those profits came from the president’s crypto schemes and his meme coin that he launched three days before his second inauguration. His promotions of these schemes have often been openly corrupt; at least twice, for instance, Trump has encouraged buyers to become the biggest holders of the coin in order to gain access to an exclusive dinner with him.

Trump and his team hardly try to hide his many other avenues of income that are boosted by his presidency. His financial team trades prolifically, often in relation to his decisions. His practice of hosting foreign leaders and power brokers at his resorts has multiplied during this term. Earlier this year, Truth Social unrolled a program to allow traders and banks to buy access to Trump’s Truth Social posts — which often move markets — at the “fastest” speed, allowing them to access information quicker than others could react.

Trump has openly bragged about the power of wielding the Oval Office; earlier this year, he said that his children have “inside information” whenever they make any sort of investment or purchase. He has also defended his profits, claiming that he doesn’t “get involved” with his personal finances and that “we have funds that run my money.”

But Trump is still aware of the public perception of corruption surrounding his administration. This week, he ordered the ouster of U.S. ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle after reports found that she had asked a Trump donor to pay off a $100,000 credit card bill in exchange for access to the administration.

According to the Wall Street Journal, Trump grew incensed at Guilfoyle because he was upset that she was profiting off of his presidency. His aides, meanwhile, were concerned about more headlines describing the Trump administration’s self-dealing ahead of the midterm elections.

author: Leanne Sanders
title: Advocate says chiefs, grassroots working to get 145,000 registered First Nations to vote in Alberta referendum
content:
An Indigenous political activist and advocate says chiefs in Alberta, along with grassroots organizers says they’re doing everything they can to get First Nations people out to vote in the Oct. 19 referendum which could open a path for Alberta to pursue a formal separation process.

With the vote less than a week away, a key strategist says mobilization has been underway since Premier Danielle Smith introduced legislation making it easier for separatists to mount a successful petition to force a referendum.

“It really started in May 2025 when the chiefs called an emergency meeting, and the response back then was to her first legislative piece, Bill 54. The chiefs came in very firm 100 per cent opposed to separation prepared to fight. They ordered her by letter, and they all signed off on the letter to cease and desist on her separation intention,” Cara Currie Hall told APTN News in an interview.

Bill 54 was an omnibus bill that received Royal Assent in May, 2025. It included a number of changes related to the electoral process in Alberta including lifting the ban on corporate and union political donations for provincial elections and direct democracy processes like referendums and introduced a $5,000 annual contribution limit and a $5 million general election spending limit for political parties.

The separation question is number 10 on the ballot. It reads: “Should Alberta remain a province of Canada, or should the Government of Alberta commence the legal process required under the Canadian Constitution to hold a binding provincial referendum on whether or not Alberta should separate from Canada?”

Voters are then given two options to choose from: Option 1: Alberta should remain a province of Canada or Option 2: The Government of Alberta should commence the legal process required under the Canadian Constitution to hold a binding provincial referendum on whether or not Alberta should separate from Canada.

Currie Hall was a key figure in the Rock the Indigenous Vote movement in Canada in 2015 and helped organize Indigenous voters in the United States to back Barack Obama in his presidential run. She’s lending her considerable political savvy to the chiefs in Alberta and contends it was easy to see what Smith’s intentions were in making legislative changes.

“Because by then, [Smith] already lowered the threshold of signatures required to advance a referendum, and she lowered it from 60 per cent required signatures… to only 10 per cent, which is how she got away with only needing a hundred and seventy seven thousand signatures to push forward for a referendum. So, she accommodated that right from the get go.”

Currie Hall has been working alongside chiefs and grassroots people at her home First Nation of Maskwacis, 96 km south of Edmonton, to inform members of the importance of this vote. That work follows legal challenges mounted by several First Nations against Alberta over the constitutionality of the referendum.

Athabasca Chipewyan First Nation and the Blackfoot Confederacy (including Siksika Nation, Piikani Nation, and Blood Tribe with a total of at least five to six distinct First Nations/groups) brought successful judicial reviews and legal challenges that led the Court of King’s Bench to quash the separation petition and rule that the province breached its constitutional duty to consult.

Sturgeon Lake Cree Nation is suing the Alberta government, the chief electoral officer, and the federal attorney general in a separate lawsuit over Bill 14 and the separation petition process. Sturgeon Lake Cree said the referendum breached the treaties which pre-dated the province of Alberta.

APTN requested an interview with the chief but were advised he is not giving interviews at this time. Instead, in an emailed statement Sunshine said they’ve been informing and educating members “ever since Danielle Smith announced there would be an unconstitutional, expensive, and divisive referendum…”

“We hope that when all votes are counted Albertans will have repudiated this farcical anti -Treaty, anti-immigrant, and anti-democratic process,” Sunshine said.

Onion Lake Cree Nation which straddles the Alberta-Saskatchewan boundary also revived a separate lawsuit against Alberta’s broader Sovereignty Within a United Canada Act over related constitutional and treaty concerns. It claimed the provincial legislation infringes on constitutionally protected treaty rights.

author: Hope Pisoni
title: Meta Has Paid Far Right Accounts for Their Posts Ahead of the Midterms
content:
An invite-only program for content creators has accounts promoting white supremacy, anti-LGBTQ, and neo-Nazi rhetoric.

An invite-only program for content creators has accounts promoting white supremacy, anti-LGBTQ, and neo-Nazi rhetoric.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

On September 14, far-right influencer Chaya Raichik, known online as Libs of Tiktok, attacked a Washington state high school on Facebook for displaying a Pride flag. “Hey Mercer Island High School, why does your profile photo display a mutilation flag??” she wrote, tagging the school’s account in the post and attaching a photo of the entrance.

A few weeks before, on August 27, neo-Nazi webcomic artist StoneToss posted a strip that used Tim Curry’s death to mock transgender suicide rates. And earlier this month, right-wing political commentator Benny Johnson shared claims that Democrats will “transition your kids while you’re at work” and “hand out gas cards to illegal aliens.”

Meta pays these creators for making posts like these. In 2024, the tech giant unveiled a new invite-only program called Facebook Content Monetization, designed to streamline earnings for creators. Many creators celebrated the move, with some reporting a major increase in their earnings through the program.

However, that program has recently come under scrutiny. In August, the Australian Broadcasting Corporation reported that Meta invited accounts promoting white supremacist and neo-Nazi ideologies. And after reviewing Meta’s monetization data, Uncloseted Media identified 29 accounts with histories of anti-LGBTQ+ rhetoric that have been invited to the program. These include the three aforementioned accounts as well as podcaster Candace Owens, who has blamed gay men for child abuse in the Catholic church, and Turning Point USA, which has been connected to an assault on a queer Arizona State University professor. Meta did not respond to Uncloseted Media and The 19th’s requests for an interview or for comment.

With the midterm elections looming, some of the accounts Meta pays through the program have been spreading political misinformation. In the first week of October, for example, Benny Johnson made 14 separate Facebook posts connecting the Democratic Party to election fraud.

Courtney Radsch, director of the Center for Media and Digital Governance at Open Markets Institute, said that promoting hateful rhetoric and misinformation like this is especially dangerous during an election season where the increasingly authoritarian Trump administration, which Meta has courted since its inauguration, has openly discussed attempts to interfere.

“Amplifying and enabling harassment campaigns and centering fringe conspiracy theories through algorithmic curation and monetization opportunities has led to a dissolution of democracy in America,” Radsch told Uncloseted Media and The 19th. “This administration is dismantling democratic oversight and increasing authoritarian control. … You can’t look at your platform policies on monetization without looking at the context in which this is occurring in the U.S. with rising technofascism.”

Meta launched its Facebook Content Monetization program to incentivize more creators to post on Facebook, which has faced an aging user base and competition from newer apps. Those incentives can be substantial — within the program’s first year, content creators who accepted Meta’s invitation to join reported huge increases in their payouts, with some calling it their most lucrative platform. One creator told The Hollywood Reporter that she consistently earned $20,000 to $30,000 per month, while another said his monthly earnings often hit six figures.

While most accounts aren’t big enough to rake in that amount of money, Meta also motivates smaller accounts to join. Starting in 2025, they launched a side program called “breakthrough bonus” that advertises up to $5,000 and an automatic onboarding into Content Monetization for creators from other platforms if they start posting regularly on Facebook.

SK Smigiel, a content creator who posts about LGBTQ+ education and activism under the username justsaysk, joined the program through the breakthrough bonus initiative in April. author: Chris Walker
title: As Inflation Goes Up, New Poll Shows 4 in 10 Struggle to Pay Basic Necessities
content:
The latest Consumer Price Index report shows that inflation has gone up 3.7 percent over the past year.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

The latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) report from the Bureau of Labor Statistics shows inflation has increased over the past month (and the year overall), as millions of Americans say they are struggling to make ends meet or pay for basic necessities.

According to the CPI report, which was published on Wednesday, consumer prices shot up by 0.6 percent from August to September. Year-over-year prices have increased by 3.7 percent.

That yearly rate is higher than previous reports in 2026. On average, the annual inflation rate, which is included in each monthly report, has been around 3.3 percent since the start of the year. The latest CPI numbers are also higher than they were immediately before Trump returned to the White House in 2025 — according to the December 2024 CPI, the inflation rate was 2.9 percent.

Costs for staple food items have increased over the past year, with ground beef prices up 5.4 percent, fruits and vegetables up 3.7 percent, bread up 3.3 percent, and fish/seafood up 6.9 percent. Energy costs are also markedly higher than they were last year, increasing by 10.9 percent overall, including a 21.5 percent increase in gas prices compared to September 2025.

Analysts largely attribute higher energy prices to Trump’s war against Iran, which began in late February and resulted in the blocking of the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of the world’s oil is normally transported. The week before the war began, gas prices across the U.S. averaged around $2.937 per gallon. As of Wednesday, prices are $4.333 per gallon on average, a 47 percent increase over the past seven months.

While prices for gasoline have been higher in the past, those increased costs were temporary. This week, the U.S. broke a record set in 2022 for the most days in a calendar year where average prices for regular gasoline have been above $4 per gallon: 158 days total since the start of 2026.

On gas costs, the Trump administration has promised throughout the war that higher prices would be short-lived.

“Rest assured, to the American people, the recent increase in oil and ​gas prices is temporary, and this operation will result in lower gas prices in the long term,” former White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said in March.

Asked by reporters about continuing high costs for fuel, Trump said in April that “gas will go down” and will “drop like a rock” as soon as the war is over. In June, he made a similar statement on Truth Social, writing that “Gas prices will plummet, and Affordability will be far better” than in the Biden years.

Earlier this week, Trump appeared to ignore entirely the fact that most Americans are feeling economic pinches, falsely stating during one of his campaign speeches that “prices are coming down very fast” right now.

The president promised on the 2024 presidential campaign trail to lower prices for groceries and other consumer goods, and to produce $2 per gallon gasoline shortly after entering office.

New polling demonstrates Americans are struggling, despite Trump’s rosy assessments.

According to a recently published Pew Research Center survey, 60 percent of Americans say they don’t have enough income to lead the life they desire. The poll also showed that 53 percent say they don’t have emergency savings that could help pay expenses for three months, and a third of respondents (32 percent) say they worry every day or almost every day about health care and debt costs.

Seventy percent of Americans have had to cut back their spending habits for “extras” — going out to eat or streaming services, for example. And 44 percent say they have had trouble paying for at least one basic necessity over the past year.

title: Le hussard noir tombe du toit / une émission de Minuit Décousu
content:
Après notre émission sur le début du mouvement lycéen à Lyon, on continue à suivre la mobilisation en passant cette fois la porte des établissements actuellement vides pour voir ce qu'il reste des fameux hussards noirs de la République et comprendre l'origine du malaise qui a poussé autant de jeunes dans les rues.


Cette semaine, cela fait déjà près d'une vingtaine de jours que le mouvement lycéen et désormais également étudiant s'est emparé des rues lyonnaises quasi quotidiennement. Partout, les lycées ont encore leurs portes solidement fermées voire barricadées de peur de la résurgence des rassemblement lycéens aux portes des établissements, malgré la répression inédite menée conjointement par la préfecture et le rectorat. Depuis notre dernière émission, où l'on écoutait dans des entretiens fleuves des lycéen-nes lyonnais-es nous parler de leurs premiers blocages, de l'organisation et des perspectives du mouvement, la répression a tenté de dégager la mobilisation des abords des établissements pour lui faire gagner la respectabilité des mobilisation sociales traditionnelles. Pourtant, la jeunesse continue de prouver jour après jour sa détermination à poursuivre le mouvement, selon son propre agenda.


Pour cette émission, on voulait aller voir ce qu'il se passait en interne dans les établissements scolaires pour comprendre l'origine du malaise qui a poussé autant de jeunes dans la rue. On est donc allés tourner dans la manifestation du 13 octobre à Lyon, où l'on écoute à nouveau des lycéen-nes, mais aussi des étudiant-es nous parler de l'avancée de leur mobilisation et la manière dont les établissements du second degré et du supérieur tentent coûte que coûte de mater la révolte en interne en gardant leurs portes fermées. Dans cette même manif', on s'est entretenu avec des profs de lycées de quartiers populaires ayant connu de nombreux blocages qui nous expliquent concrètement ce qu'il se passe dans les établissements fantômatiques depuis ces 20 derniers jours. . On écoute aussi une camarade prof de lettre en réseau d'éducation prioritaire renforcé (REP+) de banlieue lyonnaise, qui revient à notre micro sur les évolutions de l'éducation ces 10 dernières années, sur l'absence complète de démocratie dans les bahuts et sur le fossé grandissant entre l'ordre et la morale pronés par les adultes et les désirs de révolution des jeunes. Pour saupoudrer le tout d'un peu d'histoire, on est allés repiquer les archives du mouvement lycéen de 1971 à Villeurbanne dans le 2ème numéro des

Informations Rassemblées à Lyon

 (IRL).


L'émission s'écoute sur notre

audioblog

, ici, et un peu partout en podcast. Bonne écoute !


Minuit Décousu, c'est un fanzine radiophonique nocturne sur

Radio Canut

 (Lyon et alentours),

Radio Vassivière

 (Limousin) et

Cause Commune

 (Paris/IDF). Semaine après semaine pendant une heure, on en découd avec la nuit et on tire les fils de sons, de textes, d'archives et de voix qui s'entremêlent.

author: Ju-Hyun Park
title: Progressives Shouldn’t Call on Trump to Restore Military Exercises in Korea
content:
More than 20 Democrats signed a letter calling on Trump to maintain escalatory policies against North Korea.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The Korean Peninsula was thrust back into the spotlight this August following a surprise announcement from U.S. President Donald Trump that the annual Ulchi Freedom Shield joint U.S.-South Korea military exercises would be partially cancelled. In his typical meandering style, Trump simultaneously claimed the decision stemmed from his “very good relationship” with Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) President Kim Jong Un, and his growing frustration with the Republic of Korea (ROK), which he said had rebuffed his calls to join the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. While politicians and the media clamored over whether the decision was justified, few questioned the basic assumption that the U.S. military protects the Korean people or regional stability.

Trump’s up-and-down engagement with the DPRK has been a recurring story throughout his political career. It is one of the most ridiculed aspects of his presidency, and also one of the most misunderstood. At the root of this is a persistent ignorance concerning the true nature of Washington’s history and interests in Korea.

Democrats soon moved to convey their disapproval. DropSite News leaked a letter signed by 22 Democratic members of Congress expressing “alarm” at Trump’s decision, essentially urging the president to maintain a commitment to a cycle of military escalation and brinksmanship in Korea. “This decision has strained a 73-year alliance and risks undermining readiness, security, and deterrence on the Korean Peninsula,” the signatories warned. The letter was quietly published by House Democrats after the leak.

To be sure, there is much to criticize about the manner and purpose for why the Trump government made this choice to scale back these war drills in August. But it is important to recognize that Trump’s decision had little effect on the military situation. Ulchi Freedom Shield is a significant series of war drills, but it is far from the only one. In 2025, U.S. Forces Korea conducted 274 days of similar war exercises. Cancelling just a few is a drop in the bucket, and did nothing to meet his stated goal of advancing dialogue with the DPRK — which would have required stepping back from the prevailing framework of denuclearization.

So what was Trump’s purpose? In the weeks since, it has become apparent that Trump’s decision was a maneuver to pressure Seoul to concede on other matters: deliveries on the ROK’s promised $350 billion in tariff-related investments to the U.S., and joining the war on Iran. Today, South Korea is seeing a growing protest movement to prevent Seoul from capitulating to this pressure. The real issue is not Trump’s reduction of military drills; it is the U.S. war machine in Korea, and Democrats are part of this problem.

Calls for elected Democrats to drop their hawkish rhetoric on North Korea have gone unheeded. At a time when Washington is engaged in numerous destructive wars around the world, many of them escalated under Trump 2.0, the old guard of the Democratic Party is stubbornly clinging to a Cold War vision of the Korean Peninsula that can only lead to further escalation and instability.

The U.S. military has occupied Korea since 1945, when Washington made the decision to divide the peninsula into separate occupation zones, rather than permit the Korean people to organize an independent government. The U.S. military occupation in the south waged a brutal counterinsurgency war to crush a series of popular rebellions, and established the Republic of Korea (ROK) under the lead of Syngman Rhee, a staunchly pro-U.S. and anti-communist political figure. Even before the official start of the Korean War in 1950, the U.S. and ROK killed over 100,000 Koreans in the south alone.

Opposing war drills in Korea is fundamentally about opposing the violence of military occupation and Washington’s role in prolonging the Korean War.

The war itself brought only further destruction. In the south, the U.S. designated civilian refugees as enemy combatants, leading to atrocities like No Gun Ri, in which U.S. soldiers massacred hundreds of Korean refugees after evacuating them from their homes south of the 38th parallel. The U.S. backed the ROK state in its extermination campaign of …

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump’s New Press Sec Faces Scrutiny Over Lawyer Claims, Anti-Abortion Views
content:
Zacharia’s claims of being a lawyer and her spreading of anti-abortion disinformation have received renewed examination.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Following White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia’s first appearance before the media on Tuesday, numerous aspects of her background have come to light — including her staunch anti-abortion views and that she may have lied about her résumé.

Zacharia has claimed she is a lawyer, noting that she graduated from law school at Pepperdine University. However, no record of her passing a bar exam in any state exists, which is generally a requirement before a person can practice law. In states without that requirement, would-be lawyers usually have to submit an application to the state’s bar association, but there is no record of her applying in those jurisdictions either.

Asked by reporters this week where she passed the bar exam, Zacharia responded, “When I moved to China.” But critics have pointed out that a person cannot take a state bar exam while outside of the U.S.

White House press secretaries are not required to have an educational degree, let alone be a lawyer. However, the fact that Zacharia has possibly misled others about her personal history raises the question of whether she can be forthright or honest in her new role.

Perhaps more concerning are Zacharia’s views on reproductive rights. From November 2023 to February 2026, she served on the board of advisors for an organization called “White Rose Resistance,” an anti-abortion group that stole its name from a Nazi Germany-era resistance group that had nothing to do with the issue.

The contemporary White Rose Resistance has pushed for charging people with murder if they receive an abortion or help to facilitate one. On the organization’s FAQ page, the group downplays the possibility of a death penalty sentence for those found “guilty” of having an abortion while also not outright denying that it could happen.

After leaving the organization, Zacharia has pushed an anti-abortion agenda through the use of disinformation. In an interview from October 2026, she pointedly stated that “the abortion pill has the same chemicals that they used…in camps in Nazi Germany” — a verifiably false claim.

The decision to hire Zacharia as the Trump administration’s new press secretary could indicate that the White House may focus on abortion following the upcoming midterm elections. Indeed, according to a report from The Washington Sun, the Department of Justice (DOJ) has been instructed to move more slowly on abortion-related cases until after November, picking up attacks on abortion rights and access once the elections are over.

Abortion rights proponents have decried the appointment of Zacharia.

“Donald Trump is handing the anti-abortion disinformation movement one of the biggest megaphones in government,” Reproductive Freedom for All President and CEO Mini Timmaraju said in a statement. “Katie Zacharia is the latest anti-abortion extremist Trump has installed in his administration. We must put a check on their fringe agenda this November and block their plan to ban abortion after the midterms.”

On Tuesday, Zacharia stumbled at many moments during her first appearance as press secretary, and only took three questions from reporters (from Trump-friendly news outlets) after giving her initial remarks. Sources close to the White House said it was a rough start for her.

“You either got it or don’t. And she don’t got it,” one source connected to the administration told Politico.

“She needs to get much better, fast. Otherwise, she’ll break Scaramucci’s record,” a White House official said to MS NOW, referring to former White House communications director Anthony Scaramucci, who only served for 11 days in Trump’s first term.

This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

author: Andrea DiP
title: Em Israel, conferência da extrema direita exalta Flávio Bolsonaro
content:
Nos dias 06, 07 e 08 de outubro, a cidade de Jerusalém sediou a “National Conservatism Conference”, ou “NatCon” (algo como Conferência sobre Conservadorismo Nacional), evento que reúne algumas vezes ao ano políticos conservadores nacionalistas de extrema direita da Europa, Estados Unidos, Israel, Reino Unido e, algumas vezes, da América Latina.


Mas digamos que nossa região não é tão importante para eles, a não ser quando se fala contra a imigração de “países pobres” – nestes casos, os discursos nos colocam como quintal dos Estados Unidos, ou interessam a alianças que podem servir às suas causas. Sei disso porque já participei de outra NatCon em Bruxelas em 2024 e tenho me infiltrado nesses eventos transnacionais da extrema direita europeia desde 2022.


A NatCon é financiada pela Fundação estadunidense Edmund Burke, que tem entre seus principais doadores a Heritage Foundation. A Heritage Foundation, por sua vez, é uma das principais geradoras de diretrizes políticas para a atual administração Trump. Seu presidente, Kevin Roberts, descreve explicitamente a missão moderna da Heritage Foundation como a de “institucionalizar o Trumpismo” em uma

entrevista

 para o New York Times. Roberts foi um dos palestrantes da conferência em Jerusalém. E a Heritage está de olho no Brasil: em março deste ano, Paulo Figueiredo e Alexandre Ramagem

participaram

 de um evento da fundação em Miami, como revelou a

Pública

.


Eu estava lá nesta edição da NatCon, que reuniu políticos israelenses de extrema-direita, figuras europeias que enfrentaram medidas disciplinares por suposto antissemitismo e figuras nacionalistas cristãs e de extrema-direita dos Estados Unidos, como bem definiu o jornal britânico

The Guardian

. 


O foco principal estava no apoio às políticas e medidas de Benjamin Netanyahu contra os palestinos, a defesa do Estado de Israel, da conquista de territórios na Cisjordânia e na celebração e endosso de ações dos colonos israelenses que agem como uma milícia na região, cometendo todo tipo de barbaridades, como contei um pouco

na minha última coluna

. Também foram defendidas ações “anti-terrorismo” e anti-imigração na Europa e Estados Unidos e o combate ao que foi chamado de “red green alliance” (aliança verde e vermelha), que é como a extrema direita tem se referido à parte da esquerda progressista que protesta contra o genocídio do povo palestino. Uma das principais referências dessa aliança seria, na visão destes radicais, o prefeito de Nova York, Zohran Mamdani. Alguns palestrantes também atacaram ferrenhamente a comunidade LGBTQIA+, sobretudo as pessoas trans, e falaram da importância de criar grandes famílias, ter muitos filhos, mas sem se misturar com pessoas de diferentes culturas.


Um dos discursos mais violentos veio de Sebastian Gorka, subchefe de gabinete do presidente e diretor sênior de contraterrorismo no Conselho de Segurança Nacional dos Estados Unidos, que participou ao vivo e online da Casa Branca. Gorka é um dos aliados de Eduardo Bolsonaro nos EUA, a quem

foi apresentado

 por Steve Bannon.


Ele defendeu que existe hoje uma nova religião: “a religião da esquerda”.


“Seja ela preenchida por ambientalistas adoradores de Gaia como Greta Thunberg, seja pelo altar do DEI (Diversidade, Equidade e Inclusão, em inglês)”, disse. Seu discurso misturou a Irmandade Muçulmana com marxismo, se estendeu para ligações entre o Hamas, e a “mã do Irã”. “A Aliança Vermelho-Verde é real. Os islamistas trabalhando com os marxistas é real”. E finalizou parafraseando Trump: “Se você planeja machucar americanos ou matar inocentes, nós vamos encontrar você e nós vamos matar você”.


Foi neste clima de Conferência que o nome de Flávio Bolsonaro foi citado e aplaudido pelos presentes – cerca de 300 pessoas.


O europarlamentar Harald Vilimsky, que lidera a delegação do Partido da Liberdade da Áustria (FPÖ) no Parlamento Europeu e atua como vice-presidente do grupo “Patriotas pela Europa”, foi quem levantou a bola:


“Quero que a Europa fique ombro a ombro com Israel, com aqueles que, em termos de fé, são nossos irmãos mais velhos. Quero a parte conservadora dos Estados Unidos em nosso campo, não os Republicanos apenas no nome, mas os verdadeiros conservadores. Isso é algo que realmente poderia ser um divisor de águas no desenvolvimento internacional. Quero a Argentina com o presidente Javier Milei em nossas fileiras. Quero o Chile com o Presidente José Antonio Kast ao nosso lado. Quero Flávio Bolsonaro no Brasil.” …

title: Group from Zurich takes over the Freedom for Öcalan Vigil in Strasbourg
content:
The Freedom for Öcalan Vigil, which was launched on 25 June 2012, in Strasbourg, has entered its 746thweek.


The vigil, which continues in Strasbourg, where institutions such as the Council of Europe and the European Court of Human Rights are located, was taken over by Barış Çetin, Cihat Kalkan and Cesur Akar from Zurich.


Speaking on behalf of the demonstrators, Barış Çetin emphasized that they were protesting the conditions of isolation imposed for nearly 28 years on Abdullah Öcalan, who was imprisoned in 1999 as a result of an international conspiracy.


“We will continue until our leader’s physical freedom is secured,” Çetin said, adding, “We also want the international community to recognize the struggle taking place here and the reality of the situation. Our comrades have demonstrated their determination for 746 consecutive weeks. Our Leader’s physical freedom is of great importance to us.”


Calling on the international community to fulfill its duties and responsibilities, Çetin stated that stability and peace in the Middle East would only be possible through the freedom of Öcalan.
