title: Yekem rêzefîlma anîmasyonî ya kurdî: "Pirsên Azad" wê di Zarok TVyê de dest pê bike
content:
Rêzefîlma ku derhênerîya wê Ceren Asik Demîr dike ya bi navê “Pirsên Azad” di 12ê Cotmehê de li ser ekranên Zarok TV yê dest bi weşanê dike. Dûblaja rêzefîlmê bi temamî Kurmancî û dîmenên wî bi alîkarîya hişê çêkirî hatiye çêkirin.


Anîmasyon dê her hefte bi beşeka nû were pêşberî bîneran. Rêzefîlm ji bo zarokan hatiye amadekirin û lehengê bimeraq Azad, bi saya pirsên ku ji jiyana rojane, ji civaknasiyê heta stêrnasiyê, ji felsefeyê heta fîzîkê deriyên qad û dîsîplînên cuda vedike.


Di vê rêwîtîyê da ku ji kolanên kevir yên Mêrdînê heta Pira Malabadê, ji Baxçeyên Hewselê heta kûrahîyên fezayê dirêj dibe. Rêzefîlm li şûna bersivên amade, temaşevanan vedixwîne ku ew pirsan û lêkolînê bikin û li bersivên xwe bigerin.


"Rojhilat û Rojava bi hev ra diaxive"


Di rêwîtîya Azad da el-Bîrûnî û Lévi-Strauss, Îbn Xeldûn û Durkheim, Îbn Heysem û Newton li kêleka hev dipeyivin. Rêzefîlm dîroka zanistê bi awayekî yek-navend û yek-deng rave nake. Ew, nîşanî temaşevanên ciwan dide ku erdnîgarîya wan jî tevkarîya zanistê kirîye.


"Çîrok bi hişê çêkirî hatîye xêzkirin"


Dîmenên projeyê bi amûrên hişê çêkirî hatine çêkirin. Senaryo, montaj, dûblaj, muzîk û mîksaj jî bi temamî bi keda mirovan hatîye amadekirin. Ekîba projeyê, hişê çêkirî wekî amûrekê dibîne ku astengîya li pêşîya çêkirina anîmasyoneka bikalîte ya bi zimanekî bidezawantaj ji navê hiltîne .

‘Meraqa bi zimanê dayikê’


Rêzefîlm ji cihekî hêsan dide rê, berhemên ku zarokên Kurdîaxiv bikarin bi zimanê xwe zanistê keşf bikin, pir kêm in. “Pirsên Azad” armanc dike ku bi Zarok TVya ku bi salan e bi zimanê zarokên Kurd weşanê dike, vê valahîyê hinekî dagire. Derhêner Ceren Asik Demîr di derheqê rêzefîlmê de wiha dibêje: “Her zarok bi pirsan mezin dibe; me jî xwest ku zarok bi zimanê xwe yê dayikê li bersivên van pirsan bigerin. Hêvî dikim ku meraqa Azad bibe meraqa her zarokê li ber ekranê.”


Her wiha qonaxa sêwirana dîtbarî û anîmasyonê ji alîyê derhêner Ceren Asik Demîr û Erdal Tîmûr ve hatîye birêvebirin. Senaryoya wê M. Dara nivîsîye. Kawa Cengîz Yildiz dengê xwe daye karakterê Azad, derhênerîya dublajê jî Cebar Alp kirîye. Kendal Adiguzel, Eylul Nazlier û Sîmyager jî muzîka anîmasyonê amade û îcra kirine.


(AY)

author: Unknown
title: Peace Mothers join 'Tuesdays Against Executions' campaign
content:
The Kurdistan Peace Mothers issued a statement regarding their participation in the 'Sêşema Na ji bo Darvekirinê' ('Tuesdays Against Executions') campaign.


The statement drew attention to how Iran’s regime, through its unfair courts, sentences political prisoners and civilians to mass executions every day on baseless charges. It said: “With each passing day, the shadow of the executioner regime weighs more heavily on prisoners.”


Emphasizing that life, freedom, and human dignity are fundamental and inalienable rights, the statement stressed that no mother should be forced to live in fear of her child being executed. It continued: “Execution does not merely bring one person’s life to an end; it also condemns a family to suffer forever. An execution leaves a profound impact on a family for the rest of its life. We offer our support to families who have lost their loved ones.


We demand that the fate of the prisoners be clarified as soon as possible. We call on all families, human rights organizations, and defenders of freedom to be the voice of the prisoners until freedom is secured, and the truth comes to light.”

author: Unknown
title: Police raid Halk TV: broadcast suspended, trustee appointed
content:
Police raided Halk TV’s headquarters in Istanbul in the early hours of Wednesday morning. A trustee was appointed, and its television broadcast was halted. While police searches of the building continued, the road where the channel is located was closed to traffic, and employees were denied entry to the building.


Reporting on the latest developments inside the building after police entered Halk TV, channel presenter Deniz Bayramoğlu said: “Halk TV Editor-in-Chief Suat Toktaş held talks with the head of the trustee board about continuing the broadcast, but the talks were inconclusive. The broadcast has been suspended.”


As part of the investigation, arrest warrants were issued for 17 people, and 11 people were reportedly taken into custody.


Halk TV Board Chair Cafer Mahiroğlu also announced the police raid on social media. Mahiroğlu said: “Kılıçdaroğlu, the leader of the annulment faction, and his team may be happy. The police are at Halk TV.”


Press organisations and unions protest the attack on press freedom


The appointment of a trustee to Halk TV and the suspension of its broadcast prompted protests from press organisations and journalists’ unions. DISK Basın-Iş, the Contemporary Journalists’ Association (ÇGD), and the Journalists’ Union of Turkey (TGS) condemned the decision as interference in press and freedom of expression.


DİSK Basın-Iş stated that the action against Halk TV brought to mind the intervention against TELE1 last year, adding that the jobs and futures of hundreds of media workers had also been put at risk. The union called on the public to defend press freedom, the right to access information, and the labour of journalists.


The Contemporary Journalists’ Association also described the appointment of a trustee and the suspension of the broadcast as a serious infringement of press freedom and freedom of expression. ÇGD stated that no media outlet in Turkey could any longer be assured of its right to broadcast freely and declared that it would continue its struggle for a free press and democracy.


The Journalists’ Union of Turkey, meanwhile, condemned the police raid on Halk TV and the interference with its broadcast. Describing the decision as arbitrary, TGS stated: “We will not accept this bullying! The press is free and cannot be censored!”

author: Brian Hioe
title: Taiwan Again Rolls Out the Red Carpet for an Authoritarian Monarch For National Day
content:
KING MSWATI III of Eswatini was recently in Taiwan for National Day. As a result, the red carpet was once again rolled out for the authoritarian monarch, who presides over Africa’s last absolute monarchy, by the Lai administration.

In particular, apart from Mswati III’s presence at National Day, President Lai Ching-te and Mswati III visited Taiwan’s Air Force Command. Lai touted support from Mswati III on establishing the Taiwan Industrial Innovation Park, as well as Eswatini’s role as Taiwan’s gateway into Africa. Eswatini is Taiwan’s only remaining diplomatic ally in Africa.

Ties between Eswatini and the Lai administration have been in the spotlight in recent years, especially after a dramatic visit to the country by Lai. In May, a planned trip by the Taiwanese president for King Mswati III’s 58th birthday and the 40th anniversary of his accession to the throne was abruptly canceled.

This occurred because countries that Lai would have passed over on his flight to Eswatini, Madagascar, Mauritius, and the Seychelles revoked overflight permissions shortly before Lai was to set out. This was largely interpreted as China flexing its muscles in terms of its influence in Africa, with the Lai administration suggesting that China threatened to revoke debt cancellation for Madagascar, Mauritius, and the Seychelles if they did not comply.

Lai still later traveled to Eswatini aboard Mswati III’s private aircraft. This took place with Lai abruptly traveling to Eswatini, then only announcing that he had arrived after the fact. Presumably, this was to minimize the space for China to react. Lai arrived in Eswatini by traveling on King Mswati III’s personal aircraft, a former China Airlines plane that was sold to the monarch in 2015. Lai later returned on the same aircraft, taking a winding route that tested the operational limits of the plane, but similar to the route taken by then-US Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi during her August 2022 trip to Taiwan.

Still, one notes that–as is broadly the case with Taiwan’s diplomatic relationship with Eswatini–there was little criticism of Eswatini’s record on human rights afterward. Eswatini is an absolute monarchy. The constitution was voided in 1973, and political parties were banned, as a result of which free and fair elections still do not take place in Eswatini today. Although Mswati agreed to constitutional changes in 2005, he retains his grip on power. Under Mswati III’s rule, life expectancy has halved in Eswatini since 2000.

Pro-democracy protests rocked Eswatini in the summer of 2021, with the public calling for the right to vote. In the violence that followed, 28 were shot, with demonstrators alleging that at least twenty were killed. Tear gas was used by police against demonstrators, and Internet services were suspended, with a curfew declared in major urban centers, in which buildings were burned during the turmoil, including Manzini and Mbabane, as well as the industrial center of Matsapha.

Much as occurred during Taiwan’s authoritarian period, Eswatini also sees the killing of dissidents. In 2023, opposition politician Thulani Maseko was killed by unknown gunmen in a shooting widely suspected of being ordered by the monarchy. Maseko was a human rights lawyer and public intellectual. At the time, Mswati III stated, “People should not shed tears and complain about mercenaries killing them,” implying that he had ordered the killing.

Nevertheless, after the demonstrations, Taiwan announced that it would be donating 637 million NT to the government for reconstruction–an act that makes it complicit in the government’s crackdown on the protests. Either way, Taiwan simply chose to act as though the protests had never occurred.

Indeed, in spite of its human rights violations, Taiwan has continued to blithely engage in trade relations with Eswatini. And Mswati III’s visit to Taiwan and plans for the Taiwan Industrial Innovation Park are the latest such example. Still, in the absence of international criticism of Taiwan’s ties to Eswatini, there will be little incentive for the government to make any changes.

title: Coalesce, disperse, coalesce, disperse
content:
Movements get written off when they go quiet. People disperse and reconfigure, some drop out, new people come in, and new groups form out of what came before. ICE watching builds on older activist infrastructures, and following those links is how the new ones make sense.

author: Unknown
title: Crève l'école !
content:
Banderole


En écho à toutes les formes de révoltes radicales qui traversent ce mouvement, et dans l'espoir qu'il ne se laisse pas encadrer par les pacificateurs et fossoyeurs habituels, nous avons posé une grande banderole contre ce monde, ses écoles, ses partis et ses syndicats sous le nez du

SO

 de la

CGT

 au moment du passage du cortège de la manif syndicale Place d'Italie – Invalides. La réaction de ces flics de manif qui ne supportent pas la moindre contestation ne s'est pas faite attendre puisqu'ils se sont ramenés à une petite dizaine déterminés à grimper sur l'échafaudage pour la décrocher, et prêts à défoncer des anars et autonomes comme ils rêvent de le faire depuis plusieurs décennies, sous l'œil complice de

LFI

 et des autres syndicats. On a pu entendre des remarques formidables comme «

 

Vous voulez que ça soit comme 2016, tout le monde se met en noir et casse tout

 

?

 

», «

 

c'est notre manif, c'est nous qui l'avons déclarée

 

». Cette fois, ils ont fait face à notre détermination, mais aussi au soutien de plusieurs groupes de manifestants lucides sur le rôle des syndicats, ou tout simplement solidaires contre les flics en bleu comme sous couleur de

SO

 syndical, et après une bonne demi-heure d'escarmouches et de coup de pressions ridicules, ils ont fini par lâcher l'affaire et sont repartis penauds, la matraque entre les jambes.


La banderole a ainsi pu égayer l'ensemble du cortège puis être aussi visible durant le passage de la deuxième manif quand elle a rejoint le trajet de la première. Elle était accompagnée du tract intitulé «

 

Personne ne veut de la vie que l'école nous a prévue

 

».


Vive la lutte, crève l'école, les syndicats et les partis défenseurs du vieux monde

 

!


L'assemblée anti-électorale


Tract


Personne ne veut de la vie que l'école nous a prévue


Depuis fin septembre, des centaines de milliers de jeunes se bougent dans les rues. Cette mobilisation, partie d'un blocus dans un lycée de banlieue francilienne, a été rejointe par beaucoup d'autres jusqu'à devenir mouvement, comme si les lycéens n'attendaient qu'une occasion pour déclencher la révolte.


Par le blocage, par l'incendie, par le saccage, par l'attaque aux mortiers sur les lycées ou les dirlos, ils ont rompu la monotonie de l'école. Par les pavés, les coups, les railleries et les insultes, ils ont montré aux flics que ces derniers ne pourraient les harceler et les réprimer sans réponse. Par leur inventivité et leur offensivité, ils ont montré, au nez des militants décrépis, qu'il était possible de lutter en d'autres termes que par ceux de la parade et de la négociation.


Par leurs pratiques et leurs mots d'ordre, les lycéens ont surtout posé un problème essentiel : celui du refus de la vie à laquelle la société du Travail les destine.


C'est précisément cela que les bureaucrates de gauche ne veulent pas entendre. C'est pour que ce problème essentiel n'apparaisse pas sur le devant de la scène qu'ils parlent de soucis de budget, de démocratie scolaire ou de prise en compte de la parole des élèves. C'est pour masquer le refus de l'École et le monde qu'elle introduit que les politiciens ne veulent voir dans ce qu'il se passe qu'une liste réductrice de revendications, et s'empressent de s'en prétendre les portes paroles. C'est pour que l'École et le Travail comme institutions, avec leurs principes de sélection, de dressage, d'insertion, sortent indemnes du mouvement qu'ils ne perçoivent pas que la détestation du 8-18h ou de Parcoursup chez les lycéens a la même teneur que la hanes des 35 heures ou de l'entretien d'embauche chez ceux qui taffent ou chôment.


Maintenant, ce sont eux, syndicats et partis, qui tentent de récupérer le mouvement, d'en prendre la direction, par leurs manifs rangées et leurs négociations, pour le rendre respectable et raisonnable, pour néantiser cette révolte dans les urnes en mai prochain.


Certains ne voient pas d'autre position que celle de soutien face à la révolte des lycéens. D'autres se questionnent sur l'existence ou non d'un commun entre les lycéens et les autres exploités. S'il existe évidemment un commun, c'est que les lycéens refusent aujourd'hui la vie de merde qu'on leur propose, celle-là même que nous avons été obligés d'emprunter hier. Alors nous avons tous et toutes de bonnes raisons de voir que leur combat n'est pas différent du nôtre, et de rentrer en lutte, non pas à côté d'eux ou pour eux, mais

AVEC


EUX

 pour que ce mouvement ne soit plus …

author: Unknown
title: Institut du Monde Arabe, le soutien à Gaza : une vitrine
content:
Une exposition intitulée «

 

Stories of Hope and Resilience

 

» du peintre palestinien Ahmed Mujanna organisée par le Programme Alimentaire Mondial (

PAM

) des Nations Unies en partenariat avec l'

UE

, est installée une semaine sur l'esplanade de l'Institut du Monde Arabe (lMA) qui nous dit assumer accueillir cette exposition et dénoncer les violences exercées par Israël.


Nous sommes des personnes révoltées par les actes terroristes perpétrés par l'entité sioniste et déterminées à soutenir le droit des Palestiniens à vivre sur leur terre. Aussi, intriguées par le titre, nous décidons de nous y rendre.


Les peintures réalisées sur cartons d'emballage de l'aide alimentaire, sont exposées dans un container, pour, comme le mentionne le communiqué de l' exposition :

mener une campagne de visibilité, afin de sensibiliser le grand public à la grave crise humanitaire à Gaza, transformant des symboles d'aide et de survie en œuvres artistiques fortes et percutantes

.


Ben oui un Palestinien il souffre, il agonise mais en même temps tout va bien, il résilie et il espère, dixit la bonne conscience.


L'artiste nous expliquera lui-même, en direct de Gaza, que c'est lui qui a choisi ce titre : «

 

Stories of Hope and Résilience

 

»

 

; on se sentira assez bête, avec notre ironie d'occidentale pour pallier notre impuissance.


Au fil de l'expo, comme c'est systématiquement le cas, nous constatons l'absence de mention d'Israël, le communiqué de l'

IMA

 pour cette exposition, en témoigne 

Gaza, histoires d'espoir et de résilience - Une exposition itinérante


L'un d'entre nous a été témoin du retour que faisait un visiteur à la représentante du

PAM

, en lui exprimant sa

satisfaction de ne pas voir de dénonciation, aucune mention de méchant ou de gentil dans cette exposition.

 Ce qui lui plaisait c'est que ce ne soit pas politique, sous-entendu ce à quoi l'on aurait pu s'attendre vu le contexte.


La représentante du

PAM

, pleine d'approbation mielleuse, valide son commentaire en lui confirmant que c'était effectivement le cas :


Oui , vous avez vu vraiment hein et il n 'y a aucune colère

 [

1

]

"


Comme on venait d'apprendre la présence d'Anne-Claire Legendre, présidente de l'Institut du Monde Arabe dans le container itinérant, on a saisi l'opportunité pour l'interpeller. Elle était avec son chef de cabinet et la responsable de l'expo.


Nous avons engagé la conversation avec ces gens, à partir des commentaires du visiteur satisfait et rassuré que l'exposition ne soit pas politique et le fait qu'Israël ne soit jamais mentionné. On a élargi à l'absence de positionnement de l'

IMA

 contre le génocide à Gaza.


Dans un premier temps la posture de M

me

 Legendre a été de nous dire et répéter, sans argumenter «

 

j'Assuuuuume

 

». Au bout du Nième j'assume, on a fini par lui demander : 


Mais vous assumez quoi

 

? Puisque vous ne dites rien

 

?!


Elle nous a affirmé que l'

IMA

 ne minimise rien du tout et que l'Institut tient un discours politique, en nous renvoyant à ses interventions en ligne, notamment l'hommage rendu à Leila Shahid qui condamnait soi-disant Israël.


Nous les avons donc écoutés et cherché

en vain

 une quelconque condamnation d'Israël. Par contre, nous y avons bien entendu de sa bouche perfide et sournoise, son soutien aux «

 

peuples victimes du 7 octobre à Téhéran

 

»

. On y a aussi perçu, cette creuse litanie de «

 

La Culture comme Résistance

 

»


31 mars 2026 Hommage à Leïla Shahid à l'

IMA


Elle nous a ensuite listé toute une série d'évènements sur Gaza organisés par l'

IMA

. Des «

 

évènements

 

» : ce terme nous fait bondir d'une part et d'autre part ces dits évènements existent parce qu'il y' a un génocide, la famine organisée, le droit international bafoué. Cela n'est jamais dit.


Puis la patronne, cite, le regard fier, deux expositions, pour ensuite nous rappeler à la venue d'Elias Sambar et Rachid Khalidi, il y a peu de temps. Soulagée, la chienne de garde pense avoir rabattu notre caquet et nos consciences en étalant ses cautions palestiniennes. Mais au cas où nous ne serions pas convaincus, ou nous n'aurions pas bien capté, elle rétorque :


Je crois qu'ils n'ont pas mâché leurs mots, tout ça est assez clair

 

?!


Alors qu'en réalité, il s'agissait d'un débat entre Henri Lorens et Rachid Khalidi (et non Elias Sambar)


Son sbire ressent alors le besoin de nous rappeller que l'

IMA

 est le seul musée au monde à parler autant de …

author: Unknown
title: Des casques et des képis — janvier 1971
content:
En fouillant sur le site du

CRAS

, le Centre de Recherche pour l'Alternative Social, on peut trouver toutes

les archives numérisées du journal anti-autoritaire lyonnais

IRL

, «

 

Informations Recueillies à Lyon

 

» (qui devient «

 

Informations Rassemblées à Lyon

 

» dès 1973, puis «

 

Journal d'Expression Libertaire

 

» à diffusion nationale dans les années 80). Le premier numéro du journal parait en janvier 1971. Et le premier article, intitulé

Des casques et des képis

, revient sur une bagarre entre les pompiers de Lyon en grève et les flics lors d'une manifestation, et sur les originies soixante-huitardes de la haine réciproque que les deux corpos se vouent alors.


Bagarres entre les pompiers et la police, à Lyon. 150 pompiers défilaient dans la rue en portant des pancartes qui disaient qu'ils étaient mal payés. Arrivés aux abords de la préfecture, les pompiers disent qu'un commissaire donna l'ordre à ses hommes de dégager la rue à coups de matraque sans préavis. Les policiers disent le contraire. Ils ne nient pas, en tout cas qu'ils avaient des matraques, chose délicate à nier parce qu'il y avait du monde dans le secteur. Qu'est-ce qu'ils avaient besoin de matraques

 

? Ils croyaient que les pompiers allaient foutre le feu à la préfecture

 

? Bon, bref, comme dit "le Figaro" : Le contentieux entre la police et les pompiers lyonnais remonte aux évènements de mai 68. Au cours des échauffourées qui se produisirent dans la nuit du 23 au 24, celle où le commissaire Lacroix trouva la mort sur le pont La Fayette, les pompiers avaient offert la protection à de jeunes manifestants poursuivis par les policiers. Des vrais sauvages, ces pompiers.


«

 

Depuis le 20/11/70, les sapeurs pompiers de la communauté urbaine sont en grève administrative, avec l'accord de leurs syndicats =

C.G.T.

-

C.F.D.

 T.. Le 2 décembre après avoir encore évoqué le bien-fondé de leurs protestations, ils n'hésitaient pas à exprimer "Le souhait que leur voix soit entendue très rapidement sans qu'ils soient obligés d'en venir aux actes, tout en affirmant que leur action ne saurait tarder si l'administration ne faisait pas droit à leurs requêtes dans des délais très courts.

 

»


Le surlendemain ils organisent une manifestation revendicative. 200 pompiers partirent vers 14 h. 30 du Quartier Central, caserne Molière. Quelques minutes après, à l'angle des Avenue de Saxe et rue Servient,

un commissaire tenta d'arracher la première banderole

 ("Journée nationale de manifestation des sapeurs pompiers") : n'y parvenant pas, il fit appel à des renforts de police, après avoir été repoussé sur le trottoir. Rue de Bonnel, quelques cars de police barraient le passage et

le même commissaire donna l'ordre de charger aux agents armés de matraques. Les pompiers réagirent en sportifs chevronnés

 et l'échauffourée dura quelques minutes à l'issue desquelles se trouva un second commissaire pour négocier tandis que

3 agents étaient hospitalisés à Edouard Herriot

 et que plusieurs pompiers se faisaient panser au Quartier Molière. "

LA


PROCHAINE


FOIS

author: Kodao Productions
title: Mary Grace Piattos: The Mystery Sara Duterte and Marcos Jr. Cannot Escape
content:
Mary Grace Piattos may remain a mystery forever in the Sara Duterte impeachment trial. With the withdrawal of Article I, the Senate may never determine who received the money acknowledged under that name or where it went.


But the bigger question is why the search for answers should stop here, when the confidential funds in question were allocated in 2022, under the Marcos-Duterte political alliance, while Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and Sara Duterte were still close allies.


The controversy is not just about an unexplained name on a receipt. It is about millions of pesos in public funds, the officials who handled them, and the government that allocated them.


Duterte must answer for the use of funds entrusted to her offices. Marcos, for his part, cannot simply distance himself from the allocation made under his administration. His specific responsibility for the approval and oversight of those funds deserves scrutiny, even as any personal liability must be established by evidence.


Mary Grace Piattos may be a mystery, but the responsibility for the money must not be


This is the gravely troubling consequence of Day 39 of the impeachment trial. After 38 days of presenting witnesses and documentary evidence on four articles of impeachment, the House prosecution panel withdrew three charges and decided to concentrate on Article II, involving Duterte’s alleged unexplained wealth, questionable Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN), and alleged failure to divest from business interests.


Lead prosecutor Representative Gerville Luistro defended the move, saying the remaining charge was strong enough to stand on its own and that concentrating on it would shorten the proceedings.

“All-in po tayo dito,”

 she declared.


There may be a tactical justification for narrowing the case. But an impeachment trial is not merely a race toward conviction. The question is whether a faster verdict is worth leaving other serious allegations unresolved.


By withdrawing Articles I, III, and IV, the prosecution abandoned the opportunity for the Senate to rule on allegations involving confidential-fund misuse, bribery and corruption, and grave threats against Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and House Speaker Martin Romualdez. Only Article II will proceed.


While the withdrawal neither establishes guilt nor amounts to an acquittal, it does, however, leave three sets of allegations without a determination on their merits in this impeachment proceeding.


The public is entitled to ask why charges originally considered serious enough to include in the articles of impeachment are now being abandoned and what other avenues remain for investigating them.


This concern is straightforward: the choice of which charges to pursue should not determine which allegations of abuse of public power are ultimately examined.


Article I brought the confidential and intelligence funds handled by the OVP and the DepEd during Duterte’s tenure into public scrutiny. Audit records, bank transactions, liquidation reports, and testimony from government auditors and other officials raised questions about acknowledgment receipts, unusual cash withdrawals, and the documentation used to account for public money.


Mary Grace Piattos became the most memorable symbol of those questions. With Article I withdrawn, the Senate – and the public in general – will no longer determine whether the evidence presented under that charge supports a finding of fraudulent liquidation or other wrongdoings.


The investigation must therefore continue through the Commission on Audit, the Office of the Ombudsman, and other competent authorities, as appropriate to their respective mandates. The withdrawal of an impeachment charge is not a clearance of the transactions under scrutiny.


Confidentiality may be necessary for legitimate intelligence operations, but it cannot excuse questionable liquidation or inadequate documentation. These funds come from taxpayers, and the secrecy surrounding them makes credible independent oversight indispensable.


Without effective controls, as it is now, billions in confidential and intelligence funds are becoming a pork barrel for powerful officials, beyond meaningful public scrutiny.


Marcos Jr Cannot Distance Himself from the Allocation


The 2022 confidential funds allocation must also be examined in the context of the political alliance between Marcos and Duterte. They ran together, governed together, and occupied the …

author: Tamara Pearson
title: 'Never again a Mexico without us': National Indigenous Congress marks 30 years with protests
content:
"Daddy, I'm coming for you. This struggle is for you," said Jesús Plácido Domingo's daughter on Monday at the 30th anniversary meeting of the National Indigenous Congress (CNI). She looked to be perhaps six years old, and held a picture of her father, an imprisoned Indigenous activist.

Plácido was detained in July by the Mexican Army. A member of the CNI and the regional coordinator of the Indigenous and Popular Council of Guerrero-Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ), he was playing a leading role in defending Indigenous communities from organised crime and Guerrero state from environmental destruction.

Various national and international human rights organisations have criticised the arrest, and note a pattern of criminalising activists and Indigenous community leaders — particularly those that defend water rights and stand up to mining companies and other environmentally destructive corporations, and to organised crime.

On October 12, the CNI marked 534 years since the Spanish invasion of the Americas began, and 30 years since their organisation was founded. They held a three-day conference in Mexico City, with delegates from Indigenous communities around the country participating in discussions until midnight.

Allied organisations, including small farmers, human rights groups, Guatemalan migrants, environmental groups, urban and rural communities, women, community and alternative radio and media outlets, and parents of the forcibly disappeared also met and held separate discussions about how to support and strengthen Indigenous rights and resistance.

"It's important that we organise like this so that we aren't alone as Indigenous peoples and communities. The CNI is a space where we can all go to hug each other, support each other and our struggles," Tlaxco, a CNI delegate from Milpa Alta, told Green Left.

The CNI brings together peoples and tribes, including Maya, Purépecha, Mazateco, Wixárika, Yaqui, Náyeri, Nahua and at least 30 others, as well as Afro-Mexicans and Mestizo people. It practises full autonomy and strives for recognition and the rebuilding of Indigenous communities following the "permanent process of conquest that has destroyed, mutilated, fragmented, and exterminated us".

The CNI was created during forums called by the Zapatista Army of National Liberation (EZLN), in October 1996, following the San Andrés Accords between the EZLN and the Mexican government earlier that year. The agreements included ending marginalisation, recognition of Indigenous autonomy and self-determination, as well as Indigenous health, education and justice systems.

However, in 2001, following pressure by capitalists and corporate leaders, the accords were "betrayed" and wound back, says the CNI. Since then, the CNI says it practises such rights, whether the state recognises them or not.

Coming out of the conference, the CNI announced that it had adopted "important agreements to strengthen and renew the CNI, its assembly, and its work and coordination structures". It also demanded an end to the war on Palestine, that political prisoners be released, and justice for those activists that have been murdered.

The CNI stressed that original peoples, through their own assemblies and structures, are the only ones that can call and hold consultative processes, in light of the Mexican government's attempt to pass an Indigenous rights law, through "consultations" that it organises.

Thousands of CNI members and supporters also protested on October 12, shutting down three key highways around the country in rejection of the law, which they say is being "imposed" without regard for traditional authorities and general assemblies held by Indigenous communities. The proposed law comes within a history of Mexican governments imposing outside structures like mayors, municipalities and governors in order to "plunder" regions of their minerals and natural resources.

"It's important that our assemblies and the decisions we make be respected," said Tlaxco.

In Mexico, some 39 million people identify as Indigenous. They frequently experience racism, as well as institutional discrimination against their languages — especially in health and education systems. They are often at the forefront of defending their land from environmental destruction, and as a result disproportionately face human rights attacks, criminalisation, murder and forced displacement. Further, most crimes go unpunished, with systemic impunity favouring organised crime as well …

author: Peter Boyle
title: Why the RBA wants higher unemployment
content:
The latest official unemployment rate was released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics on September 24. It was 4.6% in August, seasonally adjusted, up from 4.2% a year ago. By its calculations, the number of unemployed people had grown by 12.4% in that period to 722,900. Another 6.3% were underemployed.

Two days earlier, Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Governor Michele Bullock took part in a “Fireside Chat at the Committee for Economic Development of Australia”, where she revealed that this was on the lower end of the RBA’s unemployment target of between 4.5% and 5%.

Higher unemployment, she said, will take the “heat out of the labor market” and “ease pressure on inflation”.

Every RBA governor swears blind that everything the RBA does is to “fight inflation”. If some people get hurt in the process, sorry, that is just a necessary sacrifice because inflation hurts everyone.

However, the RBA governor admitted that inflation “really hits the most vulnerable in the community the hardest”.

“They’re the ones that have the least ability and income to move ... They have less flexibility. They have less discretionary expenditure ... So inflation really, really hits the people on the lowest incomes the hardest.”

So is the RBA getting on the side of the poorest?

Bullock was just admitting the bloody obvious, when average real wages have been falling sharply since March 2021.

Greg Jericho, The Australia Institute’s chief economist, explained: “The rise of inflation above wage growth in 2022 and 2023 delivered the sharpest decline in the value of real wages since the Reserve Bank began its inflation targeting regime in the early 1990s.”

That has always been the RBA’s real intention — not to stop inflation, but to force the working class to shoulder the burden.

The RBA’s chief weapon against the working class is its ability to crank up interest rates. This forces more people out of jobs, to become part of a reserve army of labour that, in turn, pressures those still with jobs to accept falling real wages.

The official unemployment statistics hide the real pain. More than 1 million people (including children and other dependants) are currently forced to survive on unemployment payments that, according to the Antipoverty Centre, are 40% below the poverty line.

Its October 12 Anti-Poverty Week statement reported that 20% of suicide deaths are people on JobSeeker and 60% of working-age adults who die are on a Centrelink payment.

Jericho warned in his paper, The collapse of real wages and the path to recovery, that the RBA will push back against any attempt to take real wages back to 2021 levels because it is determined to limit both wage growth and wage growth expectations to avoid a “wage-price spiral”.

This argument implies that it is workers’ push for wage rises (to meet rising costs of living) that are the cause of inflation.

Prices have been rising faster than wages all around the world, first sparked by supply shortages during the COVID-19 crisis and then fed by the surge in oil prices following the illegal United States-Israeli attacks on Iran. They are now being supercharged by the AI arms race.

The RBA is doing nothing to address these drivers of inflation; instead, it is seeking to make those hardest hit carry the pain.

Iain Ross, a member of the Monetary Policy Board of the RBA, gave a detailed speech at the University of Melbourne, showing that a “wage-price spiral” is not a real threat, because the trade union movement had been dramatically weakened, including by laws restricting industrial action and workers’ solidarity.

“There is no evidence of the emergence of a wage-price spiral in the present circumstances, and recent data suggest such an outcome is unlikely,” he said.

Before the 1980s, stronger unions like the Australian Metal Workers Union would win wage rises and these gains would be spread to other industries, according to a principle of “comparative wage justice”.

“The situation today is very different,” Ross said. “Comparative wage justice no longer plays the pervasive role it once did, and quarterly indexation is not a feature of the current system. Importantly, the current system also limits how frequently wage claims can be revisited and how readily outcomes can spread across the economy.”

The major parties’ neoliberalism is responsible for this and the simultaneously terrible social and environmental costs. For decades, the billionaire class has had a free hand to obscenely enrich …

author: CMI Argentina
title: “Ley de Defensa de la Soberanía Nacional”: de nuevo el enemigo interno
content:
El Centro de Estudios Legales y Sociales (CELS) realizó un informe en el que señala la inconstitucionalidad del proyecto presentado por el Poder Ejecutivo, que incorpora el paradigma de la “seguridad nacional” y reorganiza bajo ese concepto la defensa, la seguridad interior y la inteligencia.


Compartimos el informe:


Ley de Defensa de la Soberanía Nacional. Observaciones del CELS sobre la inconstitucionalidad del proyecto presentado por el Poder Ejecutivo


El gobierno presentó en el Congreso el proyecto de Ley de Defensa de la Soberanía Nacional y sostuvo que sólo aborda amenazas externas, que no crea nuevas facultades para el Poder Ejecutivo y que no presenta problemas de constitucionalidad. Sin embargo, el proyecto incorpora el paradigma de la “seguridad nacional” y reorganiza bajo ese concepto la defensa, la seguridad interior y la inteligencia.


En esta publicación presentamos los argumentos técnicos que permiten analizar sus puntos más críticos: la concentración de atribuciones en el Poder Ejecutivo, la debilidad de los controles judiciales, el uso de definiciones vagas para investigar y sancionar y las afectaciones a garantías constitucionales.


Índice


I. La definición de las amenazas a la seguridad nacional es laxa con graves problemas de legalidad


II. El proyecto no refiere sólo a “amenazas externas”, habilita la definición de amenazas internas


III. Las atribuciones del Consejo de Seguridad Nacional también presentan problemas de legalidad


El Consejo de Seguridad Nacional no se limita a coordinar facultades preexistentes. Crea nuevas facultades que violan la división de poderes


Las “medidas urgentes” que contempla el proyecto eluden el control judicial y por lo tanto avanzan sobre facultades del Poder Judicial


El nivel de secreto con el que funcionaría el Consejo de Seguridad Nacional es incompatible con las garantías mínimas del debido proceso


Sanciones graves y de aplicación imprecisa que impactarían sobre el derecho de asociación


No hay recurso judicial efectivo si las sanciones quedan en pie


El RePET, un ejemplo de castigo administrativo arbitrario que pretende ampliarse


IV. Figuras penales abiertas e inconstitucionales


Problemas de legalidad y definición de tipos penales


Creación de nuevos delitos vinculados a “actividades terroristas”


Analisis Del CELS De La Ley De Soberania Nacional

author: Kodao Productions
title: Prosecution affirms Duterte’s innocence by its dropping of charges
content:
By

Atty. Ephraim B. Cortez

 / President,

National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers


The withdrawal of Articles 1 and 4 of the Articles of Impeachment is deemed an acquittal served on a silver platter.


The prosecution gave (impeached Vice President) Sara Duterte a favor when it withdrew Articles 1 (misuse of confidential funds), and 4 (grave threats) because withdrawal is tantamount to affirming her innocence on those charges. She was deemed innocent despite overwhelming evidence of guilt.


We must concede that the Prosecution may withdraw any of the Articles of Impeachment even after the respondent has filed an answer and evidence has been presented. The only condition is that the Impeachment Court must permit the withdrawal. The problem is that it affirmed her innocence.


Sara Duterte enjoys the constitutional presumption of innocence. For this reason, the prosecution must prove her guilt by clear and convincing evidence. The burden of proof remains with the prosecution throughout the proceedings, and Duterte has no obligation to present any evidence to the contrary.


However, once the prosecution presents a

prima facie

 case against her, the burden of evidence shifts to the respondent. The evaluation of the prosecution evidence to determine whether it proves a

prima facie

 case occurs after the presentation of evidence ends. Only when a

prima


facie

case is established is the respondent obliged to present evidence in her defense.


Notably, at the time of the withdrawal of Articles 1 and 4, the Prosecution had yet to complete the presentation of its evidence on these articles through a formal offer of its Exhibits. Although the prosecution was not able to complete and terminate the presentation of evidence in support of Articles 1 and 4 and to rest its case, it is beyond doubt that it made out a

prima facie

 case against Duterte on Articles 1 and 4.


At this point, while the presumption of innocence is not overturned and the burden of proof is not shifted, had the Prosecution completed its presentation of evidence by formally offering its documentary exhibits, the burden of evidence should have shifted to Duterte, given the overwhelming evidence against her, and she should have been compelled to present evidence in support of her defense.


As a consequence of the withdrawal, the Prosecution could not terminate its presentation of evidence with respect to Articles 1 and 4. As such, the prosecution could not overcome the presumption of innocence or meet its burden of proof. The burden of evidence never shifted to the respondent.


It follows, under the circumstances, that the respondent is deemed innocent, not because she is really innocent, but because of the withdrawal of Articles 1 and 4.


In essence, the Prosecution has given the Vice-President a favor by absolving her of accountability for Articles 1 and 4 despite overwhelming evidence that she misappropriated confidential funds amounting to hundreds of millions of pesos and made a mockery of accounting and audit procedures. #

Prosecution affirms Duterte’s innocence by its dropping of charges

author: Unknown
title: Iowa Hospital Workers Demand Return of Deported Co-Worker
content:
Fatou Traore was on her way to work as a custodian at the University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinics (UIHC) on the morning of Thursday, September 24, when ICE agents detained her.


Despite having legal immigration status in the United States and no criminal record, she was deported to Sierra Leone (a place she has no connection to) on October 12. Traore is a beloved member of the Iowa City community and of AFSCME Council 61, Local 12. She is also the mother of four children, the youngest of whom is three years old.


When I first heard the news of her September detention, I was upset that ICE had taken someone from the very hospital where I worked. Many of the workers at the hospital weren’t aware of her detention or were afraid to speak up. I wrote to all of the inpatient phlebotomists I used to work with at main campus, some of whom had also been custodians and worked with Fatou.


I wrote an opinion letter for a local paper,

Little Village

. I helped spread the word to raise awareness of her detention across community networks, from my supervisors and senior administration at UIHC, to the soccer team that my son plays on, to the yoga community I belong to, to my own family and their church communities, to the Iowa Writers’ Workshop, which I graduated from in 2022—to every person that I knew.


HOSPITAL SILENT


Next I thought a petition would be a good way to spark awareness and collective action. Months earlier a petition had circulated to change an unpopular parking policy the hospital wanted to put in place.


This time our petition called on the hospital—and the other community powers that be—to speak out against Traore’s detention. But the hospital didn’t budge, saying, “You can voice your opinion as a private citizen, but we can’t make any kind of statement about this.”


That’s precisely the problem; the people who have the most stake in protesting ICE’s actions and what happened to Fatou aren’t safe to do it—they aren’t safe as private citizens. That is why the hospital and so many organizations in Iowa need to be standing up and saying this is wrong. Fatou’s detention and deportation is an abomination. We need her back home.


Since her detention, her family and community, the worker center Escucha Mi Voz Iowa, the Iowa City Catholic Worker, and the Immigrant Welcome Network have been working tirelessly for her release, rallying the local and wider communities and calling on state representatives and religious leaders to denounce ICE’s actions.


During the legal proceedings put in motion on her behalf, Fatou was denied due process. The government deported her to a third country before a judge could rule on her stay motion, and her request for a credible fear interview was ignored.


“Due process means giving people a meaningful opportunity to be heard before the government takes an action with devastating consequences,” said Mazahir Salih of Immigrant Welcome Network.


WE’RE NOT DISPOSABLE


Fatou is a pillar of our community and our workplace. Her work at UIHC has touched countless lives, demonstrating her commitment to improving the health and well-being of others.


I’m a phlebotomist and she’s a custodian, so we’re kind of in a similar role where we’re coming in and out of patient rooms, mostly doing our work behind the scenes, and very underappreciated.


We’re thought of as disposable, and people have the impression that we don’t matter—if we’re not there to do our job, then they can fill it with anybody else—and it's just not true. The people who work these jobs are committed to being there. She had the resilience to keep showing up and doing that job for over a decade.


We call on the powers that be—the Department of Homeland Security, local representatives, and community leaders, and UIHC—to intervene to bring Fatou back now, and on Iowa’s congressional delegation to demand answers about why she was deported before a ruling on her stay motion and why her request for a credible fear interview was denied.


We need her here. As her co-workers, we have circulated a petition, attended rallies, written letters, spread the word of her story, called our representatives, and agonized every day of her absence. She belongs with us. Bring her back now.


Sara Gilmore is a phlebotomy technician at the University of Iowa Health Care Medical Center. She's an AFSCME Local 12 member.

author: Unknown
title: Диктатор с искусственным интеллектом: как технологии расширяют возможности диктаторов, и одновременно угрожают им
content:
Это эссе было написано Брюсом Шнайером и Севой Гуницким и первоначально опубликовано в журнале Foreign Affairs . Волонтеры «Автономного Действия» перевели его на русский. Мы думаем, что оно интересно с точки зрения дальнейшего развития путинского режима и технологий искусственного интеллекта.

Через две недели после полномасштабного вторжения Москвы в Украину в марте 2022 года редактор Первого канала России Марина Овсянникова ворвалась в студию вечерних новостей. Она держала над головой ведущего самодельный плакат с надписью: «Остановите войну. Не верьте пропаганде. Здесь вам врут!» Она кричала: «Нет войне!», пока её не оттащили.

С тех пор никто не протестовал против войны на российском телевидении, отчасти из-за усиления мер безопасности и общей атмосферы страха. Но в октябре 2024 года Маргарита Симоньян, одна из главных российских пропагандисток, предложила другое объяснение. По ее словам, все большее число ведущих российских телеканалов — не настоящие. «Этого лица не существует. Мы сами сгенерировали голос и все остальное». Она имела в виду, что они были созданы искусственным интеллектом. В последующем интервью газете «Ведомости» она изложила логику: «Этим ведущим не нужна зарплата или страховка, — сказала она. — Их не арестуют, и полиция не будет обыскивать их дома. Это все одновременно прекрасно и ужасно».

Это то, что ИИ обещает каждому авторитарному правителю: способность поддерживать контроль, не делегируя задачи ненадежным человеческим существам. Это чрезвычайно привлекательная перспектива. Какими бы могущественными ни были диктаторы, им всегда нужны были подчиненные — цензоры, пропагандисты , охранники, полицейские, аналитики разведки и местные чиновники — для выполнения их приказов. Но подчиненные всегда представляют потенциальную угрозу. Они могут уклоняться от ответственности, воровать, лгать, сливать информацию или вступать в заговор против своего босса. В результате одна из старейших дилемм, стоящих перед автократами, заключается в том, как наделить агентов полномочиями для выполнения приказов, не позволяя им при этом выступать против своего лидера. Автократы обычно находили компромисс, заполняя ключевые должности посредственностями, чья тупость, как выразилась политический теоретик Ханна Арендт, является «лучшей гарантией их лояльности». Но это неизбежно затрудняет управление диктатурами и выживание в условиях кризисов.

Искусственный интеллект, по-видимому, предлагает автократам два способа решения этой давней дилеммы. Во-первых, это означает, что теперь они могут легко отслеживать и дрессировать своих подчиненных в режиме реального времени. Изменение в привычках траты денег или расписании встреч местного чиновника может быть автоматически отмечено системой ИИ без необходимости использования информаторов, которые могут преследовать собственные интересы. Во-вторых, ИИ может полностью устранить подчиненных. Автоматизируя задачи, которые ранее требовали человеческих решений, правители могут заменить ненадежных посредников лояльными алгоритмами, которые невозможно подкупить или манипулировать ими. Об этом уже говорят сами чиновники в авторитарных режимах. ИИ «определенно может заменить половину чиновников», — заявил министр цифрового развития России Максут Шадаев на Московском форуме по данным в апреле 2025 года, добавив: «возможно, немного больше».

Однако эти мечты о государстве, которое работает само по себе, иллюзорны. ИИ никогда не бывает по-настоящему автономным. Системы должны создаваться и поддерживаться группой инженеров и специалистов по обработке данных, чью экспертизу политические лидеры не могут оценить. Правитель, который обращается к ИИ, чтобы уменьшить зависимость от ненадежных людей, может в итоге еще более слепо полагаться на немногих специалистов по ИИ, которые поддерживают работу этой системы. И эта новая цифровая преторианская гвардия может обладать теми же слабостями, что и старая, что делает ее угрозой для правителя.

Китай лидирует в разработке систем искусственного интеллекта, способных контролировать или заменять подчиненных. Программы «умных городов» в Пекине, Шанхае и других крупных городах используют ИИ для отслеживания эффективности работы и централизации надзора за местными чиновниками, которые ранее работали в комфортной тени, подвергая их алгоритмической оценке производительности. Китай также разработал «систему ИИ с нулевым доверием», которую за последнее десятилетие внедрил примерно в 30 уездах и городах. Эта система сопоставляла более 150 правительственных баз данных …

author: Unknown
title: Ephéméride des luttes : 14 octobre
content:
L'éphéméride des luttes du 14 octobre réserve un bien triste sort à notre Parti Socialiste préféré. Ses locaux sont en effet pulvérisés dans la région toulousaine, tandis que des manifestations antifascistes prennent les rues de Rome ou du Canada. Et pas seulement.


1876 :

 Naissance de l'anarchiste illégaliste Jules Bonnot.


1883 :

 A Pittsburg aux Etats-Unis, ouverture d'un Congrès de l'AIT, qui marque le départ de l'anarchisme "organisé" aux USA.


1906 :

 Naissance de Hannah Arendt, qui a brillament démontré la banalité du mal dans plusieurs de ses ouvrages en développant à quel point les pires atrocités organisées du monde ne pourraient exister sans les gens qui disent "je ne fais que mon travail", même s'il s'agit d'un simple travail de bureau.


1908 :

 A Cuba, parution du premier numéro du journal anarchiste "Rebelion !".


1918 :

 Dans la prison de New York, mort de l'anarchiste juif Jacob Schwartz. Celui-ci avait été mis en prison pour distribution de tracts séditieux. Ses camarades arrêtés au même moment que lui sont condamnés à des peines oscillant entre 15 et 20 ans de prison.


1920 :

 En Italie, des manifestations de soutien à la Révolution Russe se déroulent et demandent la libération des prisonniers politiques. A Bologne en particulier, la police ouvre le feu lors d'un meeting de l'anarchiste Errico Malatesta, faisant plusieurs morts.


1943 :

 Dans le camp de concentration de Sobibor en Pologne, une rébellion des prisonniers a lieu : 11 gardiens SS sont tués et 200 personnes parviennent à s'échapper. Après avoir attiré les officiers dans des endroits discrets pour les exécuter, et que des détenus connaissant l'infrastructure electrique aient pu couper l'electricité et le téléphone du camp, les détenus se sont rassemblés dans l'après-midi pour profiter de la confusion pour simplement « sortir en marchant », ce qui ne réussit pas. les pistolets volés plus tôt dans la journée, ni ceux volés dans l'armurerie ne faisaient le poid face à l'artillerie des gardes. Quelques incendies sont allumés dans l'espoir de détruire les bâtiments par le feu. Des 650 détenus le jour de la révolte, 365 environ essayerent de s'échaper et celleux qui restèrent furent executé dans les jours qui suivirent. Des évadé.e.s, 185 ont été tué par balle ou mines, et dans les 10 jours, 107 de plus furent recapturés et executés. De la centaine de personnes restantes, 23 furent tué par des non-allemands avant la fin de la guerre et plusieurs autres moururent de maladies. Entre 40 et 60 participant.e.s de cette insurrection ont survécu à la guerre. Avec les quatre autres personnes s'étant échapées avant, illes sont les seul.e.s survivant.e.s de Sobibor. Quelques jours plus tard, les SS ont démoli les bâtiments, nettoyé le site et planté le terrain de pins


1970 :

 Aux USA, la brigade des femmes du Weather Underground (Proud Eagle Tribe) fait sauter le centre des affaires internationales de Harvard.


1976 :

 Au Canada, c'est la grève générale.


1977 :

 - A Paris, place Vendôme, attentat des NAPAP (Noyaux Armés Pour l'Autonomie Populaire) contre le ministère de la Justice et contre le Palais de Justice sur l'île de la Cité.


 A Rome, deux cortèges antifascistes défilent : 50.000 personnes participent à celui appelé par la Commune, 30.000 à celui du mouvement autonome. Une bombe explose devant le local de la Démocratie Chrétienne (le parti au pouvoir depuis l'après-guerre) et une autre devant le tribunal régional administratif. Une patrouille de police est attaquée au molotov, ainsi qu'une succursale de FIAT, tandis qu'un bar et un cinéma sont saccagés et cambriolés.


1979 :

 A Washington, des dizaines de milliers de personnes participent à la première manifestation pour les droits des personnes homosexuelles aux USA.


1980 :

 A Turin, c'est la marche des 40.000. Cette manifestation marque un tournant dans l'histoire des luttes de la ville, puisqu'il s'agit de 40.000 petits propriétaires, bourgeois et patrons qui manifestent pour le retour à l'ordre après une période d'ébullition sociale dans la ville après que près de 25.000 ouvriers aient perdu leur travail. Cette manifestation a très largement été utilisée contre les mouvements sociaux et ouvriers.


1982 :

 - Le siège de la fédération du Parti Socialiste de Haute-Garonne est pulvérisé par une charge de 15 kilos de dynamite pour protester contre la répression des luttes ouvrières et antinucléaires.

title: İHD’den Osman Kavala kararına tepki: Kavala kararı hukuk devletinin sınavıdır
content:
İnsan Hakları Derneği (İHD) Genel Merkezi, İstanbul 13. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesinin Osman Kavala hakkında verilen AİHM Büyük Dairesi kararına rağmen yeniden yargılama talebini reddetmesine ilişkin açıklama yaptı.

“Kavala kararı hukuk devletinin sınavıdır” denilen açıklamada, İstanbul 13. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesinin, Avrupa İnsan Hakları Mahkemesi Büyük Dairesinin Osman Kavala hakkındaki ihlal kararına rağmen yeniden yargılama talebini reddetmesinin kabul edilemez bir hukuk ihlali olduğu vurgulanan açıklamada, “Bu karar, yalnızca Osman Kavala’nın özgürlüğünü gasp etmeyi sürdürmüyor; Türkiye’nin taraf olduğu uluslararası sözleşmeleri ve hukuk düzenini de açıkça hiçe sayıyor” vurgusu yapıldı.

Açıklamada, “AİHM Büyük Dairesi; özgürlük ve güvenlik, adil yargılanma, ifade ve örgütlenme özgürlükleri ile hakların amaç dışı kısıtlanması yasağının ihlal edildiğini tespit etti. Türkiye’ye Kavala’nın en kısa sürede serbest bırakılması ve mahkumiyetin sonuçlarının ortadan kaldırılması yükümlülüğünü hatırlattı. Avrupa İnsan Hakları Sözleşmesi’nin 46. maddesi bu kararları bağlayıcı kılar. Anayasa’nın 90. maddesi temel haklara ilişkin uluslararası sözleşmeleri kanunların üzerinde tutar; 138. maddesi ise mahkeme kararlarının bağlayıcılığını düzenler. CMK’nin 311. maddesi de AİHM’in ihlal kararını yargılamanın yenilenmesi nedeni sayar. Buna rağmen ret kararı verilmesi, hukuki bir değerlendirme sınırını aşarak bağlayıcı kararın etkisiz bırakılması sonucunu doğurmuştur” ifadelerine yer verildi.

Açıklamanın devamında şu ifadelere yer verildi:

“TBMM’deki Milli Dayanışma, Kardeşlik ve Demokrasi Komisyonunun geniş siyasi mutabakatla kabul ettiği raporda AİHM ve Anayasa Mahkemesi kararlarına eksiksiz uyum çağrısı yapılmıştır. Bu çağrının siyasi metinlerde kalmasına izin verilemez. Barış ve demokratikleşmeden söz edenler, önce yargı kararlarına uyulmasını ve temel hakların güvence altına alınmasını sağlamalıdır. İnsan Hakları Derneği olarak bu kararı kınıyoruz. Osman Kavala derhal serbest bırakılmalı, AİHM kararının tüm gerekleri yerine getirilmeli ve hukuka aykırı mahkumiyetin sonuçları ortadan kaldırılmalıdır. Bağlayıcı kararları uygulamayan bir yargı düzeni, adaleti değil keyfiliği büyütür. Hukuk, iktidarın ve mahkemelerin tercihine bırakılamaz.”

author: Unknown
title: İstifası isteniyordu: ABD'nin Atina Büyükelçisi Guilfoyle, görevinin sona erdiğini duyurdu
content:
Fotoğraf: Gage Skidmore from Peoria, AZ, United States of America/Wikimedia Commons CC BY-SA 2.0

ABD'nin Atina Büyükelçisi Kimberly Guilfoyle, görevinin sona erdiğini açıkladı. Guilfoyle, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı paylaşımda, ABD'nin Atina büyükelçiliği görevini kendisine verdikleri için ABD Başkanı Donald Trump ve ABD Dışişleri Bakanı Marco Rubio'ya teşekkür etti.

Büyükelçi olarak görevinin ilk gününden itibaren ABD'nin Yunanistan ile ilişkilerini güçlendirmek amacıyla çalıştığını ifade eden Guilfoyle, özellikle enerji alanında atılan işbirliği adımlarına dikkat çekti.

Guilfoyle, son dönemde hakkında basında yer alan bir Trump bağışçısınan kişisel kredi kartı borcunu ödemek için 100 bin dolar istediği, bir Yunan yetkiliyi tehdit ettiği, uygunsuz hediyeler kabul ettiği gibi iddiaların asılsız olduğunu belirterek, "profesyonel hayatını adaleti sağlamaya, doğrunun yanında durmaya ve ABD’yi özel kılan değerleri korumaya adadığını" ifade etti. Guilfoyle, Trump'ın sadık bir destekçisi olmaya devam edeceğini ifade etti.

Guilfoyle, mesajında, "Büyükelçilik görevim sona eriyor olsa da Başkan Trump ve 'Önce Amerika Hareketine' ve sevdiğim bu ülkeye bağlılığım asla sona ermeyecek" ifadelerini kullandı.

Beyaz Saray Sözcüsü Katie Zacharia, dün yaptığı açıklamada, "hediye kabul etme ve yönetim yetkililerine erişim sağlama karşılığında para talep etme" iddialarıyla gündeme gelen ABD'nin Atina Büyükelçisi Kimberly Guilfoyle'un istifasının istendiğini bildirmişti. ABD'li Sözcü, "Büyükelçi Guilfoyle'dan istifa etmesini istedik. Kendisi, ekip için harika bir insandı ve kendisine bol şanslar diliyoruz" demişti.

ABD Başkanı Trump da dünkü açıklamasında, Guilfoyle'un görevden alınabileceğini ifade etmişti.

author: Daron Letts
title: Nominations for KIA elections to open Oct. 26
content:
Nominations for five seats on the Kivalliq Inuit Association board of directors will open on Oct. 26.


The election is scheduled for Dec. 14, c

hief returning officer Penny Taylor announced Tuesday, in the association’s notice of election.


The roles include vice-president and secretary/treasurer, as well as the community director positions in Naujaat, Rankin Inlet and Whale Cove.


“This year’s election is more than a procedural milestone — it is an opportunity for Inuit across the Kivalliq region to help shape the future of their communities and strengthen Inuit-led governance,” Taylor said in an email on Tuesday. “

The voices of Inuit voters and nominees are essential to that work.”


The nomination period closes at 3 p.m. on Nov. 9.


Advance polls will be held on Dec. 7, Taylor said.


Mobile polls will also visit schools, elders’ centres, health centres, mine sites, boarding homes, healing facilities, and Winnipeg’s Uquutaq Medical Boarding Home. Schedules for each community will be posted by Nov. 30.


Eligible voters must be an Inuk enrolled under the Nunavut Agreement aged 16 years or older as of Dec. 14, 2026, and regularly reside in the Kivalliq region.


KIA is the designated Inuit organization under the Nunavut Final Agreement and one of three regional Inuit organizations associated with Nunavut Tunngavik Inc.

author: Unknown
title: Tupac cinayeti davasında Duane “Keffe D” Davis'e 40 yıl hapis
content:
ABD'de eski çete lideri Duane “Keffe D” Davis, rapçi Tupac Shakur’un 1996’da Las Vegas’ta öldürülmesini azmettirdiği gerekçesiyle 40 yıl hapis cezasına çarptırıldı. Eylülde jüri tarafından suçlu bulunan 63 yaşındaki Davis, kararı temyiz edeceğini söyledi.

Savcılar, Davis’in silahı ateşlememiş olsa da saldırıyı yönettiğini ve cinayette kullanılan silahı sağladığını savundu. İddia makamına göre ateş eden kişi, Davis’in yeğeni Orlando Anderson’dı. Cinayete karıştığını reddeden Anderson, 1998’de başka bir silahlı saldırıda öldü. Davanın temel delillerini Davis’in kendi anlatımları oluşturdu. Davis, saldırının düzenlendiği beyaz Cadillac’ın içinde bulunduğunu kamuoyu önünde defalarca kabul etmiş, 2019’da yayımlanan anılarında da silahı sağladığını anlatmıştı. Savunma ise bu açıklamaların kitap satmak ve para kazanmak amacıyla üretilmiş kurgu ve abartılar olduğunu ileri sürdü.

Davis, 2008’de rapçi Notorious B.I.G.’nin ölümüyle ilgili gizli bir polis görüşmesinde, kovuşturmadan korunmasını sağlayan anlaşma kapsamında Shakur cinayetindeki rolünü anlatmıştı. Daha sonra kitap ve röportajlarda yaptığı açıklamalar bu korumayı geçersiz kıldı; mahkeme polis görüşmesinin davada delil olarak kullanılmasına izin verdi.

Salı günkü ceza duruşmasında Shakur’un kardeşleri Sekyiwa ve Maurice, mümkün olan en ağır cezanın verilmesini istedi. Sekyiwa Shakur, ağabeyinin ölümünün ailelerini uzun süre derinden sarstığını söyledi.

7 Eylül 1996’da vurulan ve hip-hop tarihinin en önemli figürleri arasında gösterilen Shakur, hayatını kaybettiğinde 25 yaşındaydı. Davis’in mahkumiyeti, yaklaşık 30 yıl boyunca çözülemeyen cinayet dosyasındaki ilk mahkumiyet oldu.

author: Sicilia Libertaria
title: Attacco alle Idee!
content:
Reprimere il dissenso.


Il governo Meloni, dopo la batosta subita col Referendum sulla giustizia e le imponenti manifestazioni Pro-Pal, corre oggi ai ripari tentando di fare terra bruciata intorno ai movimenti di opposizione sociale che, finalmente usciti allo scoperto, ne hanno frenato le mire totalitarie e rivelato le collusioni genocidiarie, e minacciano in sovrappiù di farle perdere le prossime elezioni.


Contro questa vera opposizione che scende in piazza dimostrando di non temere i “decreti sicurezza” con i quali il governo avrebbe voluto silenziarla, rispolvera ora i metodi più duri ereditati dall’indimenticato Ventennio fascista, che non colpiscono più solo l’attivismo ma direttamente le idee di chi si oppone al governo. Non bastando più fogli di via, zone rosse, fermi preventivi, sanzioni onerose, “scudi penali”, minacce poliziesche e pressioni d’ogni tipo, si è deciso ad attaccare anche la libertà di espressione e di pensiero.


Due casi eclatanti

 sono venuti alla ribalta in questi giorni. Il primo riguarda tre esponenti del  movimento No Muos, tra cui un membro della Federazione Anarchica Siciliana, sottoposti a processo il 7 ottobre per istigazione all’occupazione della base MUOS di Niscemi. Il presunto reato sarebbe avvenuto a conclusione della manifestazione del 2 Agosto 2025, durante un serrato dibattito sulle future iniziative che il movimento avrebbe potuto intraprendere, tra chi era favorevole a ridiscutere la possibilità di una nuova occupazione della base (i compagni incriminati) e chi avanzava dubbi o ne contestava la proposta. Poliziotti aguzzini e magistrati, zelanti esecutori di ordini venuti dall’alto, scambiando surrettiziamente l’invito alla discussione per un invito all’azione, hanno pensato bene di ripescare un residuato del codice penale fascista, l’istigazione, reato a sé stante (perché non presuppone necessaria una successiva azione criminosa), infamante (perché prevede forme di prevaricazione della volontà altrui, subite specialmente da soggetti psichicamente labili e altamente influenzabili), che oltre a ledere la reputazione dei compagni accusati – impegnati da sempre nel creare autoconsapevolezza nelle persone – coinvolge l’intero movimento di cui fanno parte, le cui decisioni si fondano al contrario su pratiche assembleari e di condivisione politica.


È a tutti noto

 che a partire dagli anni ’80 del Novecento sono stati aboliti o fortemente ridimensionati reati similari all’istigazione, quali il plagio o l’apologia specialmente a mezzo stampa; che oggi, a costituire una vera emergenza sociale non sono gli attivisti contro le guerre e la militarizzazione dei territori, ma gli “influencer” e i “persuasori digitali” che governo e partiti politici incoraggiano e usano per i loro scopi elettorali; che appellarsi a un evanescente reato di istigazione, introdotto dal fascismo per tacitare definitivamente gli oppositori politici, se non strumentale e fazione appare quanto meno anacronistico.


Il secondo caso

 riguarda una ventina tra medici e psichiatri posti sotto inchiesta dalla procura di Ravenna con la speciosa accusa di aver redatto certificati falsi per impedire il trattenimento nei CPR (Centri di Permanenza per il Rimpatrio) di alcuni migranti irregolari. La procura ravennate entra nel merito della valutazione delle malattie e delle sofferenze patite in luoghi, come le carceri giudiziarie e i CPR, che molti dei medici indagati, aderenti in parte alla rete “Mai più lager – No ai CPR”, avevano definito come invivibili e disumani. L’accusa tende platealmente a denigrare l’azione di denuncia e di protesta portata avanti da questi medici, la cui vera colpa sarebbe quella “d’istigare alla cura”, come specificano le “Collettive Brigate Basaglia”, altra rete medica militante. Sono nuovamente le libertà di pensiero e di associazione a trovarsi sotto tiro.


Gli inquirenti vorrebbero asservire la medicina alle pulsioni repressive dello Stato, le cui strutture detentive provocano notoriamente gravi compromissioni della salute, danni mentali, autolesionismo e tentativi di suicidio in coloro che vi vengono trattenuti; e costringere a firmare falsi certificati di compatibilità carceraria anche quei medici che si rifiutano di tacere sulle inadempienze delle autorità e sottostare alle pretese del governo.


In entrambi i casi

, la presunta istigazione dei No Muos e l’ “istigazione alla cura” dei medici indagati, emergono in questi mesi palesi tentativi d’intimidire il dissenso, di creare …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump’s Mass Deportation Push May Cut Retirees’ Social Security By $2k Annually
content:
The program’s insolvency date was already pushed up to 2032, partly as a result of mass deportations.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The average retiree will soon see average cuts of over $2,000 to their annual Social Security benefits if the Trump administration’s mass deportation campaign is continued, according to a new report on the widespread economic consequences of the president’s inhumane agenda.

By 2034, retirees’ benefits may be cut by 8.6 percent, or an average of $2,152 per year, as a result of the loss of tax revenue caused by the deportation campaign. This would be a massive cut for retirees, who on average receive $25,000 a year from Social Security, which is the U.S.’s top anti-poverty program. The projected insolvency date for the program was already pushed up a year, to 2032, by the program’s trustees earlier this year, due in part to President Donald Trump’s anti-immigrant policies.

These findings were included in a report by Economic Insights and Research Consulting released by immigrant advocacy group America’s Voice and first reported by The Guardian.

This cut would compound existing poverty concerns for the elderly amid impacts on industries that rely heavily on immigrant labor. Costs for goods like groceries and housing — and services like elderly care — are rising as a result of the mass deportation policies, according to the report; immigrant labor makes up roughly 48 percent of agricultural occupations and 32 percent of construction jobs, the report finds.

The Trump administration has repeatedly claimed that their deportation agenda serves U.S.-born workers by deporting foreign-born workers and freeing up their job posts. In reality, on top of the massive harms to immigrant workers — including the deportations of tens of thousands of children — the deportation campaign is set to wreak havoc on the U.S. economy, which could lead to hundreds of thousands of job cuts for U.S.-born workers as well.

The report references a study on the effects of the deportation policies between January and September of 2025, which found that 668,000 jobs were lost in that time, with between 51,000 and 297,000 jobs lost by U.S.-born workers.

Meanwhile, even as Congress neglects to pass legislation to stave off Social Security insolvency, they have helped to balloon ICE’s budget, which is now larger than that of every other federal law enforcement agency combined. Previous research has found that federal officials have spent or have committed $269 billion to the mass deportation agenda through 2029, costing roughly $2,358 per taxpayer.

Social Security solvency issues seem to be of little concern to the Trump administration. Last week, Trump expressed a desire to privatize the program, saying that he “wanted to do it so badly” during his first term. Experts have warned against such an idea, saying that similar attempts in the past to privatize Social Security-like programs in other countries have led to major cuts to benefits.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Rep. Delia Ramirez Introduces Landmark Bill to Abolish DHS, ICE, and CBP
content:
The Department of Homeland Security was established in 2002 as part of the Bush administration’s war on terror.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Rep. Delia C. Ramirez (D-Illinois) has introduced a bill that would abolish not just ICE, but the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) altogether, repealing the 2002 law establishing the agency and replacing it with one focused on protecting civil and human rights.

The wide-ranging legislation, dubbed the Reimagining Safety Act, would repeal the Homeland Security Act. Signed by President George W. Bush as part of his administration’s post-9/11 “war on terror,” the transformational bill created DHS and led to the establishment of Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

The bill would abolish DHS, CBP, and ICE — going further than the progressive call to abolish ICE. Other offices currently housed within the department, like Transportation Security Administration (TSA), the Coast Guard, Citizenship and Immigration Services, and the customs functions of CBP would be broken off into different authorities.

“We know that DHS was intentionally established with an overbroad mission and unchecked power. The last two years have made it visible what so many communities have actually been saying for decades: That DHS, frankly, is the single greatest threat to our public safety today,” Ramirez said in a press conference previewing the legislation last month. “We must strip away every single tool they are using to terrorize us.”

In DHS’s place, Ramirez’s bill would create a cabinet-level “Department of Community Safety,” which would address community concerns ranging from gun violence to disaster relief, using a public health-based approach. All immigration detention centers would be shuttered.

The legislation comes as DHS has ballooned into one of the largest agencies in the U.S. government in just 24 years of existence, with its authorities having been expanded by every subsequent presidential administration since its establishment.

Now, it has become central in executing President Donald Trump’s agenda, carrying out his administration’s fascist campaign of mass deportation, surveillance, and suppression of communities across the U.S.

The legislation is cosponsored by Representatives Adelita Grijalva (D-Arizona), Jim McGovern (D-Massachusetts), and Rashida Tlaib (D-Michigan), as well as over 40 advocacy and progressive groups.

“From its inception, those in power have wielded DHS as a weapon. Widespread illegal and abusive detention of immigrants, violent racial profiling, and state overreach — including domestic surveillance, civil rights violations via the USA PATRIOT Act,” Ramirez said.

“The bottom line is this: From its establishment, DHS has always been empowered to violate our rights, under the pretense of securing our safety,” Ramirez said. “Enough is enough.”

The administration has targeted hundreds of thousands of immigrants with arrests, detention, and deportations, often openly defying court orders and even constitutional safeguards to wreak havoc and invoke fear. At least eight people have been killed on the streets by DHS agents since the beginning of Trump’s second term, at least 57 have died in immigration detention, and thousands have been “disappeared” within the shadowy detention network or to places abroad. Meanwhile, journalists, activists, elected officials, and more, have repeatedly been caught in DHS’s ever-expanding dragnet.

Ramirez’s new bill also seeks to defang numerous other post-9/11-era policies and actions.
