title: Ameliyatı başarılı geçen Papa 14. Leo'ya akciğer kanseri tanısı kondu
content:
Vatikan Devlet Başkanı Papa 14. Leo'nun, akciğerinde tespit edilen kitle nedeniyle dünkü ameliyatının başarılı geçtiği ve öncesindeki testlerde şüphelenildiği gibi akciğer kanseri tanısının doğrulandığı bildirildi.

Vatikan'dan yapılan yazılı açıklamada, Papa'nın planlandığı üzere dün ameliyata alındığı belirtilerek, "Sağ akciğerin alt lobu, video destekli radikal cerrahi uygulanarak çıkarıldı. Ameliyat öncesi testlerde şüphelenildiği gibi, yapılan histolojik inceleme akciğer adenokarsinomu tanısını doğruladı" ifadeleri kullanıldı.

Papa'nın ameliyathanede yaklaşık 3 saat kaldığı, ameliyatın ise yaklaşık 90 dakika sürdüğü ve başarılı geçtiği aktarıldı.

Ameliyattan sonra Papa'nın normal bir şekilde uyandığı ve kısa bir gözlem süresinin ardından 10. kattaki odasına döndüğü kaydedildi.

Papa 14. Leo, dün öğle saatlerinde Gemelli Hastanesi'ne yatmıştı.

Vatikan'dan dün akşam saatlerinde yapılan ilk açıklamada da Papa'nın ameliyatının başarılı geçtiği vurgulanmıştı.

Vatikan, ameliyattan önce de Papa'nın iyileşmesi için 20 Ekim'e kadar bütün programlarının iptal edildiğini duyurmuştu. Tarihte ilk kez bir Papa, pazar duasında ameliyat olacağını açıkladı

Papa 14. Leo, 11 Ekim'de Vatikan'ın Aziz Petrus Meydanı'na bakan ofisinin penceresinden yaptığı geleneksel pazar duası sırasında, "Doktorlar, akciğerimde bir kitle (nodül) tespit etti. Doktorlar müdahalenin uygun olduğuna inanıyor ve bu nedenle onların tavsiyesi üzerine, nodülü aldırmak için ameliyat olmaya karar verdim. Ameliyat, önümüzdeki birkaç gün içinde yapılmak üzere planlandı. Manevi yakınlığınız için teşekkür ediyor ve kendimi dualarınıza emanet ediyorum" ifadesini kullanmıştı.

71 yaşındaki Papa'nın "sürpriz" olarak değerlendirilen bu açıklamasının ardından Vatikan Basın Ofisi de operasyon sonrasında iyileşme döneminin bir hafta sürmesinin beklendiğini duyurmuştu.

İtalyan basını da tarihte ilk kez bir Papa'nın, pazar duasında gelecek günlerde ameliyat olacağını şeffaflıkla açıkladığına dikkati çekti. Basındaki haberlerde, Papa'nın 6-17 Kasım'da Uruguay, Arjantin ve Peru'yu kapsayan Güney Amerika gezisini iptal etmemek için hemen ameliyat olma kararı aldığı belirtildi.

Vatikan'ın önceki devlet başkanı Papa Franciscus'un 21 Nisan 2025'te vefatının ardından Katolik Kilisesi'nin merkezi Vatikan'da 8 Mayıs 2025'teki Konklav'da (Papalık Seçimi) Papa olarak seçilen dönemin kardinali ABD'li Robert Francis Prevost, kendisine "Papa 14. Leo" ismini almıştı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Ecological destruction in the Zilan Valley continues
content:
Construction work on an irrigation canal in the Zilan Valley (Geliyê Zîlan), near the district of Erciş in Van province, is causing increasing damage to the region’s ecosystem. Since September 23, heavy construction machinery has been operating in the canyon as part of the so-called Pay Irrigation Canal Project. Excavation and construction work in the streambed and surrounding areas have altered the natural flow of water. Water levels have dropped significantly, and some sections of the stream have already dried up.


These developments threaten not only to have serious consequences for local wildlife and vegetation but also to exacerbate water supply problems in the region. Environmental activists have initiated legal proceedings against the project and requested a suspension of construction work. A court decision is still pending, while machinery continues operating in the valley.


Trees felled and riverside vegetation destroyed


The areas along the streambanks have been particularly severely affected. Trees have been felled and large sections of natural vegetation cleared within the valley. The grasses, shrubs, and trees growing in the area perform essential functions in maintaining the ecological balance: they stabilize the soil, prevent erosion, regulate water levels, and provide habitats for numerous animal species.


With the destruction of this vegetation, the streambanks are losing their natural protection. At the same time, wildlife habitats used for shelter, feeding, and reproduction are being destroyed. These interventions threaten the interconnected relationship between water, soil, and vegetation, which is crucial to the valley’s ecological stability.


The alterations to the streambed also have far-reaching consequences. Together with its banks, the stream forms a continuous habitat for fish, aquatic invertebrates, amphibians, birds, and other wildlife. Falling water levels and drying sections of the stream can destroy these habitats, reduce moisture in the surrounding soil, and make it more difficult for animals to access water.


Legal action against construction work


Environmental activists have filed an application with the Administrative Court in Van seeking a suspension of the project’s implementation. They have also filed a criminal complaint with the public prosecutor’s office in Erciş. No decision has yet been issued on the urgent application. Construction work continues despite the ongoing legal proceedings.


The controversial irrigation canal project dates back to 1993, when the Turkish State Hydraulic Works (DSI) initiated the project and issued a positive environmental impact assessment decision. After the project remained unimplemented for many years, it was put out to tender in 2016 and awarded to the company Günsay.


Zilan Valley threatened by large-scale projects for years


The irrigation project is not the only intervention threatening the natural environment of the Zilan Valley. For years, the region has been increasingly affected by state-backed energy and infrastructure projects. Particularly controversial is the development of geothermal resources, which has been pursued since 2020 and now threatens the livelihoods of several villages.


In Şorik, Karakilise, and Çaxirbeg, drilling and development activities are encroaching on agricultural land and residential areas. Residents now even fear that their villages may be evacuated. Environmental groups have also warned about the potential discharge of thermal waters contaminated with heavy metals into the region’s irrigation systems and waterways. However, publicly documented measurements are not yet available to allow a definitive assessment of the contamination levels.


The scale of the planned development is reflected in tenders issued in 2024, which offered licenses for the exploration and exploitation of geothermal resources covering approximately 8,860 hectares in total. The ongoing construction work on the Pay Irrigation Canal represents yet another intervention in an ecosystem already under pressure from energy projects.

author: Chris Walker
title: Report: Trump Is Having Second Thoughts About Livestreaming Military Execution
content:
Trump isn’t “particularly enthusiastic” about Pete Hegseth’s plan to livestream a military execution in December.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

President Donald Trump is reportedly asking advisors if he should go through with Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth’s plan to livestream a military execution later this year.

Trump has publicly indicated that he’ll make a final decision on the matter soon.

“There are two thoughts: don’t show it and show it,” Trump said. “Because, you know, by showing it, maybe other people won’t be doing what he did.”

“I’ll make a decision ultimately. I know what the military would like to do, but I’ll make a decision,” Trump added.

But according to reporting from Axios, Trump is questioning whether the execution of former Army Maj. Nidal Hasan should be televised, asking his advisers for their views on the matter.

Hasan was convicted of killing 13 soldiers at Fort Hood in Texas in 2009. He was shot during the rampage, and is now a paraplegic, paralyzed from the waist down. Hasan is set to be executed by a firing squad in December.

The president “didn’t sound particularly enthusiastic” about a live, national showing of the execution, a source close to Trump said to the publication, adding that “he’s calling around, doing the Trump thing, asking people what they think.”

The livestream event “might not happen,” another source confirmed.

Trump’s public statements about the death penalty reveal that he has errant views about capital punishment. Multiple studies have shown that there is no evidence supporting the idea that the death penalty can act as a deterrent, or that the threat of capital punishment somehow lessens violent crime. Indeed, several years of data demonstrate that the homicide rates in states with capital punishment are higher than in states without the death penalty.

Trump is also wrong about what “the military would like to do.” While there isn’t widespread data to demonstrate most servicemembers’ views one way or another, some officers have spoken out against the planned livestreaming of Hasan’s execution.

“It takes away everything America stands for when we do public executions,” one Army officer said in an anonymous comment to CNN. “The generational harm caused by allowing troops in uniform to stand in front of a man in a wheelchair and watch him get shot to death is irreparable.”

Several religious leaders, including Pope Leo, and a bipartisan cadre of lawmakers, have also spoken out against livestreaming the execution.

Despite Trump’s reticence about this specific event, he has been an outspoken proponent of expanding the death penalty, including for non-lethal crimes such as drug dealing. In his first week in office, he signed an executive order peddling the the false claim that the death penalty is “an essential tool for deterring” crimes, calling for the attorney general to seek the death penalty for crimes involving the killing of law enforcement officers, or when the defendant being charged is an undocumented immigrant.

In an op-ed published last week, Truthout’s board of directors president Maya Schenwar decried the death penalty in all of its forms, describing the botched execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee as an act of torture and Hegseth’s decision to livestream Hasan’s execution as part of a larger “pro-death penalty fervor.”

“The brutality is the point. The torture is the point. The murder, not only state-sanctioned but state-celebrated, is the very point,” Schenwar wrote.

A cohesive life-affirming agenda rejects not only executions, but also the inherent violence of incarceration, policing, deportation, imperial wars, and military aid to genocidal forces. It makes no excuses — let alone expansions — that prop up or prolong the existence of these institutions in ‘kinder, gentler’ forms.

“Let’s not allow ourselves to give in to the inertia of our brutal present, in which death by hanging is a mercy. Let’s envision the cohesive, life-affirming agenda that embraces a future for all of us, a world in which the torture of Christa Pike — or anyone — is unthinkable,” Schenwar concluded.

author: Deborah Nyokabi
title: UN review of Kenya highlights urgent need to reform family laws that discriminate against women
content:
13th October 2026


UN review of Kenya highlights urgent need to reform family laws that discriminate against women


By Deborah Nyokabi


20 min read


News and Insights


Family law


Africa


Nairobi, Kenya, October 13, 2026:

For 42 years, Kenya has committed to ensuring women’s equality in marriage and family life.

In 1984, the country ratified the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW), and Article 2(6) of the


Constitution

 makes the treaty part of Kenyan law.

Yet in reality, this promise remains unrealised. Women in Kenya can still lose their homes when their husbands die, struggle to claim property they helped build, and face barriers to leaving marriages marked by violence.


Kenya’s record on women’s rights is currently under scrutiny as the CEDAW Committee reviews the country’s implementation of the Convention during the

Committee’s 93rd session

 at the United Nations in Geneva.


The


Global Campaign for Equality in Family Law

,

Equality Now

 and Kenyan partners, including

Come Together Widows and Orphans Organization (CTWOO),

 have submitted a

shadow report

 providing a civil society account of what happens on the ground in Kenya in relation to Article 16 of the CEDAW Convention.


What CEDAW Article 16 means for women in Kenya


Article 16 of CEDAW

 protects equality inside the family. This includes equal rights when spouses marry, during marriage and when it ends, with equal say over parenting, property and decisions about children. It protects the right to belong in a family, to be safe in it and to prosper in it, from marriage through widowhood. The Committee’s


guidance on violence against women

 extends that protection to safety at home.


That commitment is tested at every stage of family life. When a couple registers a marriage, when unpaid care counts towards family wealth, when a woman seeks a divorce, when a widow tries to keep her home and when a woman needs protection from violence. These are not separate failures but different ways in which equality can exist on paper and be denied in practice.


Kenya has made real progress. Article 27 of the Constitution guarantees equality, and


Article 45(3)

 applies that guarantee to spouses at every stage of marriage. The


Marriage Act of 2014

 brought many marriage laws into one statute, and the


Matrimonial Property Act of 2013

 recognised non-financial contribution to family wealth, reforms that the Federation of Women Lawyers in Kenya and other women’s organisations helped

advance

 through strategic litigation, legislative proposals and community education.


Marriage registration and women’s property rights in Kenya


Equality in family life starts with being able to prove a marriage exists. The Marriage Act requires registration, yet it costs


Kenya shillings 3,900

, and both spouses must appear before the registrar. Only


19.3 per cent of married women aged 15 to 49

 had registered their marriage in the 2022 Kenya Demographic and Health Survey, while the shadow report finds no fee waiver for poor households and no county registration drives to help

make it easier for couples to register their marriages locally

.


For a family living on the World Bank’s


international poverty line of US$3 a day

, the fee equals ten days of income. Many families pass land down the husband’s line, so a wife who cannot prove her marriage can struggle to claim the family home and land after a divorce or a death, and courts have been


inconsistent about the consequences of non-registration

. Free registration for poor households and mobile registration teams in every county would remove the barrier.


Kenya recognises unpaid contribution in property division, but no formula says how to value it, and in 2023 the Supreme Court


held

 that Article 45(3) does not give spouses an automatic half share.

Women must still establish their contribution to matrimonial property over the years, including non-monetary contributions such as childcare and housework.

 A presumption of equal sharing, supported by judicial guidelines on valuing unpaid work, would help turn the constitutional promise of equal rights into equal outcomes.


Divorce, access to justice and women’s safety


The question is not only whether Kenya has laws protecting women’s rights, but whether women can use them.

 Fees, distance from courts and lengthy proceedings stand between many women and justice, and Kenya’s divorce law …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump Admin Is Reportedly Offering Children as Young as 5 $3,000 to Self-Deport
content:
The offers are meant to “coerce” the children into giving up on their immigration cases, an immigrant advocate said.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

ICE is offering children as young as 5 years old $3,000 “incentives” to voluntarily depart the country, legal advocates have reported, as the Trump administration works to separate immigrant families under the hammer of their mass deportation machine.

Bloomberg Law first reported on the offers, citing attorneys and immigrant advocacy groups who say that the offers are sometimes given to children who lack legal representation. The offers, they say, are a method of forcing children to take a deal so that they drop their legal challenges before they have gone through their time in the court system.

Shaina Aber, executive director for the Acacia Center for Justice, told Bloomberg Law that the tactic is “part of a larger pattern of really trying to coerce children, bully children, intensify pressure on children so that they abandon their cases.”

“It’s part of this deport-at-all-costs policy that seems to be in particular targeting children,” Aber went on.

The offer is being made by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) attorneys as well as immigration judges. In some cases, judges are telling children that it is a one-time offer and giving them no time to consider it, forcing them to make a decision “on the spot” even though “they might not understand what the longer term consequences are down the line,” Aber said.

Another group, the Amica Center for Immigrant Rights, said that it and similar groups have received the emails from ICE’s Office of the Principal Legal Advisor offering a “$3,000 incentive” for children. Michael Lukens, head of Amica, told Bloomberg Law that the latest offer came to his office this week for an 11-year-old.

The reporting shows that the Trump administration’s policies toward child deportations are even more extreme than previously thought. Last year, NBC reported that the Trump administration was offering children aged 14 and older $2,500 to self-deport or voluntarily leave the country, according to a Department of Health and Human Services memo.

Indeed, reports have since found that the Trump administration is carrying out this policy even in cases where the children were living with their families, in cases likened to President Donald Trump’s family separation policies from his first term.

The Department of Homeland Security didn’t confirm or deny the payments, saying that the administration is supposedly working to reunite children who come to the U.S. unaccompanied with their families.

According to a tracker maintained by the Marshall Project, as of August, the federal government has deported over 22,500 children since January 1, 2025. ICE arrests of children have only continued to escalate throughout Trump’s second term, with over 8,500 children having been arrested thus far — including 562 children and babies under 4.

author: Stephen Prager
title: Air Force Major Who Called for Trump’s Impeachment Held in Solitary Confinement
content:
Some legal experts say Jason Watson’s confinement for 24 hours a day could amount to illegal pretrial punishment.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Air Force Maj. Jason Watson was arrested July 1 on the steps of the US Capitol after calling for the impeachment of President Donald Trump. According to his lawyer, he’s now being held in solitary confinement 24 hours a day in what some legal experts say could amount to illegal pretrial punishment.

The Uniform Code of Military Justice (UCMJ) contains provisions barring officers from engaging in public political activities that are typically protected for civilians, including criticizing the president and other elected officials.

Prosecutors have charged Watson with violating them when he participated in a news conference calling for Trump to be removed from office over his launching of military actions against Iran, Cuba, and Venezuela without congressional authorization.

After the speech, Watson stood on the Capitol steps holding a sign that read “Impeach, Convict, Remove” and was arrested after he refused to move.

Before he was charged, Watson gave a CNN interview on August 17 in which he continued to criticize Trump, accusing him of “flagrantly violating the Constitution” and “breaking the law.”

He acknowledged that he could face severe consequences as a result of his speech: “We just have to be willing to accept that we can change what is happening in our country if we are just willing to pay a price for it,” he said.

One day later, he was arrested while on duty and taken into pretrial confinement. He now faces a general court-martial, the military’s most severe trial, which is capable of imposing lengthy prison sentences.

“Cruel and unusual form of punishment.” U.S. Air Force Maj. Jason Watson is headed to the most severe form of military trial — a general court-martial — after calling for President Trump’s impeachment while in uniform at the U.S. Capitol. His attorney reveals that Maj. Watson… pic.twitter.com/7izEA47Gh2

On Friday, Watson’s lawyer, Christopher Mutimer, told CNN that after nearly two months, Watson is “still in solitary confinement 24 hours a day,” which he said amounted to “cruel and unusual” punishment.

“Even if he gets an hour to eat or to exercise, he is alone,” Mutimer said. “He is literally by himself, with his thoughts, in a room where the light never turns off all day.”

In an essay published Sunday by writer Monte Mader, Watson himself acknowledged spending his days in isolation, revealing that his Bible had only recently been returned to him and that he had little access to news.

Watson described the conditions of his confinement as the reality one must accept when choosing to engage in nonviolent resistance.

“Walking this path,” he said, “means exposing oneself to violence while refusing to retaliate against it.”

Major Jason Watson is NOT a Democrat. His protest was NOT about party politics. It was about what he believes his oath requires of him—and the price he’s willing to pay for speaking out. Everyone has seen the arrest. Now hear the courageous powerful speech that came first: pic.twitter.com/MMRoiYPV7K

After his July 1 protest, Watson had been restricted to Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling in Washington. Though the base reportedly has a confinement facility, following his detention, he was instead moved to a county jail in Maryland.

During Watson’s September 18 preliminary hearing, Maj. Joshua Wendell, the hearing officer, said Watson could not be confined with civilians and was therefore kept in solitary confinement.

“He was placed in confinement because of the law, which puts him in solitary confinement,” Wendell said, according to Stars and Stripes.

Article 13 of the UCMJ “forbids punishing a service member before trial and forbids pretrial restraint more rigorous than the circumstances require.”

Mutimer has pointed out that solitary confinement is “usually reserved for individuals who are disobeying or are violent, and injuring other people,” and usually only for “a day or two, or a week.” Watson, he said, has “been in there for months now.”

Rachel VanLandingham, a former Air Force judge advocate and professor of law at Southwestern Law School, told Common Dreams that this “seems to be a blatant case of illegal pretrial punishment given that the nature of his pretrial restraint does not seem necessary to either ensure his presence at trial or to …
